english: The young woman then came to the king like this: whatever she desired was given her to go with her out of the women’s house to the king’s house.
translation: Ilyo umukashana aleya ku mfumu ukufuma mu ŋanda ya banakashi ba mfumu, bali nokumupeela fyonse ifyo alefwaya ukusenda pakuya kwisano lya mfumu.

english: In the evening she went, and on the next day she returned into the second women’s house, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s eunuch, who kept the concubines. She came in to the king no more, unless the king delighted in her, and she was called by name.
translation: Afwile ukwingila icungulo elyo akacelo afuma aya mu ŋanda iyabubili iyo balesungilamo abanakashi ba mfumu. Uwalesunga iyi ŋanda ni Sha Ashigasi, mutungwi uwaleangalila abakashi ba mfumu abashaupilwe mu bwinga. Umukashana teti abwelele ku mfumu nakabili kanofye imfumu nga yamutemwa lyena kuti yamwita mwishina.

english: Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, came to go in to the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king’s eunuch, the keeper of the women, advised. Esther obtained favor in the sight of all those who looked at her.
translation: Elyo cafikile Esta umwana umwanakashi wakwa Abihaili nalume wakwa Modekai, uwalemusunga ngo mwana wakwefye, ukuya ku mfumu. Esta talombele nangu cimo kanofye ifyo Hegai mutungwi wa mfumu, uwaleangalila banamayo amwebele. Kanshi Esta aletemwikwa kuli bonse abalemumona.

english: So Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus into his royal house in the tenth month, which is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
translation: Kanshi ilyo batwele Esta ku mfumu Asuelusi mwisano lyakwe mu mweshi walenga ikumi limo, umweshi wa Tebeti mu mwaka walenga cine lubali uwa bufumu bwakwe,

english: The king loved Esther more than all the women, and she obtained favor and kindness in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal crown on her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.
translation: imfumu yatemenwe Esta ukucila bonse abanakashi bambi. Amona ukusekelelwa no luse ku mfumu ukucila banacisungu bambi bonse. Kanshi yamufwika icisote cabunamfumu ku mutwe, yamucita namfumu pa malo yakwa Fashiti.

english: Then the king made a great feast for all his princes and his servants, even Esther’s feast; and he proclaimed a holiday in the provinces, and gave gifts according to the king’s bounty.
translation: Elyo imfumu yacitile bacilolo na babomfi bakwe imitebeto iyikalamba. Kwena yali mitebeto yakwa Esta. Apeela ku fitungu fya calo cakwe ubushiku bwakutuusha no kupeela ifyabupe ukulingana nefyo imfumu ingapeela.

english: When the virgins were gathered together the second time, Mordecai was sitting in the king’s gate.
translation: Kanshi ilyo balonganike abakashana kabili umuku wabubili, Modekai ena aikele pa mpongolo ya mfumu.

english: Then the king’s servants who served him said, “Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king.
translation: Elyo ababomfi ba mfumu abaleitumika basosa abati, “Fwaileni imfumu abakashana banacisungu abasuma.

english: Esther had not yet made known her relatives nor her people, as Mordecai had commanded her; for Esther obeyed Mordecai, like she did when she was brought up by him.
translation: Esta tasokolwele ulupwa lwakwe nangu abantu bakwe ukulingana nefyo bamukonkomeshe kuli Modekai. Esta abeela Modekai ngefyo alemubeela ilyo alemusunga.

english: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting in the king’s gate, two of the king’s eunuchs, Bigthan and Teresh, who were doorkeepers, were angry, and sought to lay hands on the King Ahasuerus.
translation: Mu nshiku shilya lilya Modekai aleikala pa mpongolo ya mfumu, Bigitani na Tereshi bamutungwi babili ba mfumu abalonda pa mpongolo bafulilwa imfumu, bafwaya nokwipaya imfumu Asuelusi.

english: This thing became known to Mordecai, who informed Esther the queen; and Esther informed the king in Mordecai’s name.
translation: Kanshi Modekai aumfwa uyu mulandu. Kabili aeba namfumu Esta. Esta nao aeba imfumu mwishina lyakwa Modekai.

english: When this matter was investigated, and it was found to be so, they were both hanged on a gallows; and it was written in the book of the chronicles in the king’s presence.
translation: Elyo bafwailisha pali uyu mulandu, basanga nokuti cishinka. Aba baume bonse babili babakulika ku fimuti. Nefi fyonse fyalilembelwe mu citabo camilandu pa cinso ca mfumu.

english: Let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the beautiful young virgins to the citadel of Susa, to the women’s house, to the custody of Hegai the king’s eunuch, keeper of the women. Let cosmetics be given them;
translation: Imfumu isale bacilolo mu fitungu fyonse ifya calo cakwe abakulonganika abakashana banacisungu no kubaleta ku ŋanda ya banakashi ba mfumu iyaba mu musumba wa Susa. Aba bakashana bakalasungwa na Hegai mutungwi umubomfi wa kwisano uwaleyangalila abanakashi ba mfumu. Babapeele na mafuta na tumbi utwakuti bamoneka bwino.

english: and let the maiden who pleases the king be queen instead of Vashti.” The thing pleased the king, and he did so.
translation: Pali aba bakashana, uukasekesha imfumu eukapyana namfumu Fashiti.” Ici casansamwishe imfumu, no kucita efyo yacitile.

english: There was a certain Jew in the citadel of Susa whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite,
translation: Kanshi mu musumba wa Susa mwali Umuyuda umo ishina lyakwe ni Modekai umwana wakwa Yairi, umwana wakwa Shimei, umwana wakwa Kishi, umwina Benjamini,

english: who had been carried away from Jerusalem with the captives who had been carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away.
translation: uwali pa basha basendele ukufuma ku Yerusalemu pamo na Yekoniya imfumu ya ku Yuda uo Nebukadinesa imfumu ya ku Babiloni asendele.

english: He brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter; for she had neither father nor mother. The maiden was fair and beautiful; and when her father and mother were dead, Mordecai took her for his own daughter.
translation: Modekai alesunga Hadasa , umufyala wakwe, pantu takwete wishi na nyina. Umukashana uwaishibikwa ne shina Esta, alikwete icata icisuma nganshi kabili uwaemba, ne cinso cakwe icisuma. Ilyo wishi na nyina bafwile, Modekai amubuula alamusunga ngo mwana wakwe.

english: So, when the king’s commandment and his decree was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together to the citadel of Susa, to the custody of Hegai, Esther was taken into the king’s house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women.
translation: Kanshi ilyo babilishe imbila ne cebo ca mfumu, abakashana abengi babalonganika mu musumba wa Susa, balasungwa na Hegai. Esta nao balimusendele kwisano lya mfumu no kumubika mu minwe yakwa Hegai, uwaleangalila abaleikala ku ŋanda ya banakashi ba mfumu.

english: The maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindness from him. He quickly gave her cosmetics and her portions of food, and the seven choice maidens who were to be given her out of the king’s house. He moved her and her maidens to the best place in the women’s house.
translation: Esta awamina Hegai, nao amutemwa. Ecalengele ukuti mukwangufyanya amupeela ifyakumuyemfya ne fyakulya ali nokupoka. Kabili amupeela na bakashana abatumishi cine lubali abo asalile ukufuma mwisano lya mfumu, atwala Esta na bakashana bakwe ku muputule uusuma mu ŋanda ya banakashi ba mfumu,

english: After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes who were with him.
translation: Panuma ya ifi fintu imfumu Asuelusi asumbula Hamani umwina Agagi, umwana wakwa Hamedata, amupeela umulimo wakwangalila bamushika banankwe bonse.

english: The king took his ring from his hand, and gave it to Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy.
translation: Elyo imfumu yafuule imbalaminwe yakufwatikilako no kupeela Hamani umwina Agagi umwana wakwa Hamedata, umulwani wa Bayuda.

english: The king said to Haman, “The silver is given to you, the people also, to do with them as it seems good to you.”
translation: Kabili imfumu yaeba Hamani aiti. “Indalama shalipeelwa kuli iwe pamo pene na bantu bene, kanshi ucitile umo ulefwaila.”

english: Then the king’s scribes were called in on the first month, on the thirteenth day of the month; and all that Haman commanded was written to the king’s local governors, and to the governors who were over every province, and to the princes of every people, to every province according to its writing, and to every people in their language. It was written in the name of King Ahasuerus, and it was sealed with the king’s ring.
translation: Kanshi imfumu yaita bakalemba baiko pa bushiku bwalenga ikumi limo na shitatu (13) mu mweshi wakubalilapo ukuti balembe icebo ukulingana na fyonse ifyo Hamani alandile. Ici cebo calembelwe ku nkonkani sha mfumu shonse na balashi aba cila citungu mu calo, na ku bakalamba ba bantu bonse. Balembele ukulingana ne filembo fya cila citungu no lulimi lwa cila mutundu. Ici cebo calembelwe mwishina lya mfumu Asuelusi, pafwatikwe ne nshimbi ya mbalaminwe yakwe.

english: Letters were sent by couriers into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to plunder their possessions.
translation: Batumine bakapaso ku fitungu fyonse ifya calo ca mfumu no kubapeela amakalata apali icebo icakonaula, ukwipaya no kulofya Abayuda bonse, abalumendo na bakalamba, banamayo na bana, ukwabula ukushapo nangu umo, no kupoka ifyuma fyabo. Ici cali nokucitika pa bushiku bwalenga ikumi limo na shitatu (13) ubwa mweshi walenga ikumi limo na ibili (12), umweshi batila Ada.

english: A copy of the letter, that the decree should be given out in every province, was published to all the peoples, that they should be ready against that day.
translation: Icikope ca uyu kalata cali nokubilikishiwa mu fitungu fya calo fyonse nge cebo pakuti abantu bonse bakaipekanye pali ubu bushiku.

english: The couriers went out in haste by the king’s commandment, and the decree was given out in the citadel of Susa. The king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city of Susa was perplexed.
translation: Bakapaso bwangu bwangu bakonka icipope ca mfumu, neci cebo caishibikwa mu musumba wa Susa. Elyo imfumu na Hamani bena baikele panshi balanwa no kunwa, lelo mu musumba wa Susa mwaba icimfulunganya.

english: All the king’s servants who were in the king’s gate bowed down and paid homage to Haman, for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai didn’t bow down or pay him homage.
translation: Kanshi bonse ababomfi ba mfumu abali pa mpongolo bali nokupeela Hamani umucinshi pakumwinamina, pantu e cebo imfumu yapeele. Nomba Modekai ena alikene ukulamwinamina nangu ukumupeela uyu mucinshi.

english: Then the king’s servants who were in the king’s gate said to Mordecai, “Why do you disobey the king’s commandment?”
translation: Elyo ababomfi ba mfumu abali pa mpongolo baeba Modekai ati. “Bushe cinshi ushikonkele icebo ca mfumu?”

english: Now it came to pass, when they spoke daily to him, and he didn’t listen to them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s reason would stand; for he had told them that he was a Jew.
translation: Efyo balamweba cila bushiku nomba ena taleumfwa, alebasuka ukuti Muyuda. Basuka baeba Hamani pakuti bamone ukuti amashiwi yakwa Modekai nga yacishinka.

english: When Haman saw that Mordecai didn’t bow down nor pay him homage, Haman was full of wrath.
translation: Ilyo Hamani amona ukuti Modekai talemwinamina nangu ukumupeela umucinshi, alifulilwe nganshi.

english: But he scorned the thought of laying hands on Mordecai alone, for they had made known to him Mordecai’s people. Therefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews who were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even Mordecai’s people.
translation: Nomba talefwaya ukwipaya Modekai eka iyoo. Panuma yakumweba abantu bakwa Modekai, Hamani apanga ukwipaya Abayuda bonsefye mu calo conse cakwa Asuelusi.

english: In the first month, which is the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, and chose the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.
translation: Mu mweshi wakubalilapo uwitwa Nisani, mu mwaka walenga ikumi limo na ibili (12) uwa bufumu bwakwa Asuelusi, bependula ukubomfya Puri pa cinso cakwa Hamani pakufwailisha ukwishiba ubushiku no mweshi. Kanshi cawila pa mweshi walenga ikumi limo na ibili, umweshi batila Ada.

english: Haman said to King Ahasuerus, “There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom, and their laws are different from other people’s. They don’t keep the king’s laws. Therefore it is not for the king’s profit to allow them to remain.
translation: Elyo Hamani aeba imfumu Asuelusi ati. “Kuliko abantu bamo abaipatulula abasalanganina mu bantu bobe aba mu fitungu fyonse fya bufumu bobe. Balipusana ku bantu bambi ku ntambi shabo, kabili tabakonka amafunde ya mfumu. Kanshi tacilingile ukuti imfumu isumine ukwikala na bantu ba musango uyu.

english: If it pleases the king, let it be written that they be destroyed; and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who are in charge of the king’s business, to bring it into the king’s treasuries.”
translation: Ngakuti casansamusha imfumu, kaipange icebo icakulofya aba bantu, na ine nkapeela indalama amatalanta amakana ikumi limo (10,000) aya silifa mu minwe ya bantu abasunga icipao ca mfumu pakuti bakayabike mu cipao ca mfumu.”

english: Now when Mordecai found out all that was done, Mordecai tore his clothes and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the middle of the city, and wailed loudly and bitterly.
translation: Ilyo Modekai aumfwile ifyacitike fyonse, alepula insalu shakwe, afwala insalu shabulanda, aisuba ne mito. Elyo aingila mukati ka musumba no kulila umusowa ukalamba uwacililishi.

english: Then Esther spoke to Hathach, and gave him a message to Mordecai:
translation: Panuma yakulanda, Esta amweba ukubwelela kuli Modekai no kumweba ukuti,

english: “All the king’s servants and the people of the king’s provinces know that whoever, whether man or woman, comes to the king into the inner court without being called, there is one law for him, that he be put to death, except those to whom the king might hold out the golden scepter, that he may live. I have not been called to come in to the king these thirty days.”
translation: “Ababomfi ba mfumu bonse na bantu bakwe mu fitungu fya calo cakwe fyonse balishiba ukuti umwaume nelyo umwanakashi uwaingila mu lubansa lwamukati kukumona imfumu ukwabula ukuti imwite, pabafye ifunde limo kumwipaya. Kanofye imfumu yatambika inkonto ya golide kuli ena, lyena kuti apusuka. Na ine wine nomba papita inshiku amakumi yatatu (30) apo imfumu yanjitile ukuya uko ili.”

english: They told Esther’s words to Mordecai.
translation: Elyo baebele Modekai ifyo Esta asosele.

english: Then Mordecai asked them to return this answer to Esther: “Don’t think to yourself that you will escape in the king’s house any more than all the Jews.
translation: Pakwasuka Esta, Modekai atile ati. “Witontonkanya ukuti ifi uli mwisano ukapusuka ku cikaponena Abayuda bambi.

english: For if you remain silent now, then relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
translation: Pantu iwe nga waikalafye tondolo pali ino nshita, ukupusuka no kulubuka kwa Bayuda kulefuma ku ncende imbi, lelo iwe no lupwa lwa bawiso mukaloba. Kuti twaishiba shani limbi eco wabelele namfumu pakuti wafwilishe pa nshita iyaba ngeyi?”

english: Then Esther asked them to answer Mordecai,
translation: Mukwasuka Modekai, Esta amweba ati,

english: “Go, gather together all the Jews who are present in Susa, and fast for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day. I and my maidens will also fast the same way. Then I will go in to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish.”
translation: “Kabiye ulonganike Abayuda bonse abekala mu Susa no kubeba ukuti bakamfungileko pa nshiku shitatu akasuba no bushiku ukwabula ukulya no kunwa amenshi. Na ine wine na babomfi bandi banamayo tukafunga nga imwe. Panuma yakufunga elyo nkaya ku mfumu, nangu line nkatoba icebo. Nga kufwa, kankafwe!”

english: So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.
translation: Elyo Modekai aya cita fyonse ifyo Esta amwebele.

english: He came even before the king’s gate, for no one is allowed inside the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth.
translation: Aya fika na ku mpongolo ya mfumu. Nomba takwali umuntu nangu umo uwasuminishiwe ukwingila pa mpongolo ya mfumu nafwala insalu shabulanda.

english: In every province, wherever the king’s commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
translation: Kanshi mu citungu conse ica calo umwafikile icipope ne cebo ca mfumu, mwali imisowa ikalamba nganshi mu Bayuda, ukufunga ukulya, ukulila no kuloosha. Elyo Abayuda abengi bafwele insalu shabulanda no kuisuba imito.

english: Esther’s maidens and her eunuchs came and told her this, and the queen was exceedingly grieved. She sent clothing to Mordecai, to replace his sackcloth, but he didn’t receive it.
translation: Elyo ababomfi bakwa Esta abanakashi na bamutungwi wakwe bamushimikile ifyalecitika, awe namfumu aikatwa no bulanda ubukalamba. Atumina Modekai ifyakufwala pakuti afuule insalu shabulanda, nomba ena alikene.

english: Then Esther called for Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs, whom he had appointed to attend her, and commanded him to go to Mordecai, to find out what this was, and why it was.
translation: Elyo Esta aita Hataki, umo pali bamutungwi ba mfumu uo basalile ukumutumika, amweba ukuya kuli Modekai pakwisa mweba ifyalecitika ne calengele ukuti filecitika.

english: So Hathach went out to Mordecai, to the city square which was before the king’s gate.
translation: Hataki aya kuli Modekai mu lubansa lwa musumba pantanshi ya mpongolo ya mfumu.

english: Mordecai told him of all that had happened to him, and the exact sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the king’s treasuries for the destruction of the Jews.
translation: Elyo Modekai amweba fyonse ifyamucitikile, amweba ne cipendo ca ndalama umo cabelele ico Hamani alaile ukulipila ku cipao ca mfumu pakuti onaule Abayuda.

english: He also gave him the copy of the writing of the decree that was given out in Susa to destroy them, to show it to Esther, and to declare it to her, and to urge her to go in to the king to make supplication to him, and to make request before him for her people.
translation: Modekai kabili amupeela ne cikope ca cebo, icalembelwe no kusalangana mu Susa icakulofya Abayuda, pakuti aye langa Esta no kumulondolwela, no kumweba ukuti aye ku mfumu mukufwailisha ubwafwilisho, apapatileko abantu bakwe ku mfumu.

english: Hathach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.
translation: Elyo Hataki aya kuli Esta no kumweba ifyo Modekai amwebele.

english: Now on the third day, Esther put on her royal clothing and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, next to the king’s house. The king sat on his royal throne in the royal house, next to the entrance of the house.
translation: Pa bushiku bwalenga shitatu Esta afwala insalu shakwe ishabunamfumu, aya iminina mu lubansa lwamukati ke sano lya mfumu pantanshi ya muputule wa mfumu. Imfumu nayo ninshi naikala pa cipuna cabufumu mukati ke sano ukulungatana ne mpongolo ye sano.

english: Nevertheless Haman restrained himself, and went home. There, he sent and called for his friends and Zeresh his wife.
translation: Lelo kwena ashipikisha aya na ku ŋanda kumwakwe. Elyo atuma abakwita abanankwe no mukashi wakwe Sereshi.

english: Haman recounted to them the glory of his riches, the multitude of his children, all the things in which the king had promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the princes and servants of the king.
translation: Elyo Hamani atampa ukubashimikila ubwingi bwa fyuma fyakwe, ne mpendwa ya bana bakwe abaume, na pafyo imfumu yamucindike pakumupeela ififulo ifikalamba, no kumusonta ukuba umukalamba wa bacilolo na babomfi ba mfumu.

english: Haman also said, “Yes, Esther the queen let no man come in with the king to the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and tomorrow I am also invited by her together with the king.
translation: Alundapo nokuti, “Eico cine na namfumu Esta wine taitileko umuntu nangu umo ku mitebeto apekenye kanofye ine pamo ne mfumu. Na mailo line nkayako kabili pamo ne mfumu.

english: Yet all this avails me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.”
translation: Lelo ifi fyonse tafilepilibula akantu nangu kamo kuli ine nga cakuti ndemona Modekai Umuyuda naikala pa mpongolo ya mfumu.”

english: Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends said to him, “Let a gallows be made fifty cubits high, and in the morning speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on it. Then go in merrily with the king to the banquet.” This pleased Haman, so he had the gallows made.
translation: Elyo umukashi wakwe Sereshi na banankwe bamweba abati, “Fwayeni abakupanga ifimuti fyakukulikilapo abantu icilepele amakubiti amakumi yasano (50) . Elyo ulucelo ukebe imfumu ikakulikilepo Modekai. Elyo ukaye pamo ne mfumu ku mitebeto ninshi nausansamuka.” Kanshi Hamani atemwa pali aya mano bamupandileko, apanga ne fimuti fyakukulikilapo abantu ba milandu.

english: When the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she obtained favor in his sight; and the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. So Esther came near and touched the top of the scepter.
translation: Ilyo imfumu yamwene Esta naiminina mu lubansa, yatemwa pakumumona. Imfumu epakutambika inkonto ya golide iyali mu minwe yaiko kuli ena. Elyo Esta apalamina aikata pa mulu wa nkonto.

english: Then the king asked her, “What would you like, queen Esther? What is your request? It shall be given you even to the half of the kingdom.”
translation: Imfumu yamwipusha aiti, “Ninshi namfumu Esta? Cinshi ulefwaya? Ndekupeela conse ico ulefwaya nangufye ukukwakanya ubufumu bwandi pakati!”

english: Esther said, “If it seems good to the king, let the king and Haman come today to the banquet that I have prepared for him.”
translation: Elyo Esta asosa ati, “Nga cakuti casansamusha imfumu, lekeni imfumu na Hamani bese ilelo ku mitebeto iyo napekanishisha imfumu.”

english: Then the king said, “Bring Haman quickly, so that it may be done as Esther has said.” So the king and Haman came to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
translation: Imfumu nayo epakusosa aiti, “Iteni Hamani bwangu bwangu pakuti tucite ifyo Esta alefwaya.” Kanshi imfumu na Hamani baisa na ku mitebeto Esta apekenye.

english: The king said to Esther at the banquet of wine, “What is your petition? It shall be granted you. What is your request? Even to the half of the kingdom it shall be performed.”
translation: Ilyo bacili balenwa umwangashi panuma ya matebeto, imfumu yaipusha Esta aiti, “Bushe cinshi ulefwaya. Ala ulepeelwa. Cinshi ulelomba? Nangufye ukufika kukwakanya ubufumu bwandi pakati cilefikilishiwa!”

english: Then Esther answered and said, “My petition and my request is this.
translation: Elyo Esta ayasuka ati. “Ifyo ndefwaya nefyo ndelomba nifi.

english: If I have found favor in the sight of the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and to perform my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I will prepare for them, and I will do tomorrow as the king has said.”
translation: Nga ninsanga uluse pa cinso ca mfumu elyo nga cakuti casansamusha imfumu ukumpeela ico ndelomba no kufikilisha ico mfwaya, baleke ukuti imfumu na Hamani bakese nakabili mailo ku mitebeto nkabapekanishisha, lyena nkacita ifyo imfumu isosele.”

english: Then Haman went out that day joyful and glad of heart, but when Haman saw Mordecai in the king’s gate, that he didn’t stand up nor move for him, he was filled with wrath against Mordecai.
translation: Ilyo Hamani afumine ku malila, alisaminwe ne nsansa ishingi mu mutima. Lelo ilyo amwene Modekai mu mpongolo ya mfumu, nokuti taimine nangu ukumutiina, ici ecalengele ukuti Hamani afulwe nganshi.

english: On that night, the king couldn’t sleep. He commanded the book of records of the chronicles to be brought, and they were read to the king.
translation: Muli ubo bushiku imfumu Asuelusi alifililwe ukusendama utulo. Kanshi epakweba abakumuletela icitabo camilandu, umo balemba ifikankala ifyacitika mu bufumu bwakwe, pakuti babelengele imfumu.

english: Then the king said to Haman, “Hurry and take the clothing and the horse, as you have said, and do this for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king’s gate. Let nothing fail of all that you have spoken.”
translation: Elyo imfumu yaeba Hamani aiti. “Endesha, buula ifyakufwala na kabalwe, ngefyo usosele, efyo ucitile Modekai Umuyuda ulya ekala pa mpongolo ya mfumu. Wishapo ne cimo pafyo ulandile.”

english: Then Haman took the clothing and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and had him ride through the city square, and proclaimed before him, “Thus it shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!”
translation: Hamani epakuya buula ifyakufwala na kabalwe, afwika Modekai, amuteka na pali kabalwe, amutandasha na mu lubansa lwa musumba no kubilikisha kuli bonse pa cinso cakwe ati, “Moneni ifi efyo imfumu icitila umuntu uo ilefwaya ukucindamika.”

english: Mordecai came back to the king’s gate, but Haman hurried to his house, mourning and having his head covered.
translation: Elyo Modekai abwelela ku mpongolo ya mfumu lelo Hamani bwangu bwangu aya ku ŋanda kumwakwe, aleloosha kabili nafimba na ku mutwe.

english: Haman recounted to Zeresh his wife and all his friends everything that had happened to him. Then his wise men and Zeresh his wife said to him, “If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of Jewish descent, you will not prevail against him, but you will surely fall before him.”
translation: Elyo Hamani ashimikila umukashi wakwe Sereshi na banankwe bonse fyonsefye ifyamucitikile. Bampandamano wakwe na bakashi bakwe epakumweba abati. “Nga ni Modekai ulya ufwaya ukuwisha, elyo nga Muyuda, ninshi tawakamucimfye. Icine cine ukawa pa cinso cakwe.”

english: While they were yet talking with him, the king’s eunuchs came, and hurried to bring Haman to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
translation: Bacili balelanda nankwe, bamutungwi ba mfumu bafika mukwangufyanya batwala Hamani ku mitebeto iyo Esta apekenye.

english: It was found written that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs, who were doorkeepers, who had tried to lay hands on the King Ahasuerus.
translation: Awe basanga apo balembele ifyo Modekai asokolwele batungwi ba mfumu babili, Bigitani na Tereshi abalelonda pa mwinshi, abalefwaya ukwipaya imfumu Asuelusi.

english: The king said, “What honor and dignity has been given to Mordecai for this?” Then the king’s servants who attended him said, “Nothing has been done for him.”
translation: Elyo imfumu yaipusha aiti, “Uyu wine Modekai, bupulami nshi kabili bucindami nshi apokelapo pali ici?”

english: The king said, “Who is in the court?” Now Haman had come into the outer court of the king’s house, to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.
translation: Imfumu nayo aiti, “Ngo uli mu lubansa lwe sano lya mfumu nani?” Ilyo linefye Hamani ninshi elyo aingila mu lubansa lwa kunse ye sano lya mfumu, alefwaya ukulanda ne mfumu pakukulikila Modekai ku cimuti ico amupekanishishe.

english: The king’s servants said to him, “Behold, Haman stands in the court.” The king said, “Let him come in.”
translation: Ababomfi ba mfumu bayasuka abati, “Moneni Hamani naiminina mu lubansa.”

english: So Haman came in. The king said to him, “What shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor?” Now Haman said in his heart, “Who would the king delight to honor more than myself?”
translation: Kanshi Hamani aingila, elyo imfumu yamwipusha ukuti, “Kuliko umuntu umo ndefwaya ukucindika, bushe kuti namucitila nshi?”

english: Haman said to the king, “For the man whom the king delights to honor,
translation: Hamani epakweba imfumu ati, “Uyo muntu imfumu ilefwaya ukucindika,

english: let royal clothing be brought which the king uses to wear, and the horse that the king rides on, and on the head of which a royal crown is set.
translation: leteni ifyakufwala fyabufumu ifyo imfumu yafwalapo na kabalwe imfumu yaninapo, na ku mutwe wakwe kube ingala yabufumu.

english: Let the clothing and the horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king’s most noble princes, that they may array the man whom the king delights to honor with them, and have him ride on horseback through the city square, and proclaim before him, ‘Thus it shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!’”
translation: Elyo buulenipo umo pa balashi ba mfumu abacindamisha nganshi eo mupeele insalu na kabalwe. Uyu mulashi afwike uyu muntu imfumu ilefwaya ukucindika, umuteke na pali kabalwe no kumutandasha mu lubansa lonse ulwa musumba, no kubilikisha kuli bonse pa cinso cakwe ukuti, ‘Moneni ifi efyo imfumu icitila umuntu uo ilefwaya ukucindamika.’”

english: So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.
translation: Kanshi imfumu na Hamani baingila mu malila na namfumu Esta.

english: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the king’s wrath was pacified.
translation: Imfumu epakusosa ati, “Mukulikileni pali ico cine.” Kanshi bakulika Hamani pa cimuti apekenye ukwipailapo Modekai. Elyo ubukali bwa mfumu bwapwile.

english: The king said again to Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine, “What is your petition, queen Esther? It shall be granted you. What is your request? Even to the half of the kingdom it shall be performed.”
translation: Pali ubu bushiku bwacibili, elyo balenwa umwangashi panuma ya malila, imfumu yaipusha Esta nakabili aiti, “Bushe cinshi ulelomba iwe namfumu Esta? Ndekupeela. Cinshi ulefwaya? Nangufye ukufika kukwakanya ubufumu bwandi pakati, cilefikilishiwa!”

english: Then Esther the queen answered, “If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request.
translation: Elyo namfumu Esta ayasuka ati, “Nga cakuti ninsanga uluse, we mfumu, elyo kabili nga cakuti kuti casansamusha imfumu, kankwate ubumi ifyo ndefwaya, pamo na bantu bandi efyo ndelomba.

english: For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for male and female slaves, I would have held my peace, although the adversary could not have compensated for the king’s loss.”
translation: Pantu balitushitisha ine na bantu bandi pakuti batonaule, ukutwipaya no kutulofya. Abatushitishafye nga basha, abaume na banakashi, nga kuti nasunga icibote candi, pantu ukucula kwa musango uyu takwalinga ukuti twingacusha imfumu no mulandu wesu .”

english: Then King Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen, “Who is he, and where is he who dared presume in his heart to do so?”
translation: Elyo mfumu Asuelusi aipusha namfumu Esta ati, “Nani uyo wine, elyo ali kwi uulefwaya ukucita ifi?”

english: Esther said, “An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman!” Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.
translation: Esta epakwasuka ati, “Umulwani ne cipondo ni uyu Hamani, uwabipisha!”

english: The king arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden. Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen, for he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king.
translation: Elyo imfumu yaleka ukunwa umwangashi, yaima mu cifukushi yaya ingila na mwibala lya kwisano. Hamani ena ashala alepapata namfumu Esta pa bumi bwakwe pantu alimwene ubukali bwa mfumu ubwali nokumuponena.

english: Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman had fallen on the couch where Esther was. Then the king said, “Will he even assault the queen in front of me in the house?” As the word went out of the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.
translation: Ilyo imfumu yabwelele ukufuma mwibala lye sano, yafika mu muputule wa mitebeto, yasanga Hamani nawila pa ncende apaikele Esta. Imfumu epakusosa aiti, “Bushe tacene namfumu mu menso yandi, kabili mu ŋanda yandi?” Ilyo ishiwi lyafuminefye pa kanwa ka mfumu, bafimba Hamani pa menso.

english: Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs who were with the king, said, “Behold, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman has made for Mordecai, who spoke good for the king, is standing at Haman’s house.” The king said, “Hang him on it!”
translation: Elyo Habona umo pali bamutungwi abaletumika imfumu asosa ati, “Nakuba pa ŋanda yakwa Hamani paliko icimuti ico Hamani apekanishishe ukukulalikapo Modekai uyo amashiwi yakwe yakupuswishe, we mfumu. Ici cimuti cilepele amakubiti amakumi yasano (50) .”

english: On that day, King Ahasuerus gave the house of Haman, the Jews’ enemy, to Esther the queen. Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was to her.
translation: Ubushiku bulya imfumu Asuelusi yapeela namfumu Esta iŋanda yakwa Hamani umulwani wa Bayuda. Elyo Modekai aisa ku mfumu pantu Esta aliyebele ukuti muntu wakwe.

english: He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, and sealed it with the king’s ring, and sent letters by courier on horseback, riding on royal horses that were bred from swift steeds.
translation: Alembele kalata mwishina lya mfumu Asuelusi no kufwatikapo inshimbi ya mbalaminwe yakwe. Elyo atuma amakalata aya ne nkombe shalubilo ishaninine pali bakabalwe abalubilo nganshi abafyelwe kuli bakabalwe abasalwa abo imfumu yalebomfya.

english: In those letters, the king granted the Jews who were in every city to gather themselves together and to defend their lives—to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish all the power of the people and province that would assault them, their little ones and women, and to plunder their possessions,
translation: Mu makalata aya mwalembelwe ukuti Abayuda aba muli cila musumba nabapeelwa insambu ishakuti balongane no kucingilila ubumi bwabo, ukonaula, ukwipaya no kulofya abantu bonse nangu icitungu conse abaipekanya ku nkondo abengesa balwisha, pamo penefye na baice na banamayo, no kutapa ifyuma fyabo.

english: on one day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.
translation: Ifi fifwile ukucitika pa bushiku bumofye mu fitungu fyonse ifya calo ca mfumu Asuelusi, ubushiku bwalenga ikumi limo na shitatu (13) ubwa mu mweshi walenga ikumi limo na ibili (12), umweshi batila Ada.

english: A copy of the letter, that the decree should be given out in every province, was published to all the peoples, that the Jews should be ready for that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
translation: Icikope ca fyalembelwe cali nokupeelwa nge cebo mu fitungu fya calo fyonse, elyo cili nokubilwa ku bantu bonse pakuti Abayuda baipekanye pakwisa ipokololako ku balwani babo ilyo ubo bushiku bukafika.

english: So the couriers who rode on royal horses went out, hastened and pressed on by the king’s commandment. The decree was given out in the citadel of Susa.
translation: Kanshi inkombe shanina na pali bakabalwe balubilo abo imfumu yalebomfya, shaima bwangu bwangu ukulingana nefyo mfumu yabakonkomeshe. Kanshi efyo icebo capeelwe mu musumba wa Susa.

english: Mordecai went out of the presence of the king in royal clothing of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a robe of fine linen and purple; and the city of Susa shouted and was glad.
translation: Awe Modekai afuma pa cinso ca mfumu ninshi nafwala ne fyakufwala fyabufumu ifyacifufya ne fyabuuta, ne cisote cabufumu ica golide, no mwingila wapikulwa ubusaka uwakashikila, elyo umusumba wa Susa wapunda no kusansamuka.

english: The Jews had light, gladness, joy, and honor.
translation: Pantu kwaba ubuseko, ukwanga, insansa no bucindami ku Bayuda.

english: In every province and in every city, wherever the king’s commandment and his decree came, the Jews had gladness, joy, a feast and a holiday. Many from among the peoples of the land became Jews, for the fear of the Jews had fallen on them.
translation: Elyo kabili mu fitungu fya calo fyonse ne misumba yonse, ukwafikile icebo ca mfumu no bupingushi bwaiko, kwali nsansa no kwanga imitebeto no kutuusha mu Bayuda. Kanshi na bantu abengi aba mu calo cilya baicita ukuba Abayuda ico umwenso wakutiina Abayuda wabekata.

english: The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
translation: Kabili imfumu yafula imbalaminwe yakufwatikilako iyo yapokolwele kuli Hamani yapeela na Modekai. Esta nao apeela Modekai amaka pa ŋanda yakwa Hamani.

english: Esther spoke yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet and begged him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his plan that he had planned against the Jews.
translation: Elyo Esta abwekeshapo ukulanda ne mfumu. Awa pa nkasa shakwe alelila no kumupapata pakuti ekonka amapange ayabi yakwa Hamani umwina Agagi ayo apangile Abayuda.

english: Then the king held out to Esther the golden scepter. So Esther arose, and stood before the king.
translation: Ilyo imfumu yalangile Esta inkonto ya golide,

english: She said, “If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor in his sight, and the thing seems right to the king, and I am pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews who are in all the king’s provinces.
translation: Esta epakwima aya iminina na pali mfumu. Elyo asosa ati, “Nga cakuti casansamusha imfumu kabili nga ninsanga uluse pa cinso ca mfumu, nga cakuti ici cintu camoneka ukulungama ku mfumu elyo kabili nga cakuti ndi musuma pa cinso ca mfumu, imfumu nailembe icebo icakonaula amakalata Hamani umwina Agagi, umwana wakwa Hamedata, alembele ayakonaula Abayuda mu fitungu fyonse ifya calo ca mfumu.

english: For how can I endure to see the evil that would come to my people? How can I endure to see the destruction of my relatives?”
translation: Bushe ine kuti natemwa shani ukumona icinkunka icileishila abantu bandi? Bushe kuti nashipikisha shani ukumona ubonaushi bwa ba lupwa lwandi?”

english: Then King Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, “See, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and they have hanged him on the gallows because he laid his hand on the Jews.
translation: Elyo imfumu Asuelusi aeba namfumu Esta na Modekai Umuyuda ati, “Moneni, napeela Esta iŋanda yakwa Hamani, kabili bakulikile Hamani pa cimuti pantu alefwaya ukwipaya Abayuda.

english: Write also to the Jews as it pleases you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring; for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may not be reversed by any man.”
translation: Nomba kuti mwalembelako Abayuda mu musango mulefwailamo mwishina lya mfumu. Mufwatikepo ne nshimbi ya mbalaminwe ya mfumu, pantu icebo cilembelwe mwishina lya mfumu nacumwapo ne nshimbi ya mbalaminwe ya mfumu, teti cipilibulwe.”

english: Then the king’s scribes were called at that time, in the third month, which is the month Sivan, on the twenty-third day of the month; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded to the Jews, and to the local governors, and the governors and princes of the provinces which are from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven provinces, to every province according to its writing, and to every people in their language, and to the Jews in their writing, and in their language.
translation: Pali ilya ine nshita bakalemba ba mfumu balibetile, cali mu mweshi wabutatu, umweshi uo baleti Sifani, pa bushiku bwalenga amakumi yabili na shitatu (23). Kanshi icebo epakulembwa ukulingana nefyo Modekai abebele palwa Bayuda, no kutuma bacituma ku nkonkani sha mfumu shonse, na balashi aba cila citungu ca calo ca mfumu na bakalamba ba bantu ukufuma ku India ukufika na ku Kushi . Ifitungu fyali umwanda umo na makumi yabili na cine lubali (127). Ici cebo calembelwe ukulingana ne filembo fya cila citungu no lulimi lwa cila mutundu. Kabili calembelwe na ku Bayuda ukulingana ne filembo fyabo no lulimi lwabo.

english: Now in the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the month, when the king’s commandment and his decree came near to be put in execution, on the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to conquer them, (but it turned out that the opposite happened, that the Jews conquered those who hated them),
translation: Kanshi mu mweshi walenga ikumi limo na ibili (12), umweshi batila Ada, pa bushiku bwalenga ikumi limo na shitatu (13) ubwa uyu wine mweshi, icebo ne cipope ca mfumu fyali nokucitikilapo. Ubushiku bwine ubo ebo abalwani ba Bayuda balesubila ukubacimfya, nomba fyayaluka. Bayuda ebacimfishe ababapatile.

english: the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Jews’ enemy, but they didn’t lay their hand on the plunder.
translation: abana ikumi limo abakwa Hamani mwana Hamedata, umulwani wa Bayuda. Lelo ifyuma fyabo fyena tabafitapile iyoo.

english: On that day, the number of those who were slain in the citadel of Susa was brought before the king.
translation: Pa bushiku bwine ubo baya shimikilako imfumu impendwa ya bantu baipeye mu musumba wa Susa.

english: The king said to Esther the queen, “The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in the citadel of Susa, including the ten sons of Haman; what then have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces! Now what is your petition? It shall be granted you. What is your further request? It shall be done.”
translation: Elyo imfumu yaeba namfumu Esta aiti, “Mu musumba wa Susa, Abayuda bepeye no konaula abaume imyanda isano (500) elyo na bana bakwa Hamani ikumi limo. Nga kanshi mu fitungu fimbi fya calo ca mfumu finshi bacitilemo? Finshi fimbi ifyo ulelomba? Filepeelwa kuli iwe. Cinshi ulefwaya? Cilefikilishiwa.”

english: Then Esther said, “If it pleases the king, let it be granted to the Jews who are in Susa to do tomorrow also according to today’s decree, and let Haman’s ten sons be hanged on the gallows.”
translation: Elyo Esta ayasuka ati, “Nga cakuti cakusekesha we mfumu, leka Abayuda aba muno Susa basuminishiwe ukucita nakabili mailo ifyo bacitile ukulingana ne cebo ca bushiku bwa lelo. Lekeni bamwana Hamani ikumi babakulikile pa fimuti.”

english: The king commanded this to be done. A decree was given out in Susa; and they hanged Haman’s ten sons.
translation: Kanshi imfumu epakupeela icebo icakucita ifyo fine. Ne funde lyapeelwa mu musumba wa Susa, na bana ikumi limo abakwa Hamani babakulika.

english: The Jews who were in Susa gathered themselves together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and killed three hundred men in Susa; but they didn’t lay their hand on the plunder.
translation: Abayuda abali mu Susa balongana nakabili pa bushiku bwalenga ikumi limo na shine (14) ubwa mu mweshi wa Ada, baipaya abaume imyanda itatu (300) lelo tabasampile ifyuma.

english: The other Jews who were in the king’s provinces gathered themselves together, defended their lives, had rest from their enemies, and killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them; but they didn’t lay their hand on the plunder.
translation: Elyo Abayuda bambi balongana mu fitungu fya calo ca mfumu, baicingilila no kuipokololako ku balwani babo, no kwipaya ababapatile amakana amakumi cine lubali na yasano (75,000) nomba tabasampile ifyuma fyabo.

english: This was done on the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of that month they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
translation: Ubu bwali bushiku bwalenga ikumi limo na shitatu (13) ubwa mu mweshi wa Ada. Elyo pa bushiku bwalenga ikumi limo na shine (14) balituushishe no kubucita ubwakusefya ne nsansa.

english: But the Jews who were in Susa assembled together on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth days of the month; and on the fifteenth day of that month, they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
translation: Abayuda bali mu Susa bena balongene pa bushiku bwalenga ikumi limo na shitatu (13) no bwalenga ikumi limo na bune (14), elyo nomba ubwalenga ikumi limo na busano (15) batuusha no kubucita ubwakusefya ne nsansa.

english: Therefore the Jews of the villages, who live in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, a holiday, and a day of sending presents of food to one another.
translation: E mulandu walenga ukuti Abayuda, balya bekala mu ncende sha mu mushi, balecindika ubushiku bwalenga ikumi limo na shine (14) ubwa mu mweshi wa Ada. Ubu bushiku buba bwakusansamukamo, ukusefya no kutuusha, bushiku bwakupeelana ubupe bwa fyakulya.

english: the Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the King Ahasuerus, to lay hands on those who wanted to harm them. No one could withstand them, because the fear of them had fallen on all the people.
translation: Abayuda mu misumba yonse na mu fitungu fyonse ifya calo ca mfumu Asuelusi balongana mukwipaya abo abalefwaya ukubalofya. Kanshi tapali nangu umo uwakubalwisha pantu umwenso wakubatiina waliketefye abantu bonse.

english: Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of the King Ahasuerus, both near and far,
translation: Modekai alembele ifintu fyonse no kutuma amakalata ku Bayuda bonse mu fitungu fyonse fya calo ca mfumu Asuelusi ifyakutali ne fyamupepi.

english: to enjoin them that they should keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month Adar yearly,
translation: Mu makalata aya abakonkomeshe ukucindika ubushiku bwalenga ikumi limo na bune (14) ubwa mu mweshi wa Ada elyo no bwalenga ikumi limo na shisano (15) cila mwaka.

english: as the days in which the Jews had rest from their enemies, and the month which was turned to them from sorrow to gladness, and from mourning into a holiday; that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, and of sending presents of food to one another, and gifts to the needy.
translation: Pantu e bushiku Abayuda balubwikemo ku balwani babo, kabili e mweshi ubulanda bwabo bwayalwikemo insansa, no kuloosha kwabo kwayalwike ubushiku bwakutuusha. Ishi nshiku shifwile shaba shakusansamukamo no kusefya. Ni nshiku shakupeelanamo ubupe bwa fyakulya ne shakupeelamo abalanda ifyabupe.

english: The Jews accepted the custom that they had begun, as Mordecai had written to them,
translation: Kanshi Abayuda basuminisha ifyalembele Modekai, bayamba no kufikonka.

english: because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast “Pur”, that is the lot, to consume them and to destroy them;
translation: Hamani umwina Agagi umwana wakwa Hamedata, umulwani wa Bayuda ewali na mapange yakulofya Abayuda no kubuula Puri pakupendula pakuti abonaule no kubalofya.

english: but when this became known to the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked plan, which he had planned against the Jews, should return on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
translation: Nomba ilyo imfumu yaumfwile ifi ukufuma kuli Esta, yalipingwile no kulemba ukuti amapange yakwe ayabi ayo akwatile Abayuda yamwalukile, ena na bana bakwe babakulike no kubakulikila ku fimuti.

english: Therefore they called these days “Purim”, from the word “Pur.” Therefore because of all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and that which had come to them,
translation: E mulandu wine bainikile inshiku ati Purimu ukufumya kwishiwi lya puri. Kabili ni pa mulandu wa fyonse ifyalembelwe muli iyi kalata nefyo bamwene ne fyabaponene,

english: the Jews established and imposed on themselves, on their descendants, and on all those who joined themselves to them, so that it should not fail that they would keep these two days according to what was written and according to its appointed time every year;
translation: Abayuda baipangile no kukonka ulutambi pamo na bana babo na bantu bonsefye ukucindika cila mwaka apabula ukufilwa ishi nshiku shibili umo mwine calembelwa na pa nshita iyasalwa cila mwaka.

english: and that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor their memory perish from their offspring.
translation: Ishi nshiku shibili bafwile bashicindika no kushikonka mu nkulo shonse, mu ndupwa shonse na mu fitungu fyonse ifya calo, na mu misumba monse. Elyo ishi nshiku sha Purimu tabafwile baleka ukushisefya ku Muyuda onse nelyo ukuleka ukushibukisha mu bana ba mu lupwa lwabo.

english: Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.
translation: Elyo namfumu Esta, umwana wakwa Abihaili, na Modekai Umuyuda balemba inkalata yabubili no kubikapo amaka nganshi ukushininkisha palwa nshikunkulu ya Purimu.

english: All the princes of the provinces, the local governors, the governors, and those who did the king’s business helped the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai had fallen on them.
translation: Bonsefye abalashi ba mfumu aba mu fitungu fya calo, inkonkani sha mfumu, bakateeka na babomfi ba mfumu bayafwilisha Abayuda pantu umwenso wakutiina Modekai walibekete.

english: He sent letters to all the Jews in the hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus with words of peace and truth,
translation: Aya makalata yatuminwe ku Bayuda bonse aba mu fitungu fyonse umwanda umo amakumi yabili na cine lubali (127) ifya calo ca mfumu Asuelusi mu mashiwi yacibote no kubateeka imitima.

english: to confirm these days of Purim in their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had decreed, and as they had imposed upon themselves and their descendants in the matter of the fastings and their mourning.
translation: Amashiwi yali mu makalata yabakonkomesha ukuti bakalesefya inshiku sha Purimu pa nshita iyasontwa pamo ngefyo namfumu Esta na Modekai Umuyuda babebele ukucita pamo na bana babo mukukonka ulutambi lwakufunga ukulya no kuloosha.

english: The commandment of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.
translation: Icebo capeele Esta ecalengele ukuti ukusefya Purimu kube ulutambi elyo no kulembwa mu citabo.

english: For Mordecai was great in the king’s house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces, for the man Mordecai grew greater and greater.
translation: Pantu Modekai ali na maka ayengi mu ŋanda ya mfumu, no lulumbi lwakwe lwalikumene mu calo conse, pantu amaka Modekai akwete yalekulilakofye.

english: The Jews struck all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and with slaughter and destruction, and did what they wanted to those who hated them.
translation: Kanshi Abayuda bakoma bonse abalwani babo ku lupanga, ukubepaya no kubonaula no kucita abalwani babo mu musango balefwailamo.

english: In the citadel of Susa, the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.
translation: Mu musumba wa Susa wekafye Abayuda baipeye no konaula abantu abaume imyanda isano (500).

english: They killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
translation: Kabili baipaya na Pashandata na Dalufoni na Asipata,

english: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,
translation: na Porata, na Adalia, na Aridata,

english: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha,
translation: na Pamashita na Arisai na Aridai na Faisata,

english: The LORD said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the heart of his servants, that I may show these my signs among them;
translation: Elyo Yawe aebele Mose ati, “Kabiye kuli Farao, pantu ninenga umutima wakwe ne mitima ya bacilolo bakwe ukumalala pakuti ncite ifipeshamano uko bali.

english: He said to them, “The LORD be with you if I let you go with your little ones! See, evil is clearly before your faces.
translation: Farao abatumfya ati, “Yawe abe na imwe, nga cakuti ndemuleka muye na banakashi benu na bana benu! Ninshi cine cine muli na mapange ayabi.

english: Not so! Go now you who are men, and serve the LORD; for that is what you desire!” Then they were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.
translation: Awe iyoo! Abaumefye beka ebo baye kukupepa Yawe pantu efyo mwalelomba.” Awe batamfya Mose na Aroni ukufuma ku cinso cakwa Farao.

english: The LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up on the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land, even all that the hail has left.”
translation: Elyo Yawe aebele Mose ati, “Tambalikila ukuboko kobe pa calo ca Egupto pakuti makanta ese pa calo. Aleisa lya fyonse ifilepuka mu mabala ne fyapuswike ku mfula ya mabwe.”

english: Moses stretched out his rod over the land of Egypt, and the LORD brought an east wind on the land all that day, and all night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts.
translation: Awe Mose atambalikila inkonto pa calo ca Egupto. Yawe nao aimya umwela ku kabanga walapupa pa calo ca Egupto akasubafye konse no bushikufye bonse. Cilya buleca ulucelo ninshi umwela waleta makanta,

english: The locusts went up over all the land of Egypt, and rested in all the borders of Egypt. They were very grievous. Before them there were no such locusts as they, nor will there ever be again.
translation: akupafye icalo conse ca Egupto. Kabili makanta asalanganinefye mpanga yonse mu calo. Awe takwatalile akuba makanta uwafula ifi, kabili takwakatale akuba uwafula fi.

english: For they covered the surface of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened, and they ate every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail had left. There remained nothing green, either tree or herb of the field, through all the land of Egypt.
translation: Akupile pa mushili ponse pasuka pafiita na fititi. Alya fyonse ifyapuswike ku mfula ya mabwe. Alya fyonse ifyalepuka mu mabala ne fitwalo fya ku miti. Mu calo conse ca Egupto tamwashele ibula nelyo limo ku miti nangu ku fimena panshi fyonse.

english: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste, and he said, “I have sinned against the LORD your God, and against you.
translation: Elyo Farao aitile Mose na Aroni bwangu bwangu, abeba ati, “Nimbifya kuli Yawe, Lesa wenu, elyo na kuli imwe bene.

english: Now therefore please forgive my sin again, and pray to the LORD your God, that he may also take away from me this death.”
translation: Mbeleleniko uluse uno winefye muku, mumpapatileko na kuli Yawe, Lesa wenu, afumye pali ine ici cinkunka cabipisha.”

english: Moses went out from Pharaoh, and prayed to the LORD.
translation: Elyo Mose afuma pali Farao alapapata Yawe.

english: The LORD sent an exceedingly strong west wind, which took up the locusts, and drove them into the Red Sea. There remained not one locust in all the borders of Egypt.
translation: Yawe nao epakwalula umwela walapupa na maka nganshi ukufuma ku masamba. Awe waulula makanta onse no kumutwala muli Bemba Wakashika . Tamwashele makanta nelyo umo mu calo ca Egupto.

english: and that you may tell in the hearing of your son, and of your son’s son, what things I have done to Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them; that you may know that I am the LORD.”
translation: Epakuti ukaleshimikilako abana bobe na beshikulu bobe ifyo nafulwile abena Egupto ilyo nalecita ifipeshamano uko bali, pakuti mwishibe ukuti ine ndi Yawe.”

english: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he didn’t let the children of Israel go.
translation: Lelo Yawe alengele umutima wakwa Farao ukumalala, akaana nokuleka abana bakwa Israeli ukuti baleya.

english: The LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.”
translation: Elyo Yawe aebele Mose ati, “Imisha ukuboko kobe mu mulu, ne mfifi yalakupa icalo conse ca Egupto, imfifi iyakuti umuntu aipampanta.”

english: Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days.
translation: Mose nao aimisha ukuboko kwakwe mu mulu, awe ne mfifi iyafitisha fititi yakupa ne calo ca Egupto conse pa nshiku shitatu.

english: They didn’t see one another, and nobody rose from his place for three days; but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.
translation: Abena Egupto balafilwa ukumona ababiye, balafilwa no kufuma apo bali pa nshiku shitatu. Lelo ku bena Israeli kwena kwali ulubuuto, takwali mfifi iyoo.

english: Pharaoh called to Moses, and said, “Go, serve the LORD. Only let your flocks and your herds stay behind. Let your little ones also go with you.”
translation: Elyo Farao aitile Mose, amweba ati, “Kabiyeni muye mupepe Yawe. Musende na banakashi na bana, lelo impaanga ne mbushi ne ŋombe shena shishale kuno.”

english: Moses said, “You must also give into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.
translation: Lelo Mose nao ayasuka ati, “Uli nokutulekafye tusende inama shakulekela Yawe, Lesa wesu, ilambo ne sha mutuulo wakoca.

english: Our livestock also shall go with us. Not a hoof shall be left behind, for of it we must take to serve the LORD our God; and we don’t know with what we must serve the LORD, until we come there.”
translation: Awe tuli nokuya ne fitekwa fyesu fyonse, tapakashale nelyo cimo. Tukabomfyapo fimo pakupepa Yawe, Lesa wesu. Nomba teti twishibe ifyo tukabomfya pakupepa ilyo tushilafika kulya.”

english: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he wouldn’t let them go.
translation: Yawe alengele umutima wakwa Farao ukumalala, kabili akaana no kubaleka baleya.

english: Pharaoh said to him, “Get away from me! Be careful to see my face no more; for in the day you see my face you shall die!”
translation: Amalu 105:28

english: Moses said, “You have spoken well. I will see your face again no more.”
translation: Mose nao ayasuka ati, “Ifyo fine wasosa, ine nshakatale moneka ku cinso cobe nakabili.”

english: Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and said to him, “This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, that they may serve me.
translation: Kanshi Mose na Aroni baile kuli Farao bamweba abati, “Ifi efyo Yawe, Lesa wa Bahibulu, asosa ati, ‘Bushe iwe ukaleka lilali ukukanaicefya pali ine? Leka abantu bandi baleya, pakuti baye mpepa.

english: Or else, if you refuse to let my people go, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your country,
translation: Nga wabalesha ukuti baleya, mailo nkaleta makanta mu calo cobe.

english: and they shall cover the surface of the earth, so that one won’t be able to see the earth. They shall eat the residue of that which has escaped, which remains to you from the hail, and shall eat every tree which grows for you out of the field.
translation: Makanta akakupafye ponse pa mushili icakuti no mushili tawakalemoneka. Akesa lya fyonse ifyapuswikeko ku mfula ya mabwe, akesa lya ne miti yonse iyilepuka mu mabala.

english: Your houses shall be filled, and the houses of all your servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians, as neither your fathers nor your fathers’ fathers have seen, since the day that they were on the earth to this day.’” He turned, and went out from Pharaoh.
translation: Akesula mwisano lyobe na mu mayanda ya bacilolo bobe na mu mayanda ya bena Egupto bonse. Ici cena bashinwe ne fikolwe fyenu tabacimonapo apo baishile pesonde lino ukufika na lelo.’” Awe Mose apilibuka alaya asha Farao.

english: Pharaoh’s servants said to him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the men go, that they may serve the LORD, their God. Don’t you yet know that Egypt is destroyed?”
translation: Bacilolo bakwa Farao bamweba abati, “Bushe uyu muntu akaleka lilali ukulatucusha? Shilekafye abantu baleya pakuti baye bapepe Yawe, Lesa wabo. Bushe taumwene ifyo icalo ca Egupto conaike?”

english: Moses and Aaron were brought again to Pharaoh, and he said to them, “Go, serve the LORD your God; but who are those who will go?”
translation: Elyo babweseshe Mose na Aroni kuli Farao, nao abeba ati, “Kabiyeni kukupepa Yawe, Lesa wenu. Nomba bushe abaleya ni bani?”

english: Moses said, “We will go with our young and with our old. We will go with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds; for we must hold a feast to the LORD.”
translation: Mose ayasuka ati, “Tuleya na baice na bakote besu, abana besu abaume na banakashi, tulesenda ne mpaanga, imbushi ne ŋombe shesu pantu tuleya kukucitila Yawe inshikunkulu.”

english: The LORD said to Moses, “I will bring yet one more plague on Pharaoh, and on Egypt; afterwards he will let you go. When he lets you go, he will surely thrust you out altogether.
translation: Elyo Yawe aebele Mose ati, “Nalaleta icinkunka na cimbi icakulekelesha pali Farao na pa calo ca Egupto. Panuma ya ifyo lyena akaleka mukafume kuno. Ilyo akacita ifyo, akamutamfyamofye bonse.

english: Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh, but the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he didn’t let the children of Israel go out of his land.
translation: Mose na Aroni bacitile ifisungusho ifi fyonse pa menso yakwa Farao. Lelo Yawe aumike umutima wakwe, nao akaana no kuleka abena Israeli ukuti bafume mu calo cakwe.

english: Speak now in the ears of the people, and let every man ask of his neighbor, and every woman of her neighbor, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold.”
translation: Kanshi eba abena Israeli, abaume na banakashi bena ukuti balombe ifintu fya silifa ne fya golide ku bena mupalamano babo.”

english: The LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover, the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh’s servants, and in the sight of the people.
translation: Kabili Yawe alengele abena Egupto ukukwatila abena Israeli umucinshi. Mose nao ali umuntu mucindami nganshi mu calo ca Egupto, abantu na bacilolo bakwa Farao balimucindike.

english: Moses said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘About midnight I will go out into the middle of Egypt,
translation: Elyo Mose aebele Farao ati, “Ifi efyo Yawe asosa ati, ‘Ubushiku pakati, ndepitana mu calo conse ca Egupto.

english: and all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne, even to the firstborn of the female servant who is behind the mill, and all the firstborn of livestock.
translation: Amabeli yonse ayaume mu calo ca Egupto yalefwa. Ukutendekelafye pebeli lyakwa Farao, ilili nokumupyana pa cipuna cabufumu, ukufika na kwibeli lya musha umwanakashi uupela ubunga, na mabeli ya fitekwa yonse yali nokufwa.

english: There will be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there has not been, nor will be any more.
translation: Kabili mu calo conse ica Egupto mukaba ukuloosha ukukalamba ukushatala akubamo kabili takwakatale akubamo.

english: But against any of the children of Israel a dog won’t even bark or move its tongue, against man or animal, that you may know that the LORD makes a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel.
translation: Lelo mu bena Israeli mwena nangufye ni mbwa tayakabosele pa muntu nelyo umo nelyo pa citekwa.’ Elyo mukeshiba ukuti Yawe alalekanya pakati ka bena Egupto na bena Israeli.

english: All these servants of yours will come down to me, and bow down themselves to me, saying, “Get out, with all the people who follow you;” and after that I will go out.’” He went out from Pharaoh in hot anger.
translation: Kabili bacilolo bobe bonse bakesa kuli ine no kumfukamina, bakasosa nokuti, ‘Kabiye, iwe na bantu bobe bonse abakukonka.’ Panuma ya ifyo ninshi nkaya.” Awe Mose afuma ne cipyu pali Farao.

english: The LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh won’t listen to you, that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.”
translation: Yawe aebele Mose ati, “Farao takakumfwe nakalya epakuti nkacite ifisungusho ifingi mu calo ca Egupto.”

english: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
translation: Yawe aebele Mose na Aroni mu calo ca Egupto ati,

english: You shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; but that which remains of it until the morning you shall burn with fire.
translation: Kabili mwikaleka nelyo cimo cikafike ku lucelo. Ifikashalapo fyonse ukufika ulucelo mukoce.

english: This is how you shall eat it: with your belt on your waist, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in haste: it is the LORD’s Passover.
translation: Kanshi ifi efyo muli nokulya iyi nama namupimpa insalu shenu mushifyantike mu mushipi, namufwala ne ndyato shenu kabili namwikata ne nkonto shenu mu minwe. Mulye mukwangufyanya pantu lipasaka lyakwa Yawe.

english: For I will go through the land of Egypt in that night, and will strike all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and animal. I will execute judgments against all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
translation: Pali bulya bwine ubushiku, nkapita mu calo conse ica Egupto mu nshita ya bushiku no kwipaya amabeli yonse aya bantu ne nama. Kabili nkakanda imilungu yonse iya bena Egupto. Nine Yawe.

english: The blood shall be to you for a token on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will be on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
translation: Umulopa eukaba icishibilo cenu pa mayanda umo muli. Nkalacilila nga namona umulopa. Imwe icinkunka tacakamonaule ico nkaponesha pa bena Egupto.

english: This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall keep it as a feast to the LORD. You shall keep it as a feast throughout your generations by an ordinance forever.
translation: “Mukaleibukisha ubu bushiku mu nkulo shenu shonse. Mukalebusefya nge nshikunkulu yakwa Yawe. Ili lifunde lyakubelelela.

english: “‘Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; even the first day you shall put away yeast out of your houses, for whoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.
translation: Ukuf 23:15

english: You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread; for in this same day I have brought your armies out of the land of Egypt. Therefore you shall observe this day throughout your generations by an ordinance forever.

There shall be no yeast found in your houses for seven days, for whoever eats that which is leavened, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he is a foreigner, or one who is born in the land.
translation: Muli ishi nshiku cine lubali, intutumushi taili nakusangwa mu mayanda yenu. Noyo onse uukalya icintu umuli intutumushi, wakutamfyafye mu lukuta lwa bena Israeli, nangu abe umweni nangu mwana calo.

english: “This month shall be to you the beginning of months. It shall be the first month of the year to you.
translation: “Uno mweshi ewakulaba kuli imwe uwakubalilapo, umweshi wakutendeka mu mwaka wenu.

english: You shall eat nothing leavened. In all your habitations you shall eat unleavened bread.’”
translation: Mwikalya cintu nangu cimo umuli intutumushi. Konse uko muli, mukalelya umukate umwabula intutumushi.”

english: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said to them, “Draw out, and take lambs according to your families, and kill the Passover.
translation: Elyo Mose aitile abakalamba bonse aba mu bena Israeli abeba ati, “Kabiyeni nombaline, muye salila indupwa shenu inama, mwipaye umwana wa mpaanga wa pe Pasaka.

english: You shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike the lintel and the two door posts with the blood that is in the basin. None of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning.
translation: Mubuule utumisambo twa hisopo mutumpike mu mulopa uuli mu lunweno, mushinge pamulu elyo na mumbali ya filu fya pa mwinshi wa ŋanda. Kwikaba nelyo umo uwakufumina panse mpaka ulucelo.

english: For the LORD will pass through to strike the Egyptians; and when he sees the blood on the lintel, and on the two door posts, the LORD will pass over the door, and will not allow the destroyer to come in to your houses to strike you.
translation: Ilyo Yawe akalapita mu calo conse ica Egupto kukwipaya abena Egupto, akalacilila nga amona umulopa ku filu fya pa mwinshi na pa mulu wa ciibi. Yawe akalesha malaika wa mfwa ukwingila mu ŋanda yenu no kumwipaya.

english: You shall observe this thing for an ordinance to you and to your sons forever.
translation: Mukalebaka ifi fyonse mwebele nge funde lyakubelelela kuli imwe ne ndupwa shenu.

english: It shall happen when you have come to the land which the LORD will give you, as he has promised, that you shall keep this service.
translation: Nga mwafika mu calo Yawe alaya ukumupeela, mukalebaka ifi fyonse mwebele.

english: It will happen, when your children ask you, ‘What do you mean by this service?’
translation: Ilyo abana benu bakamwipusha abati, ‘Ngefi fyonse filolele mwi?’

english: that you shall say, ‘It is the sacrifice of the LORD’s Passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians, and spared our houses.’” The people bowed their heads and worshiped.
translation: Mukalebeba mwati, ‘Lilambo lye Pasaka lyakwa Yawe uwacilile amayanda ya bena Israeli mu calo ca Egupto no kupususha abana besu, lelo aipeye abena Egupto.’” Awe abantu bafukama balapepa.

english: The children of Israel went and did so; as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.
translation: Bahi 11:28

english: At midnight, the LORD struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of livestock.
translation: Pakati ka bushiku, Yawe aipeye amabeli yonse mu calo ca Egupto, ukutendekelafye kwibeli lyakwa Farao uwaleikala pa cipuna cabufumu, ukufika na kwibeli lya mufungwa uwali mu cifungo, na mabeli ya fitekwa fyonse aliyepeye.

english: Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying, ‘On the tenth day of this month, they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to their fathers’ houses, a lamb for a household;
translation: Mwebe ulukuta lonse ulwa bena Israeli amuti, pa bushiku ubwalenga ikumi ubwa uno wine mweshi, umwaume onse akafwaile aba mu lupwa lwakwe umwana wa mpaanga umo pali cila ŋanda.

english: Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not one dead.
translation: Farao na bacilolo bakwe bonse na bena Egupto bonse balibukile ubushiku. Awe mwali misowa iyikalamba mu calo ca Egupto, pantu takwali ŋanda nangu imo umushafwile muntu.

english: He called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, “Rise up, get out from among my people, both you and the children of Israel; and go, serve the LORD, as you have said!
translation: Ilyo line ubushiku Farao aita Mose na Aroni abeba ati, “Imeni, fumeni mu bantu bandi imwe na bena Israeli! Kabiyeni mukupepa Yawe nga filya fine mwalombele.

english: Take both your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and be gone; and bless me also!”
translation: Pamo ngefyo mwasosele, musende impaanga, imbushi ne ŋombe shenu muleya. Elyo na ine mumpaaleko.”

english: The Egyptians were urgent with the people, to send them out of the land in haste, for they said, “We are all dead men.”
translation: Abena Egupto balapamfya abena Israeli ukuti bafume mu calo bwangu bwangu abati, “Pantu limbi bonse kuti twafwa.”

english: The people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneading troughs being bound up in their clothes on their shoulders.
translation: Kanshi abena Israeli babikile umufuba uwabulamo intutumushi mu fyakukashilamo, bafipomba mu nsalu, basenda na pa mabeya yabo.

english: The children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they asked of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing.
translation: Kabili abena Israeli bacitile ifyo Mose abebele, balombele ku bena Egupto ifintu fya silifa ne fya golide elyo ne fyakufwala.

english: The LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they let them have what they asked. They plundered the Egyptians.
translation: Kabili Yawe alengele abena Egupto ukukwatila abena Israeli umucinshi, kabili babapeele ne fintu fyonse ifyo balebalomba. Kanshi efyo abena Israeli batapile ifyuma fya bena Egupto.

english: The children of Israel traveled from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot who were men, in addition to children.
translation: Abena Israeli baendele ukufuma ku Ramesesi, ukuya ku Sukoti. Abaume beka beka aba pa makasa bali amakana imyanda mutanda (600,000) ukwabula ukupendelako abanakashi na baice.

english: A mixed multitude went up also with them, with flocks, herds, and even very much livestock.
translation: Kabili ibumba ilikalamba ilya bantu bambi lyaile nabo pamo ne fitekwa, impaanga, imbushi ne ŋombe.

english: They baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought out of Egypt; for it wasn’t leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt, and couldn’t wait, and they had not prepared any food for themselves.
translation: Bapangile imikate iyishatutumuka ku mufuba untu bafumine nao mu Egupto. Mu mufuba tamwali ntutumushi iyoo, pantu babatamfishefye mu calo ca Egupto, tabakwete na nshita yakupekanya ifyakulya fya pa lwendo nakalya.

english: and if the household is too little for a lamb, then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take one according to the number of the souls. You shall make your count for the lamb according to what everyone can eat.
translation: Aba mu ŋanda imo nga bacepa icakuti bafilwa ukupwa umwana wa mpaanga, bali nokwakana no mwina mupalamano, ukulingana ne mpendwa ya bantu ba mu ŋanda yakwe. Muli nokupima impaanga ilefwaikwa ukulingana umo cila umo engaliila.

english: Now the time that the children of Israel lived in Egypt was four hundred thirty years.
translation: Inshita abena Israeli baikele mu calo ca Egupto yali imyaka imyanda ine na makumi yatatu (430).

english: At the end of four hundred thirty years, to the day, all of the LORD’s armies went out from the land of Egypt.
translation: Pali ubo bwine bushiku bwakupwa kwa myaka imyanda ine na makumi yatatu (430), impuka shonse shakwa Yawe shafumine mu calo ca Egupto.

english: It is a night to be much observed to the LORD for bringing them out from the land of Egypt. This is that night of the LORD, to be much observed by all the children of Israel throughout their generations.
translation: Pali ubo bushiku Yawe alolele bushiku bonse pakuti abafumye mu Egupto. Kanshi, pali ubu bushiku abena Israeli bali nokulalolamo pakucindika Yawe mu nkulo shabo shonse ishikakonkapo.

english: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the ordinance of the Passover. No foreigner shall eat of it,
translation: Yawe aebele Mose na Aroni ati, “Amafunde yakukonka aye Pasaka inshikunkulu ya Cakucilila ni aya. Umwinafyalo onse tafwile kulyako Ipasaka.

english: but every man’s servant who is bought for money, when you have circumcised him, then shall he eat of it.
translation: Lelo umusha onse uo washita kuti alyako nga cakuti walimusembulula.

english: A foreigner and a hired servant shall not eat of it.
translation: Lelo umweni na uyo waingisha incito, bena tabafwile kulyako iyoo.

english: It must be eaten in one house. You shall not carry any of the meat outside of the house. Do not break any of its bones.
translation: Mufwile ukuliilafye inama yonse mu ŋanda imo, tekwesha ukufumisha umupusa wa nama panse. Kabili tekwesha ukutoba ifupa nelyo limo.

english: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.
translation: Ulukuta lwa bena Israeli lonse lukalesefya inshikunkulu ye Pasaka,

english: When a stranger lives as a foreigner with you, and would like to keep the Passover to the LORD, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it. He shall be as one who is born in the land; but no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
translation: Umwinafyalo onse uwaikala na imwe nga alefwaya ukulyako Ipasaka lyakucindika Yawe, afwile ukusembulula abaume bonse aba mu ŋanda yakwe. Lyena kuti alalyako nga bakaya mu calo. Lelo umwaume onse uushasembululwa wena tali nakulyako.

english: One law shall be to him who is born at home, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you.”
translation: Umwana calo no mweni mwikala nao bonse bali nokusunga ifunde limo line.”

english: Your lamb shall be without defect, a male a year old. You shall take it from the sheep or from the goats.
translation: Levi 23:5

english: All the children of Israel did so. As the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.
translation: Abena Israeli bonse bacitile fyonse ifyo Yawe akonkomeshe Mose na Aroni.

english: That same day, the LORD brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their armies.
translation: Kabili muli bulya bwine bushiku Yawe afumishe abena Israeli bonse mu calo ca Egupto mu mpuka mu mpuka shabo.

english: You shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month; and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it at evening.
translation: Mukashisunge mpaka no bushiku ubwalenga ikumi na shine (14) ubwa uno mweshi. Elyo ulukuta lwa bena Israeli lonse lukashipaye lilya akasuba kaba kukuwa.

english: They shall take some of the blood, and put it on the two door posts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they shall eat it.
translation: Elyo abantu bakabuulepo umulopa umo, bakashinge mumbali elyo na pa mulu wa filu fya pa mwinshi wa mayanda bakalaliilamo.

english: They shall eat the meat in that night, roasted with fire, with unleavened bread. They shall eat it with bitter herbs.
translation: Mu nshita ya bushiku bwine ubo bakoca inama pa mulilo no kuilila pamo ne mikate iyishatutumuka ne misalu iyalula.

english: Don’t eat it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roasted with fire; with its head, its legs and its inner parts.
translation: Mwikalya inama iyibishi nangu iyaipikwa lelo mukalyefye yonse iyaocewa, umutwe, imyendo ne fya munda fyonse.

english: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
translation: Yawe aebele Mose ati,

english: You shall therefore keep this ordinance in its season from year to year.
translation: Muli nokusunga ili funde cila mwaka pa nshita iyasontwa.”

english: “It shall be, when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanite, as he swore to you and to your fathers, and will give it to you,
translation: “Ilyo Yawe akamufisha mu calo ca bena Kenani, ico alaile no mulapo kuli imwe ne fikolwe fyenu ukuti akamupeela,

english: that you shall set apart to the LORD all that opens the womb, and every firstborn that comes from an animal which you have. The males shall be the LORD’s.
translation: mufwile mukaletuula na mabeli yonse kuli Yawe. Kabili amabeli yonse ayalume aya fitekwa fyenu yakwa Yawe.
