english: Before he had finished speaking, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher on her shoulder.
translation: Kutifye talati apwe no kupepa, Rebeka aisa, nasenda no mutondo pa kubeya. Uyu mukashana ali ni mwana Betueli, uo Naho munyina kwa Abrahamu afyele muli Milika umukashi wakwe.

english: The young lady was very beautiful to look at, a virgin. No man had known her. She went down to the spring, filled her pitcher, and came up.
translation: Umukashana ali uwayemba nganshi kabili nacisungu, uushatala akuma ku mwaume. Rebeka atentemukila ku cishima, atapila amenshi mu mutondo elyo alabweluluka.

english: The servant ran to meet her, and said, “Please give me a drink, a little water from your pitcher.”
translation: Elyo umubomfi wakwa Abrahamu abutukilako amukumanya. Aeba Rebeka ati, “Napapata leka nwemo utumenshi mu mutondo obe.”

english: She said, “Drink, my lord.” She hurried, and let down her pitcher on her hand, and gave him a drink.
translation: Rebeka ati, “Aleni kanshi shikulu nabanwemo.” Awe bwangu bwangu aisha umutondo, amwikatila, no mubomfi anwamo.

english: When she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “I will also draw for your camels, until they have finished drinking.”
translation: Panuma ya kumupa amenshi yakunwa, Rebeka asosa ati, “Kanje ntapileko ingamila shenu nasho amenshi mpaka shipwe ukunwa.”

english: Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, who ruled over all that he had, “Please put your hand under my thigh.
translation: Ubushiku bumo Abrahamu aebele umukalamba wa babomfi bakwe, mushika wa fyuma fyakwe fyonse, ati, “Pisha iminwe yobe pesamba lye tanta lyandi.

english: She hurried, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again to the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.
translation: Bwangu bwangu aitulwila na menshi yali mu mutondo mu mulimba. Elyo abutukila nakabili ku cishima kukutapa amenshi. Atapafye ayengi ayakunwa ingamila shonse.

english: The man looked steadfastly at her, remaining silent, to know whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous or not.
translation: Umubomfi wena ninshi alifye tondolo alelolekesha umukashana pakuti amone nga cine cine Yawe amucitila ico aendele.

english: As the camels had done drinking, the man took a golden ring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold,
translation: Ilyo ingamila shapwa ukunwa amenshi, umubomfi elyo abuula imbalaminwe ya ku myona iya golide iya citika wa shekeli, afwika umukashana ku myona. Elyo amufwika na makosa yabili aya golide ku maboko aya mashekeli ikumi.

english: and said, “Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father’s house for us to stay?”
translation: Elyo aipusha umukashana ati, “Bushe niwe mwana ani? Napapata njebako. Bushe ku ŋanda kwa bawiso, kuti kwabako incende ukwakuti twaisa sendamako ubushiku bwa lelo?”

english: She said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.”
translation: Umukashana ayasuka ati, “Nine mwana Betueli uwafyelwe kuli Naho muli Milika.”

english: She said moreover to him, “We have both straw and feed enough, and room to lodge in.”
translation: Kabili umukashana alundapo nokuti, “Natukwata ifyakuti ingamila shalya ne cani cakuti shalalapo. Elyo natukwata ne ncende ukwakuti na imwe mwalala ubushiku bwa lelo.”

english: The man bowed his head, and worshiped the LORD.
translation: Elyo umubomfi akontamina panshi alapepa Yawe.

english: He said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his loving kindness and his truth toward my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the way to the house of my master’s relatives.”
translation: Asosa ati, “Napaalwe na matotelo Yawe, Lesa wakwa shikulu wandi Abrahamu, uushileka kulanga uluse ne cishinka cakwe kuli shikulu wandi. Kabili na ine wine ni Yawe euntungulwile muli ubu bulendo bwa kwisa ku ŋanda yakwa munyina kwa shikulu wandi.”

english: The young lady ran, and told her mother’s house about these words.
translation: Umukashana elyo abutwike ulubilo aya shimikila nyina na ba mu ŋanda ifyacitike.

english: Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.
translation: Nomba Rebeka alikwete ndume yakwe ishina lyakwe ni Labani. Elyo Labani afuma bwangu bwangu mukukumanya ulya muntu ku cishima.

english: I will make you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that you shall not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I live.
translation: Ndefwaya ulape kuli Yawe, Lesa wa mulu na pano isonde ukuti tawakafwaile umwana wandi Isaki umwanakashi wakuupa pa bakashana ba muno calo ndeikalamo, abena Kenani.

english: When he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, “This is what the man said to me,” he came to the man. Behold, he was standing by the camels at the spring.
translation: Ilyofye Labani amwene ukuti Rebeka ali ne mbalaminwe ya mu myona, nafwala na makosa ku maboko, aumfwa na Rebeka ifyo ashimika ifintu umuntu amwebele, ilyo ayako, asanga umubomfi eminine ne ngamila shakwe mupepi ne cishima.

english: He said, “Come in, you blessed of the LORD. Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.”
translation: Amweba ati, “Natuleya ku ŋanda, imwe mwe bapaalwa na Yawe. Nga cinshi ico mwiminine kuno kunse? Nimpekanya iŋanda ne ncende ya ngamila.”

english: The man came into the house, and he unloaded the camels. He gave straw and feed for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
translation: Kanshi umubomfi wakwa Abrahamu epakuya ku ŋanda. Labani ena akakula ifipe pa ngamila, ashanshila ifyani, ashipeela ne fyakulya. Elyo aleta amenshi pakuti umubomfi wakwa Abrahamu na bantu ali nabo basambe ku makasa.

english: Food was set before him to eat, but he said, “I will not eat until I have told my message.” Laban said, “Speak on.”
translation: Elyo baleta icakulya, lelo umubomfi wakwa Abrahamu asosa ati, “Ine nshalye mpaka ntale nande umulandu nyendele.” Labani ati, “Kanshi nabalande.”

english: He said, “I am Abraham’s servant.
translation: Nao asosa ati, “Ine ndi mubomfi wakwa Abrahamu.

english: The LORD has blessed my master greatly. He has become great. The LORD has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male servants and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
translation: Yawe alipaala shikulu apakalamba nganshi, amulenga nokuti abe umukankala wa fyuma. Alimupeela imikuni ya mpaanga, imbushi ne ŋombe, silifa na golide, ababomfi abaume na banakashi, ingamila na bapunda.

english: Sarah, my master’s wife, bore a son to my master when she was old. He has given all that he has to him.
translation: Kabili Sara muka shikulu Abrahamu, alimufyalila umwana umwaume mu bukote. Uyu mwana eo shikulu Abrahamu apeela ifyuma fyakwe fyonse.

english: My master made me swear, saying, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live,
translation: Kabili shikulu wandi alengele nokuti ndape umulapo. Anjebele ati, ‘Wikafwaila umwana wandi Isaki umwanakashi wakuupa pa bakashana abena Kenani aba muno calo ndeikalamo.

english: but you shall go to my father’s house, and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son.’
translation: Lelo uli nokuya ku ba mu ŋanda yakwa tata, ba lupwa lwandi, eko ukaye buulila umwana wandi Isaki umwanakashi wakuupa.’

english: I asked my master, ‘What if the woman will not follow me?’
translation: Elyo ine naipwishe shikulu wandi nati, ‘Bushe cikaba shani nga cakuti umwanakashi akaana ukwisa na ine kuno?’

english: But you shall go to my country, and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son Isaac.”
translation: Lelo uli nokuya ku calo candi uko natula na kuli ba lupwa lwandi, eko ukaye buulila umwana wandi Isaki umwanakashi wakuupa.”

english: He said to me, ‘The LORD, before whom I walk, will send his angel with you, and prosper your way. You shall take a wife for my son from my relatives, and of my father’s house.
translation: Nao shikulu anjaswike ati, ‘Yawe uwaishiba ifyo ine nyenda pa cinso cakwe, akakutumina malaika wakwe uwakuba nobe, pakuti akakucitile ico ukendela. Epakuti ukasange umwanakashi ukufuma kuli ba lupwa bakwa tata, ba lupwa lwandi, uwakuti umwana wandi akese upa.

english: Then you will be clear from my oath, when you come to my relatives. If they don’t give her to you, you shall be clear from my oath.’
translation: Lelo nga waya kuli ba lupwa lwandi ninshi umulapo wapwa, nangu abene nga ebakaana ukuti umulete ninshi nalyo line umulapo wapwa.’

english: I came today to the spring, and said, ‘The LORD, the God of my master Abraham, if now you do prosper my way which I go—
translation: “Ilyo nacifika ilelo pa cishima, nacisosa nati, ‘We Yawe, Lesa wakwa shikulu Abrahamu, shi wingancitila ico nyendele pali luno lwendo.

english: behold, I am standing by this spring of water. Let it happen, that the maiden who comes out to draw, to whom I will say, “Please give me a little water from your pitcher to drink,”
translation: Mona, njiminine mupepi ne cishima ca menshi, nga cakuti umukashana umo aisa kukutapa amenshi, na ine mwebe nati napapata leka nweko amenshi mu mutondo obe,

english: then she tells me, “Drink, and I will also draw for your camels,”—let her be the woman whom the LORD has appointed for my master’s son.’
translation: nao nga aisa ayasuka ati nwamo, ne ngamila shobe nasho nalashitapilako amenshi, ninshi uyo mukashana abe eo Yawe asalila umwana wakwa shikulu wandi.’

english: Before I had finished speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came out with her pitcher on her shoulder. She went down to the spring, and drew. I said to her, ‘Please let me drink.’
translation: Ilyo nshilapwa ukupepa mu mutima wandi, Rebeka aisa, nasenda no mutondo pa kubeya kwakwe. Atentemukila pa cishima, atapa na menshi. Na ine namweba nati, ‘Napapata mpeelako amenshi nwe.’

english: She hurried and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink.’ So I drank, and she also gave the camels a drink.
translation: Bwangu bwangu aisha umutondo pa kubeya ati nokuti, ‘Nweni, nalaya tapila ne ngamila shenu amenshi shinwe.’ Nanwa, elyo apeela ingamila amenshi shanwa.

english: I asked her, and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bore to him.’ I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her hands.
translation: Elyo namwipusha nati, ‘Bushe niwe mwana ani?’ Nao ayasuka ati, ‘Nine mwana Betueli umwana mwaume wakwa Naho uo Milika afyele kuli ena.’ Elyo namufwika imbalaminwe ya ku myona na makosa ku maboko yakwe.

english: I bowed my head, and worshiped the LORD, and blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the right way to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.
translation: Elyo nakontamina panshi nalapepa Yawe. Nalumbanya Yawe, Lesa wakwa shikulu wandi Abrahamu, uuntungulwile mu nshila iyalungama kukwisa buulila umwishikulu wakwa munyina shikulu wandi ukuti abe umukashi wa mwana wakwe.

english: Now if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me. If not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.”
translation: Kanshi nomba nga mulelanga icitemwiko no bufumacumi kuli shikulu wandi, njebeni, elyo nga teifyo naco cine njebeni epakuti njishibe ifyakucita.”

english: The servant said to him, “What if the woman isn’t willing to follow me to this land? Must I bring your son again to the land you came from?”
translation: Umubomfi nao amwipusha ati, “Nga kanshi cikaba shani nga cakuti umwanakashi talefwaya ukwisa na ine kuli cino calo? Bushe ninshi nkaba nokubweseshamo mwano ku calo uko wafumine?”

english: Then Laban and Bethuel answered, “The thing proceeds from the LORD. We can’t speak to you bad or good.
translation: Labani na Betueli bamwasuka abati, “Ici cintu ni kuli Yawe cafuma, kanshi ifwe tekuti tukwate icakulandapo.

english: Behold, Rebekah is before you. Take her, and go, and let her be your master’s son’s wife, as the LORD has spoken.”
translation: Rebeka uyu, mubuule, umusende, uleke akaye ba umukashi wa mwana wakwa sokulu, ngefyo Yawe alandile.”

english: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed himself down to the earth to the LORD.
translation: Cilya umubomfi wakwa Abrahamu aumfwa ifyo balanda, akontamina panshi alapepa Yawe.

english: The servant brought out jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious things to her brother and her mother.
translation: Elyo umubomfi wakwa Abrahamu abuula ifisamo ifyakuiyemfya ifya golide na silifa ne fyakufwala apeela Rebeka. Kabili apeelako ndume yakwa Rebeka na nyina ifyabupe ifyamutengo nganshi.

english: They ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and stayed all night. They rose up in the morning, and he said, “Send me away to my master.”
translation: Elyo umubomfi wakwa Abrahamu pamo na bantu ali nabo balalya no kunwa, no kusendama basendama uko kwine. Ilyo babuka ulucelo, umubomfi wakwa Abrahamu abeba ati, “Lekeni mbwelelemo kuli shikulu.”

english: Her brother and her mother said, “Let the young lady stay with us a few days, at least ten. After that she will go.”
translation: Lelo ndume yakwa Rebeka na nyina basosa abati, “Lekeni umukashana ekaleko inshiku ikumi limo nangu ukucilapo, elyo ninshi akaleya.”

english: He said to them, “Don’t hinder me, since the LORD has prospered my way. Send me away that I may go to my master.”
translation: Umubomfi nao asosa ati, “Mwileka nkokole kuno, apo Yawe nafikilisha ico naendele, lekenifye ndeya kuli shikulu.”

english: They said, “We will call the young lady, and ask her.”
translation: Elyo basosa abati, “Kanshi katwite umukashana, tumfwe ifyo alaisa sosa.”

english: They called Rebekah, and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” She said, “I will go.”
translation: Elyo baita Rebeka, bamwipusha abati, “Bushe bati uleya noyu muntu?” Nao ayasuka ati, “Ee ndeya.”

english: They sent away Rebekah, their sister, with her nurse, Abraham’s servant, and his men.
translation: Kanshi epakuleka nkashi yabo Rebeka no muleshi wakwe ukuti baleya no mubomfi wakwa Abrahamu na bantu bakwe.

english: Abraham said to him, “Beware that you don’t bring my son there again.
translation: Abrahamu amwasuka ati, “Tecakwesha ukubwesesha umwana wandi kuli cilya calo!

english: They blessed Rebekah, and said to her, “Our sister, may you be the mother of thousands of ten thousands, and let your offspring possess the gate of those who hate them.”
translation: Elyo bapaala Rebeka no kumweba abati,

english: Rebekah arose with her ladies. They rode on the camels, and followed the man. The servant took Rebekah, and went his way.
translation: Elyo Rebeka na bakashana balemubombela baima, banina pa ngamila bakonka no mubomfi wakwa Abrahamu. Kanshi efyo umubomfi asendele Rebeka no kuya aya.

english: Isaac came from the way of Beer Lahai Roi, for he lived in the land of the South.
translation: Mu nshita iyo, Isaki ninshi alifuma ku cishima ca Bere Lai Roi, aleikala mu matololo ya Negebu.

english: Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the evening. He lifted up his eyes and looked. Behold, there were camels coming.
translation: Ubushiku bumo cilya akasuba kalasumbila kukuwa, Isaki aya aletandala mwibala. Elyo ati enune amenso, amona ingamila shileisa.

english: Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she got off the camel.
translation: Rebeka nao ati enune amenso amona Isaki, elyo aika pa ngamila

english: She said to the servant, “Who is the man who is walking in the field to meet us?” The servant said, “It is my master.” She took her veil, and covered herself.
translation: aipusha umubomfi wakwa Abrahamu ati, “Bushe ulya muntu aleisa mwibala kukutukumanya nani?” Umubomfi amwasuka ati, “Ni shikulu wandi.” Elyo Rebeka abuula insalu afimba pa menso.

english: The servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.
translation: Umubomfi epakushimikila Isaki fyonse ifyo acitile.

english: Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife. He loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.
translation: Isaki epakwingisha Rebeka mwitenti lyakwa nyina Sarah, amubuula ukuba umukashi wakwe. Efyo Rebeka asangwike umukashi wakwe. Isaki alitemenwe Rebeka, no mutima wakwe watalala ukufuma apo nyina afwilile.

english: The LORD, the God of heaven—who took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my birth, who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying, ‘I will give this land to your offspring—he will send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
translation: Yawe, Lesa wa mu mulu uwamfumishe mu ŋanda ya batata na mu calo nafyalilwemo, uwalandile no kundaya no mulapo ati, ‘Cino calo nkacipeela ku ba mu lupwa lobe.’ Yawe akatangisha malaika wakwe ku ntanshi yobe epakuti kulya kwine eko ukaye buula umwanakashi uwakuti umwana wandi akoope.

english: If the woman isn’t willing to follow you, then you shall be clear from this oath to me. Only you shall not bring my son there again.”
translation: Lelo ngo mwanakashi talefwaya ukwisa nobe, lyena ninshi tapali mulandu wakusungila uyu umulapo. Lelo umwana wandi wena wikamubweseshamo kulya.”

english: The servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and swore to him concerning this matter.
translation: Kanshi umubomfi epakupisha iminwe yakwe pesamba lye tanta lyakwa shikulu wakwe Abrahamu, alapa no mulapo wakucita ifyo Abrahamu amwebele.

english: Abraham took another wife, and her name was Keturah.
translation: Abrahamu alyupile umwanakashi umbi, ishina lyakwe ni Ketura.

english: the field which Abraham purchased from the children of Heth. Abraham was buried there with Sarah, his wife.
translation: Iyi e mpanga Abrahamu ashitile ku bena Hiti. Kabili umu mwine emo Abrahamu no mukashi wakwe Sara bashiikilwe.

english: After the death of Abraham, God blessed Isaac, his son. Isaac lived by Beer Lahai Roi.
translation: Ilyo Abrahamu afwile, Lesa apaalile umwana wakwe Isaki. Isaki nao epakwikala ku Bere Lai Roi.

english: Now this is the history of the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s servant, bore to Abraham.
translation: Ubu e butantiko bwa lupwa lwakwa Ishimaeli umwana umwaume uo Abrahamu afyele muli Haga umwina Egupto, umusha mwanakashi wakwa Sara.

english: These are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to the order of their birth: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
translation: Aya e mashina ya bana abaume bakwa Ishimaeli umo bakonkanine ukufyalwa. Ibeli ni Nebaiyoti, elyo pakonka Keda, Adibeli, Mibisamu,

english: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
translation: Icite 16:14

english: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
translation: Hadadi, Tema, Yetu, Nafishi na Kedema.

english: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their villages, and by their encampments: twelve princes, according to their nations.
translation: Kanshi aba e bamwana Ishimaeli. Kabili aya e mashina ya bakateeka ba mikowa yabo ikumi limo na ibili (12) ayo bainikeko imishi yabo ne nkambi shabo.

english: These are the years of the life of Ishmael: one hundred thirty-seven years. He gave up his spirit and died, and was gathered to his people.
translation: Ishimaeli aikele umumi imyaka yonse pamo umwanda umo na makumi yatatu na cine lubali (137). Elyo aleka umweo no kufwa afwa, aya no kwalala ifikolwe fyakwe.

english: They lived from Havilah to Shur that is before Egypt, as you go toward Assyria. He lived opposite all his relatives.
translation: Aba mu lupwa lwakwa Ishimaeli baleikala mu calo ca pakati ukufuma ku Hafila ukufika na ku Shuri, mupepi no mupaka wa Egupto ukulola ku Asiria. Ishimaeli tabaleumfwana na bamunyina bonse.

english: This is the history of the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son. Abraham became the father of Isaac.
translation: Kanshi ubu e butantiko bwa lupwa lwakwa Isaki mwana Abrahamu. Wishi wakwa Isaki ni Abrahamu.

english: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
translation: Ketura afyele kuli Abrahamu abana aba, Simurani, Yokishani, Medani, Midiani, Ishibaki na Shua.

english: Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Paddan Aram, the sister of Laban the Syrian, to be his wife.
translation: Isaki ali ne myaka amakumi yane (40) ilyo aupile Rebeka. Wishi wakwa Rebeka ali ni Betueli umwina Aramu mu Padani Aramu. Ndume yakwa Rebeka ali ni Labani umwina Aramu.

english: Isaac entreated the LORD for his wife, because she was barren. The LORD was entreated by him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
translation: Isaki alepepelako umukashi wakwe kuli Yawe, pantu Rebeka ali ni ŋumba. Yawe alyumfwile ipepo lyakwe, na Rebeka umukashi wakwe epakuba pabukulu.

english: The children struggled together within her. She said, “If it is like this, why do I live?” She went to inquire of the LORD.
translation: Lelo ilyo abana bacili mwifumo balakusana. Elyo Rebeka asosa ati, “Nga cinshi calancitikila ifi?” Kanshi Rebeka epakuya kukumfwa ifyo Yawe alesosapo.

english: The LORD said to her, “Two nations are in your womb. Two peoples will be separated from your body. The one people will be stronger than the other people. The elder will serve the younger.”
translation: Yawe nao amweba ati,

english: When her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
translation: Ilyo inshita yafikile iyakupaapa, mwifumo lyakwa Rebeka mwali bampundu abaume beka beka.

english: The first came out red all over, like a hairy garment. They named him Esau.
translation: Uwabalilepo ukufyalwa, ali uwakashika na mapipi umubili onse kwati ni nsalu ya mafufu. Kanshi epakumwinika ishina lya Esau.

english: After that, his brother came out, and his hand had hold on Esau’s heel. He was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.
translation: Panuma munyina nao afyalwa, ekete ku citende cakwa Esau. Kanshi nao bamwinika ishina lya Yakobo. Isaki ali ne myaka amakumi mutanda (60) ilyo Rebeka afyele aba bampundu.

english: The boys grew. Esau was a skillful hunter, a man of the field. Jacob was a quiet man, living in tents.
translation: Ilyo aba bana bakulile, Esau aishile ba umubamfi uwine wine uwa nama, umuntu uwakusabantafye mu mpanga. Yakobo wena ali umuntu uwapetama, atemenwe ukwikala pa mushi.

english: Now Isaac loved Esau, because he ate his venison. Rebekah loved Jacob.
translation: Isaki, uwalefwaya inama sha mpanga atemenwe Esau. Lelo Rebeka atemenwe Yakobo.

english: Jacob boiled stew. Esau came in from the field, and he was famished.
translation: Ubushiku bumo Yakobo aleipika ifyakulya, Esau nao afuma mu mpanga ali ne nsala nganshi.

english: Jokshan became the father of Sheba, and Dedan. The sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
translation: Yokishani afyele Sheba na Dedani. Abena Ashurimu, abena Letushi na bena Leumimu bonse ba mu lupwa lwakwa Dedani.

english: Esau said to Jacob, “Please feed me with some of that red stew, for I am famished.” Therefore his name was called Edom.
translation: Esau aebele Yakobo ati, “Endesha, mpeelako ndye ifyo fyakulya ifyakashika, pantu insala yansuma nganshi.” (Eico Esau bamwinikile ne shina lya Edomu .)

english: Jacob said, “First, sell me your birthright.”
translation: Yakobo amwasuka ati, “Pakubala nshitisha insambu sha bubeli bobe.”

english: Esau said, “Behold, I am about to die. What good is the birthright to me?”
translation: Esau amweba ati, “Mona ine ndi pakufwa, nga kanshi insambu sha bubeli shikamombela nshi?”

english: Jacob said, “Swear to me first.” He swore to him. He sold his birthright to Jacob.
translation: Yakobo amweba ati, “Pakubala lapa kuli ine.” Esau alapa na kuli Yakobo, ashitisha ne nsambu sha bubeli bwakwe kuli Yakobo.

english: Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew. He ate and drank, rose up, and went his way. So Esau despised his birthright.
translation: Elyo Yakobo amupeelako umukate no muto we landa. Esau alya umukate anwa no muto we landa, elyo aima alaya noko aleya.

english: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
translation: Abana bakwa Midiani bena ni Efah, Eferi, Hanoki, Abida na Eluda. Aba bonse ba mu lupwa lwakwa Ketura.

english: Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac,
translation: Abrahamu apeele ifyuma fyonse fintu akwete kuli Isaki.

english: but Abraham gave gifts to the sons of Abraham’s concubines. While he still lived, he sent them away from Isaac his son, eastward, to the east country.
translation: Lelo ilyo acili umumi, Abrahamu apeele ifyabupe ku bana abaume aba mu bakashi bakwe abashaupilwe mu bwinga no kubatuma ukuya ikala mu calo ca ku kabanga pakuti bataluke ku mwana wakwe Isaki.

english: These are the days of the years of Abraham’s life which he lived: one hundred seventy-five years.
translation: Abrahamu aikele umumi pano calo imyaka yonse pamo umwanda umo na makumi cine lubali na isano (175).

english: Abraham gave up his spirit, and died at a good old age, an old man, and full of years, and was gathered to his people.
translation: Abrahamu asukile aleka umweo. Afwa mu bukote bufwaikwa, umukote uwa myaka iyingi. Epakuya lala ku fikolwe fyakwe.

english: Isaac and Ishmael, his sons, buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron, the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is near Mamre,
translation: Abana bakwe abaume Isaki na Ishimaeli bamushiikile mu lucengo lwa Makipela, mu mpanga yakwa Efuloni mwana Sowa umwina Hiti, lwa ku kabanga ka Mamure.

english: There was a famine in the land, in addition to the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
translation: Kanshi mu calo mwaliponene icipowe na cimbi nga cilya caponene kale mu nshita yakwa Abrahamu. Isaki epakuya ku Gerari kuli Abimeleki imfumu ya Bafilisiti.

english: Abimelech said, “What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt on us!”
translation: Elyo Abimeleki asosa ati, “Cinshi ico wacitila ici kuli ifwe? Umwaume nga cakuti aile sendama no mukashi obe, ninshi nga niwe watuletele umulandu.”

english: Abimelech commanded all the people, saying, “He who touches this man or his wife will surely be put to death.”
translation: Kanshi Abimeleki epakupeela icipope ku bantu bonse ati, “Umuntu onse uukacusha uyu muntu nangu umukashi wakwe akepaiwa.”

english: Isaac sowed in that land, and reaped in the same year one hundred times what he planted. The LORD blessed him.
translation: Isaki alibyelemo imbuto muli cilya calo. Kabili muli uyo wine mwaka asombwelemo imbuto ishingi, imiku umwanda umo pafyo abyele. Yawe alipaalile Isaki,

english: The man grew great, and grew more and more until he became very great.
translation: Icite 12:13

english: He had possessions of flocks, possessions of herds, and a great household. The Philistines envied him.
translation: Akwata imikuni iyingi iya mpaanga ne mbushi ne ya ŋombe na babomfi abengi, icakuti Abafilisiti bamufimbila.

english: Now all the wells which his father’s servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped, and filled with earth.
translation: Kanshi Abafilisiti baisushamo iloba mu fishima ababomfi bakwa wishi baimbile ninshi Abrahamu wishi acili umumi.

english: Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go away from us, for you are much mightier than we.”
Isaac departed from there, encamped in the valley of Gerar, and lived there.
translation: Kanshi Isaki epakufumako aya cita inkambi mwishika lya ku Gerari, eko no kwikala aikala.

english: Isaac dug again the wells of water, which they had dug in the days of Abraham his father, for the Philistines had stopped them after the death of Abraham. He called their names after the names by which his father had called them.
translation: Isaki afukula ifishima ifyaimbilwe ninshi Abrahamu wishi epo acili, ifyo Abafilisiti bashiikile panuma ya mfwa yakwa Abrahamu. Isaki afinika na mashina ayo yene wishi afinike.

english: Isaac’s servants dug in the valley, and found there a well of flowing water.
translation: Kabili ababomfi bakwa Isaki balimbile icishima mwishika, basangamo na kamfukumfuku ka menshi.

english: The LORD appeared to him, and said, “Don’t go down into Egypt. Live in the land I will tell you about.
translation: Elyo Yawe amonekela kuli Isaki, amweba ati, “Wikaya ku Egupto, ukekale mu calo ndekweba ukwikalamo.

english: The herdsmen of Gerar argued with Isaac’s herdsmen, saying, “The water is ours.” So he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.
translation: Lelo bakacema ba mu Gerari balaumanya bakacema bakwa Isaki, balabeba abati, “Aya menshi yesu.” Kanshi Isaki epakwinika icishima ishina lya Eseki, pantu abena Gerari balepusaninapo nankwe.

english: They dug another well, and they argued over that, also. So he called its name Sitnah.
translation: Kabili ababomfi bakwa Isaki baimba icishima cimbi, lelo naco cine balaumaninapo. Kanshi Isaki epakucinika ishina lya Sitina.

english: He left that place, and dug another well. They didn’t argue over that one. So he called it Rehoboth. He said, “For now the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.”
translation: Kanshi epakufumako kulya, aya imba icishima cimbi. Pali ici cena tapali nelyo umo uwalemumanya, acinika ne shina lya Rehoboti, asosa ati, “Nomba Yawe natupeela incende iyifungulwike, kanshi tukasanduluka muli ici calo.”

english: He went up from there to Beersheba.
translation: Ukufuma uko, Isaki aile ku Beresheba.

english: The LORD appeared to him the same night, and said, “I am the God of Abraham your father. Don’t be afraid, for I am with you, and will bless you, and multiply your offspring for my servant Abraham’s sake.”
translation: Ubo bwine bushiku, mu nshita ya bushiku, Yawe amumonekela, amweba ati,

english: He built an altar there, and called on the LORD’s name, and pitched his tent there. There Isaac’s servants dug a well.
translation: Isaki epakukuulako ubulambo, elyo alapepa Yawe. Uku kwine acitile inkambi yakwe, na babomfi bakwe baimbako icishima.

english: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath his friend, and Phicol the captain of his army.
translation: Kanshi Abimeleki na Ahusati uwalemupandako amano, elyo na Fikoli umukalamba wa fita fyakwe, afumine ku Gerari aisa kuli Isaki.

english: Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me, since you hate me, and have sent me away from you?”
translation: Isaki abepusha ati, “Cinshi mwaishila kuli ine apo mwalimpata, kabili mwalintamfya na kumwenu?”

english: They said, “We saw plainly that the LORD was with you. We said, ‘Let there now be an oath between us, even between us and you, and let’s make a covenant with you,
translation: Bamwasuka abati, “Natumonafye bwino bwino ukuti Yawe aba na iwe. Kanshi twatile, ‘Pafwile ukuba umulapo wakusuminishanya pakati kesu,’ pakati kesu na iwe. Kanshi leka tupangane na iwe

english: that you will do us no harm, as we have not touched you, and as we have done to you nothing but good, and have sent you away in peace.’ You are now the blessed of the LORD.”
translation: ukuti tawakatucite nelyo cimo icabipa, nga filya ifwe tatwacitile nelyo cimo icakukucusha. Lelo ifwe twalekusungafye bwino no kuleka ukuti ufume kumwesu umutende. Nomba Yawe nakupaala.”

english: Live in this land, and I will be with you, and will bless you. For I will give to you, and to your offspring, all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I swore to Abraham your father.
translation: Pa nshita ino ikala muli cino cine calo ngo mweni, kabili nakulaba nobe, no kupaala nkakupaala. Kabili ni kuli iwe na ba mu lupwa lobe eko nkapeela ifi fyalo fyonse, efyo nkafikilisha umulapo nalapile kuli wiso Abrahamu.

english: He made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
translation: Isaki elyo abapekanishisha imitebeto, balya no kunwa banwa.

english: They rose up some time in the morning, and swore an oath to one another. Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.
translation: Ubushiku bwakonkelepo ulucelocelo, cila muntu alapa umulapo ku mubiye. Isaki epakubaleka baya, nabo bafumako umutende.

english: The same day, Isaac’s servants came, and told him concerning the well which they had dug, and said to him, “We have found water.”
translation: Pali ubo bwine bushiku ababomfi bakwa Isaki baishile mushimikila pa cishima baimbile. Bamweba abati, “Natusanga amenshi.”

english: He called it “Shibah”. Therefore the name of the city is “Beersheba” to this day.
translation: Isaki acinika ishina lya Shiba. Eico ukufika na lelo umusumba witwa Beresheba.

english: When Esau was forty years old, he took as wife Judith, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
translation: Ilyo Esau afikile pa myaka amakumi yane (40), aupile Yuditi mwana Beri umwina Hiti, elyo na Basemati mwana Eloni, nao umwina Hiti.

english: They grieved Isaac’s and Rebekah’s spirits.
translation: Aba banakashi baleleta isakamika kuli Isaki na Rebeka.

english: I will multiply your offspring as the stars of the sky, and will give all these lands to your offspring. In your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed,
translation: Nkasandulula aba mu lupwa lobe nge ntanda sha mu mulu, kabili ebo nkapeela ifi fyalo fyonse. Elyo imishobo yonse pano calo ikapaalilwa mu ba mu lupwa lobe,

english: because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my requirements, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.”
translation: pantu Abrahamu alembeela kabili alebaka ifyo mfwaya, amafunde yandi, ifipope fyandi elyo ne fyebo fyandi.”

english: Isaac lived in Gerar.
translation: Kanshi Isaki epakwikala mu Gerari.

english: The men of the place asked him about his wife. He said, “She is my sister,” for he was afraid to say, “My wife”, lest, he thought, “the men of the place might kill me for Rebekah, because she is beautiful to look at.”
translation: Nomba ilyo abantu ba kuli ilya ncende bamwipwishe pa mukashi wakwe, Isaki abebele ati, “Ni nkashi yandi.” Asosele ukuti ni nkashi yandi ico aletiina ukulanda ati “Mukashi wandi.” Atontonkenye ukuti, “Abantu ba ino ncende kuti banjipaya pa mulandu wakwa Rebeka pantu aba uwayemba.”

english: When he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was caressing Rebekah, his wife.
translation: Cilya aikalako inshiku ishingi, ubushiku bumo Abimeleki imfumu ya Bafilisiti yalolesha pa nsolokoto, yamona Isaki alecenya umukashi wakwe Rebeka.

english: Abimelech called Isaac, and said, “Behold, surely she is your wife. Why did you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac said to him, “Because I said, ‘Lest I die because of her.’”
translation: Kanshi Abimeleki epakwita Isaki, amweba ati, “Rebeka cine cine mukashi obe. Nga cinshi wasosele auti, ‘Rebeka ni nkashi yandi?’” Isaki amwasuka ati, “Pantu natontonkenye ukuti nalimo kuti banjipaila pa mulandu wakwa Rebeka.”

english: When Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his elder son, and said to him, “My son?” He said to him, “Here I am.”
translation: Ilyo Isaki akotele, na menso yakwe yanakuka icakuti alafilwa no kumona, aitile umwana mwaume mukalamba Esau, amweba ati, “We mwana wandi!” Nao mwane ayasuka ati, “Epo ndi.”

english: You shall bring it to your father, that he may eat, so that he may bless you before his death.”
translation: Elyo wise utwalile bawiso balye pakuti bakupaale ilyo bashilafwa.”

english: Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
translation: Lelo Yakobo aebele nyina Rebeka ati, “Munyinane Esau muntu uwamapipi, lelo ine ndi muntu wa mubili uwatelela.

english: What if my father touches me? I will seem to him as a deceiver, and I would bring a curse on myself, and not a blessing.”
translation: Nga cakuti batata baya mpampanta, cileya moneka kwati ndebomfya ubucenjeshi. Lyena ninshi te paalo ndeya poka, lelo kuiletelelafye ukulapishiwa.”

english: His mother said to him, “Let your curse be on me, my son. Only obey my voice, and go get them for me.”
translation: Nyina amweba ati, “We mwana wandi, leka uko kulapishiwa kukese pali ine. Iwe citafye ifyo nandile. Kabiye, kandetele utwana twa mbushi.”

english: He went, and got them, and brought them to his mother. His mother made savory food, such as his father loved.
translation: Kanshi Yakobo epakuya buula utwana twa mbushi, atuleta kuli nyina. Nyina nao epakupekanya icakulya icanunkila mu musango wishi atemenwe.

english: Rebekah took the good clothes of Esau, her elder son, which were with her in the house, and put them on Jacob, her younger son.
translation: Elyo Rebeka abuula ifyakufwala ifyawamishe ifyali mu ŋanda ifya mwana mukalamba Esau, afwika no mwana wakwe mwaice Yakobo.

english: She put the skins of the young goats on his hands, and on the smooth of his neck.
translation: Elyo apomba impapa sha twana twa mbushi ku maboko yakwa Yakobo na mu mukoshi umushali mapipi.

english: She gave the savory food and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.
translation: Apeela mwane Yakobo mu minwe icakulya icanunkila no mukate apangile.

english: He came to his father, and said, “My father?” He said, “Here I am. Who are you, my son?”
translation: Yakobo aya kuli wishi, asosa ati, “Tata wandi!” Wishi nao ayasuka ati, “Epo ndi. Niwe ani we mwana wandi?”

english: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau your firstborn. I have done what you asked me to do. Please arise, sit and eat of my venison, that your soul may bless me.”
translation: Yakobo ayasuka wishi ati, “Nine Esau ibeli lyenu. Nincita ifyo mwacinjeba. Aleni imeni mulyeko inama yandi, pakuti mumpeele ipaalo lyenu.”

english: He said, “See now, I am old. I don’t know the day of my death.
translation: Isaki amweba ati, “Mona, nomba ninkota, kabili nshishibe no bushiku ningafwa.

english: Isaac said to his son, “How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?” He said, “Because the LORD your God gave me success.”
translation: Isaki aipusha mwane ati, “We mwana wandi, apa pene epo wasanga inama?” Yakobo ayasuka ati, “Ni Yawe, Lesa wenu uwampeela ishuko.”

english: Isaac said to Jacob, “Please come near, that I may feel you, my son, whether you are really my son Esau or not.”
translation: Elyo Isaki aebele Yakobo ati, “Palama kuno mwana wandi uleke nkupampante, pakuti njishibe nga cine niwe mwana wandi Esau nangu iyoo.”

english: Jacob went near to Isaac his father. He felt him, and said, “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”
translation: Yakobo epakupalama kuli wishi Isaki. Wishi nao alamupampanta elyo asosa ati, “Ishiwi lyena lishiwi lyakwa Yakobo, lelo amaboko yena maboko yakwa Esau.”

english: He didn’t recognize him, because his hands were hairy, like his brother Esau’s hands. So he blessed him.
translation: Isaki taishibe ukuti ni Yakobo pantu amaboko yakwe yali na mapipi kwati yakwa Esau munyina. Kanshi Isaki epakupaala Yakobo.

english: He said, “Are you really my son Esau?” He said, “I am.”
translation: Lelo Isaki amwipusha ati, “Bushe cine cine niwe mwana wandi Esau?” Yakobo ayasuka ati, “Ee nine wine.”

english: He said, “Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son’s venison, that my soul may bless you.” He brought it near to him, and he ate. He brought him wine, and he drank.
translation: Elyo Isaki asosa ati, “Mwana wandi, ndetelako inama wipeye mukulunga, uleke ndye, pakuti nkupaale.” Yakobo epakumuletela inama no kulya alya. Amuletelako no mwangashi, nao anwa.

english: His father Isaac said to him, “Come near now, and kiss me, my son.”
translation: Elyo Isaki wishi amweba ati, “Palama kuno mwana wandi untomone pakumposha.”

english: He came near, and kissed him. He smelled the smell of his clothing, and blessed him, and said, “Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the LORD has blessed.
translation: Kanshi Yakobo epakuya tomona Isaki pakumuposha. Cilya Isaki aumfwa icena ca nsalu shakwe, alamupaala, no kusosa ati,

english: God give you of the dew of the sky, of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of grain and new wine.
translation: Lesa engakupeela umume wa ku mulu,

english: Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers. Let your mother’s sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone who curses you. Blessed be everyone who blesses you.”
translation: Imishobo ingalakutumika

english: Now therefore, please take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field, and get me venison.
translation: Kanshi nomba buula ifyanso fyobe, imifwi yobe no buta bobe, uye mu mpanga mukulunga, unjipaileko inama.

english: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had just gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
translation: Atilefye cilya Isaki apwa ukupaala Yakobo, na Yakobo afuma pali wishi, Esau munyina nao abwela kukulunga.

english: He also made savory food, and brought it to his father. He said to his father, “Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s venison, that your soul may bless me.”
translation: Esau nao apekanya icakulya icanunkila, atwala na kuli wishi. Elyo aeba wishi ati, “Tata wandi, imeni mulyeko inama njipeye kukulunga pakuti mumpeele ne paalo lyenu.”

english: Isaac his father said to him, “Who are you?” He said, “I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.”
translation: Isaki wishi amwipusha ati, “Bushe niwe ani?” Nao ayasuka ati, “Nine mwana wenu, ibeli lyenu Esau.”

english: Isaac trembled violently, and said, “Who, then, is he who has taken venison, and brought it to me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him? Yes, he will be blessed.”
translation: Isaki epakulakanka no mwenso ukalamba ati, “Nga kanshi uwacibamba inama no kundetela nani? Nalyafye ili line ninshi taulaisa elyo nimupaala, kabili nalala napaalwa.”

english: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father, “Bless me, even me also, my father.”
translation: Cilya Esau aumfwa ifyo wishi alanda, alila umusowa uukalamba kabili uukali, alaeba wishi ati, “Mpaaleni, na ine, tata wandi!”

english: He said, “Your brother came with deceit, and has taken away your blessing.”
translation: Lelo Isaki amweba ati, “Munonko acisa mu bucenjeshi, napoka ne paalo lyobe.”

english: He said, “Isn’t he rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times. He took away my birthright. See, now he has taken away my blessing.” He said, “Haven’t you reserved a blessing for me?”
translation: Esau epakusosa ati, “Bushe tacalungama ukumwinika ishina lya Yakobo? Nomba ancenjesha imiku ibili. Alimpokele insambu sha bubeli bwandi. Kabili apoka ne paalo.” Elyo aipusha ati, “Bushe tamunshilileko ipaalo?”

english: Isaac answered Esau, “Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given to him for servants. I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What then will I do for you, my son?”
translation: Isaki ayasuka Esau ati, “Mona nimusonta ukuba imfumu yobe, kabili nimupeela ba lupwa lwakwe bonse ukuba ababomfi bakwe. Elyo nimupeela ifyakumusunga, ifisabo elyo no mwangashi upya. Kanshi finshi fimbi ningakucitila mwana wandi?”

english: Esau said to his father, “Do you have just one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, my father.” Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.
translation: Esau aebele wishi ati, “Bushe tata mwakwatafye ipaalo limo epela? Tata wandi mpaaleniko na ine wine!” Elyo Esau asansula ishiwi lyakwe alalila.

english: Isaac his father answered him, “Behold, your dwelling will be of the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of the sky from above.
translation: Isaki wishi epakwasuka mwane ati,

english: Make me savory food, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat, and that my soul may bless you before I die.”
translation: Elyo wise umpekanishisheko icakulya icanunkila, cilya natemwa, ulete njise ndye. Epakuti nkupaale ilyo nshilafwa.”

english: You will live by your sword, and you will serve your brother. It will happen, when you will break loose, that you will shake his yoke from off your neck.”
translation: Ni ku lupanga eko ukamwena ukwikala umumi.

english: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father blessed him. Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand. Then I will kill my brother Jacob.”
translation: Kanshi Esau nomba alipatile Yakobo, pa mulandu we paalo wishi amupeele. Alaisosha umwine ati, “Inshiku shakuloosha batata shilifye mupepi. Elyo ninshi nkepaya munyinane Yakobo.”

english: The words of Esau, her elder son, were told to Rebekah. She sent and called Jacob, her younger son, and said to him, “Behold, your brother Esau comforts himself about you by planning to kill you.
translation: Ilyo Rebeka bamwebeleko ifyo umwana mukalamba Esau alandile, Rebeka epakutuma abakwita Yakobo umwana mwaice. Amweba ati, “Mona munonko Esau aleitalalika umutima ne pange lya kukwipaya.

english: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice. Arise, flee to Laban, my brother, in Haran.
translation: Kanshi nomba we mwana wandi, cita ifyo nalakweba, fulumukila kuli ndume yandi Labani ku Harani.

english: Stay with him a few days, until your brother’s fury turns away—
translation: Uye ikala nankwe pa nshita ino mpaka munonko icipyu cikapwe.

english: until your brother’s anger turns away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send, and get you from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?”
translation: Ilyo munonko akaleka ukukufulilwa kabili akalabe nefyo wamucita, elyo nkakutumina amashiwi ukabwelulukeko. Nga cinshi ningalekela ukuti ndufye abana bandi bonse babili mu bushiku bumo bwine?”

english: Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these, of the daughters of the land, what good will my life do me?”
translation: Kabili Rebeka aebele Isaki ati, “Ine nintendwa ukuba umumi pa mulandu wa aba banakashi abena Hiti. Nga cakuti Yakobo nao aupa umwanakashi umo pa banakashi ba muli cino calo pali aba abena Hiti, ine ninshi no kufwa kwawama.”

english: Rebekah heard when Isaac spoke to Esau his son. Esau went to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.
translation: Kanshi Rebeka aleumfwako ilyo Isaki alelanda kuli mwane Esau. Ilyo aile mu mpanga mukulunga inama nokuti alete,

english: Rebekah spoke to Jacob her son, saying, “Behold, I heard your father speak to Esau your brother, saying,
translation: Rebeka aeba mwane Yakobo ati, “Mona, naumfwako ifyo bawiso bacilaeba munonko Esau, baleti,

english: ‘Bring me venison, and make me savory food, that I may eat, and bless you before the LORD before my death.’
translation: ‘Undetele inama elyo umpekanishishe icakulya icanunkila icakuti ndye, uleke nkupaale pa cinso cakwa Yawe ilyo nshilafwa.’

english: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command you.
translation: Kanshi we mwana wandi, umfwa bwino kuli ine, ucite nefyo ndekweba.

english: Go now to the flock and get me two good young goats from there. I will make them savory food for your father, such as he loves.
translation: Kabiye ku mukuni wa mbushi, undeteleko utwana twa mbushi tubili utusuma pakuti njise mpekanishishe bawiso icakulya icanunkila umusango bacitemenwamo.

english: Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and commanded him, “You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
translation: Kanshi Isaki aitile Yakobo no kumupaala, amukonkomesha ati, “Iwe wikopa umwanakashi umwina Kenani.

english: Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.
translation: Yakobo afumine ku Beresheba, alungama ku Harani.

english: He came to a certain place, and stayed there all night, because the sun had set. He took one of the stones of the place, and put it under his head, and lay down in that place to sleep.
translation: Ilyo afikile pa ncende imo, ico akasuba kawa, epo asendama ubo bushiku. Abuulapo ilibwe limo epo asaila, alala nokulala.

english: He dreamed and saw a stairway set upon the earth, and its top reached to heaven. Behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.
translation: Alota iciloto umo amwene umutanto ushimpile panshi, kabili ufikile na mu mulu. Elyo bamalaika bakwa Lesa balenina no kwika pa mutanto.

english: Behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, “I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. I will give the land you lie on to you and to your offspring.
translation: Pa mulu wauko, amona Yawe naiminina. Elyo amweba ati, “Nine Yawe, Lesa wakwa wiso Abrahamu kabili Lesa wakwa Isaki. Ici calo ulelepo niwe nkapeela pamo na ba mu lupwa lobe.

english: Your offspring will be as the dust of the earth, and you will spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south. In you and in your offspring, all the families of the earth will be blessed.
Behold, I am with you, and will keep you, wherever you go, and will bring you again into this land. For I will not leave you until I have done that which I have spoken of to you.”
translation: Mona, ine naba nobe lyonse, nakulakusunga konse uko wakulaya. Kabili nkakubwesesha kuli cino cine calo. Nshakakulekeleshe mpaka nkacite fyonse ifyo nakulaya.”

english: Jacob awakened out of his sleep, and he said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I didn’t know it.”
translation: Cilya Yakobo abuuka mu tulo, asosa ati, “Cine cine pano pantu Yawe epo ali, na ine nshacishiba.”

english: He was afraid, and said, “How awesome this place is! This is none other than God’s house, and this is the gate of heaven.”
translation: Yakobo epakumfwa umwenso, asosa nokuti, “We ncende nobe ulakatama! Iyi ncende teyafye, ni ŋanda yakwa Lesa! Iyi e mpongolo ya ku mulu.”

english: He called the name of that place Bethel, but the name of the city was Luz at the first.
translation: Yakobo ainika iyo ncende ishina lya Betele, nangu uyu musumba kale waleitwa Lusi.

english: Arise, go to Paddan Aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother’s father. Take a wife from there from the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
translation: Ima akuya ku calo ca Padani Aramu kwa Betueli, sokulu uwafyala banoko. Uli nokuupa umo pa bakashana bamwana Labani ndume ya banoko.

english: Jacob vowed a vow, saying, “If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and clothing to put on,
translation: Elyo Yakobo alaya icilayo ati, “Nga cakuti Lesa akulaba na ine, no kunsunga pali ulu lwendo ndipo, no kulampeela ifyakulya ne fyakufwala,

english: so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, and the LORD will be my God,
translation: pakuti nkabwelele na ku ŋanda ya batata umutende, ninshi Yawe ewakulaba Lesa wandi.

english: then this stone, which I have set up for a pillar, will be God’s house. Of all that you will give me I will surely give a tenth to you.”
translation: Kabili ilibwe njiminike lyakulaba e ŋanda yakupepelapo Lesa. Kabili pali fyonse ifyo ukampeela, nkalabuulapo cimo pekumi no kukupeela.”

english: May God Almighty bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, that you may be a company of peoples,
translation: Lesa Umwine wa maka yonse engakupaala, akakupeele ubufyashi, akakusandulule, mpaka ukabe ibumba lya mishobo ya bantu.

english: and give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring with you, that you may inherit the land where you travel, which God gave to Abraham.”
translation: Lesa engakupeela iwe pamo na ba mu lupwa lobe ipaalo apeele Abrahamu, pakuti cino calo umo nomba wikala ngo mweni, ukacipoke cikabe calo cobe.”

english: Isaac sent Jacob away. He went to Paddan Aram to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.
translation: Elyo Isaki aleka Yakobo ukuya, nao aya ku calo ca Padani Aramu, kuli Labani mwana Betueli umwina Aramu, ndume yakwa Rebeka, nyina wakwa Yakobo na Esau.

english: Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan Aram, to take him a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he gave him a command, saying, “You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;”
translation: Nomba Esau aumfwile ukuti Isaki alipaala Yakobo kabili alimutuma ku Padani Aramu pakuti eko akaye upila. Kabili aumfwile nokuti, ilyo amupaalile, alimukonkomeshe ati, “Wikopa umwanakashi umwina Kenani”

english: and that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Paddan Aram.
translation: elyo nokuti Yakobo nao alibeela wishi na nyina aliya na ku Padani Aramu.

english: Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan didn’t please Isaac, his father.
translation: Esau epakushininkisha ukuti wishi Isaki tatemwa abanakashi abena Kenani.

english: So Esau went to Ishmael, and took, in addition to the wives that he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebaioth, to be his wife.
translation: Kanshi Esau ekuya kuli Ishimaeli mwana Abrahamu, aupa na Mahalati mwana Ishimaeli, nkashimbiye kwa Nebaiyoti, ukulunda pa bakashi akwete kale.

english: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came to the land of the children of the east.
translation: Kanshi Yakobo alikonkenyepo ulwendo lwakwe, asuka afika na ku calo ca bantu babela ku kabanga.

english: When Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban, his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban, his mother’s brother, Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.
translation: Cilya Yakobo amona Rakeli mwana Labani nalume, ali ne mpaanga shakwa Labani, awe Yakobo aya kunkulushapo icilibwe balecilika pa cishima. Apeela na menshi ku mpaanga shakwa nalume, shanwa.

english: Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.
translation: Elyo Yakobo atomona Rakeli pakumuposha, atendeka nokulila, aleikatisha.

english: Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s relative, and that he was Rebekah’s son. She ran and told her father.
translation: Alaeba Rakeli ati, “Ine ndi lupwa lwa bawiso, nine mwana Rebeka.” Kanshi Rakeli epakubutuka aya ebako wishi.

english: When Laban heard the news of Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet Jacob, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. Jacob told Laban all these things.
translation: Cilya Labani aumfwa ifyo Rakeli amweba ukuti ni Yakobo mwana nkashi yakwe, Labani abutuka kukumukumanya. Awe amukukutila, kabili amutomona pakumuposha, elyo amusenda kumwakwe. Yakobo nao epakumushimikilako ifi fintu fyonse.

english: Laban said to him, “Surely you are my bone and my flesh.” Jacob stayed with him for a month.
translation: Labani epakumweba ati, “Iwe uli lupwa lwandi pakatifye.”

english: Laban said to Jacob, “Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what will your wages be?”
translation: Labani epakumweba ati, “Bushe iwe ico uli lupwa lwandi, eco wingamombelafye ukwabula kulipilwa? Awe njebafye amalipilo ulefwaya.”

english: Laban had two daughters. The name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
translation: Labani ali na bana abakashana babili. Ishina lya wamukalamba ni Leya, elyo uwamwaice ni Rakeli.

english: Leah’s eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and attractive.
translation: Leya ali na menso ayafuuka, lelo Rakeli ali no mubili uusuma kabili uwayemba.

english: Jacob loved Rachel. He said, “I will serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.”
translation: Yakobo atemenwe Rakeli. Kanshi aebele Labani ati, “Nkamubombela pa myaka cine lubali pa mwana wenu umukashana Rakeli umwaice bantu.”

english: Laban said, “It is better that I give her to you, than that I should give her to another man. Stay with me.”
translation: Labani nao asosa ati, “Cena ico cawamapo ukuti namupeela kuli iwe ukucila ku muntu umbi. Iwe ikalafye kuno kwine kumwandi.”

english: He looked, and saw a well in the field, and saw three flocks of sheep lying there by it. For out of that well they watered the flocks. The stone on the well’s mouth was large.
translation: Mu mpanga iyo amona icishima ca menshi ne mikuni ya mpaanga itatu ilele mupepi ne cishima,

english: Jacob served seven years for Rachel. They seemed to him but a few days, for the love he had for her.
translation: Kanshi Yakobo abombele imyaka cine lubali pakuti bamupeele Rakeli. Lelo iyo myaka yamonekefye kwati ni nshiku shampendwa ico atemenwe Rakeli.

english: Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in to her.”
translation: Elyo Yakobo aebele Labani ati, “Mpeeleni umukashi wandi. Inshita mwapimine naipwa ndefwaya tulelala nankwe.”

english: Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
translation: Kanshi Labani epakulonganika abantu bonse aba kulya kwine, atebeta ne mitebeto.

english: In the evening, he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to Jacob. He went in to her.
translation: Lelo cilya caba icungulo, Labani abuula mwane Leya amutwala kuli Yakobo, na Yakobo asendama nankwe.

english: Laban gave Zilpah his servant to his daughter Leah for a servant.
translation: Kabili Labani apeela mwane Leya umwanakashi uwakumubombela, umukashana umusha wakwe, Silipa.

english: In the morning, behold, it was Leah! He said to Laban, “What is this you have done to me? Didn’t I serve with you for Rachel? Why then have you deceived me?”
translation: Kutifye cilya bwaca, Yakobo asanga ukuti ni Leya! Elyo aebele Labani ati, “Ngeco mwancitila ifi cinshi? Ine ilyo nalemubombela, nalefwaya Rakeli, bushe teifyo? Bushe kanshi cinshi mwancenjesesha?”

english: Laban said, “It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.
translation: Labani amwasuka ati, “Ifwe kuno tatwaba na lutambi ulwakuufya umwaice ilyo umukalamba wakwe talati opwe.

english: Fulfill the week of this one, and we will give you the other also for the service which you will serve with me for seven more years.”
translation: Kanshi tala pwisha umulungu wakusefya ubwinga, lyena elyo tukakupeela no mwaice bantu wine, lelo ukamombela imyaka na imbi cine lubali.”

english: Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week. He gave him Rachel his daughter as wife.
translation: Yakobo nao acita ifyo Labani asosele. Apwisha umulungu wakusefya ubwinga ali na Leya, elyo Labani amupeela mwane Rakeli ukuba umukashi wakwe.

english: Laban gave Bilhah, his servant, to his daughter Rachel to be her servant.
translation: Labani apeela mwane Rakeli umwanakashi uwakumubombela, umukashana umusha wakwe, Bilua.

english: There all the flocks were gathered. They rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone back on the well’s mouth in its place.
translation: pantu muli ici cishima baletapa amenshi ayakuti imikuni inwe. Icilibwe balecilika pa cishima cali icikalamba. Baleti cilya imikuni ya fitekwa yalongana, bakacema bakunkulusha bafumyapo icilibwe balecilika pa cishima, elyo batapa amenshi yakuti ifitekwa finwe. Kabili elyo balebwekesha icilibwe cakucilika pa cishima pa ncende yaciko.

english: He went in also to Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him seven more years.
translation: Yakobo epakulasendama na Rakeli wine. Lelo Yakobo atemwishishepo Rakeli ukucila Leya. Kanshi alundilepo ukubombela Labani na imbi imyaka cine lubali.

english: The LORD saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.
translation: Ilyo Yawe amwene ukuti Yakobo tatemenwe Leya, apeele Leya ubufyashi, lelo Rakeli wena ali ŋumba.

english: Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she named him Reuben. For she said, “Because the LORD has looked at my affliction; for now my husband will love me.”
translation: Leya epakuba pabukulu apaapa no mwana umwaume. Amwinika ne shina lya Rubeni, pantu asosele ati, “Nico Yawe namona ubulanda bwandi. Nomba umulume wandi cine cine akantemwa.”

english: She conceived again, and bore a son, and said, “Because the LORD has heard that I am hated, he has therefore given me this son also.” She named him Simeon.
translation: Awe Leya aba nakabili pabukulu, apaapa no mwana umwaume, asosa ati, “Nico Yawe alyumfwa ukuti nshatemwikwa, eico ampeelela umwana na umbi.” Kanshi epakumwinika ishina lya Simeoni.

english: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “Now this time my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore his name was called Levi.
translation: Leya nakabili aba pabukulu, apaapa no mwana umwaume. Lyena asosa ati, “Nomba ino nshita umulume wandi akansakamana, pantu nimufyalila abana abaume batatu.” Kanshi epakumwinika ishina lya Levi.

english: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” Therefore she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.
translation: Nakabili Leya aba pabukulu, apaapa no mwana umwaume. Elyo asosa ati, “Lino lyena ndelumbanya Yawe.” Kanshi epakwinika umwana ishina lya Yuda. Awe Leya atala aiminina mu bufyashi.

english: Jacob said to them, “My relatives, where are you from?” They said, “We are from Haran.”
translation: Elyo Yakobo aipwishe bakacema ati, “Mwe bamunyinane bushe ni kwi mwafuma?” Nabo bamwasuka abati, “Twafuma mu Harani.”

english: He said to them, “Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?” They said, “We know him.”
translation: Abepusha ati, “Bushe mwalishiba Labani, umwishikulu wakwa Naho?” Nabo bamwasuka abati, “Ee twalimwishiba.”

english: He said to them, “Is it well with him?” They said, “It is well. See, Rachel, his daughter, is coming with the sheep.”
translation: Yakobo abepusha ati, “Bushe ali umutende?” Nabo bayasuka abati, “Ee alifye umutende, no mwana wakwe umukashana Rakeli, uyu aleisa ali ne mpaanga.”

english: He said, “Behold, it is still the middle of the day, not time to gather the livestock together. Water the sheep, and go and feed them.”
translation: Elyo Yakobo abeba ati, “Moneni akasuba kacili katuntulu. Ino taili nshita yakulonganika ifitekwa. Imwe fipeelenifye amenshi finwe, elyo mufibwekeshemo kukulya.”

english: They said, “We can’t, until all the flocks are gathered together, and they roll the stone from the well’s mouth. Then we will water the sheep.”
translation: Nabo bamwasuka abati, “Teti tucite ifyo kano imikuni yonse yalongana ne cilibwe bacilika pa cishima bacikunkulushapo. Lyena elyo tulenwesha ifitekwa amenshi.”

english: While he was yet speaking with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she kept them.
translation: Ilyo acili alelanda nabo, awe Rakeli aisa ali ne mpaanga shakwa wishi, pantu ali ni kacema mwanakashi.

english: The heavens, the earth, and all their vast array were finished.
translation: Kanshi efyo umulu ne sonde ne fintu fyonse ifyabamo fyapwililile ukupangwa.

english: A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers.
translation: Mu Edeni mwafumine umumana uwakutapilila ibala. Ukufuma mulya walekene mu milonga ine.

english: The name of the first is Pishon: it flows through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;
translation: Ukuf 20:11

english: and the gold of that land is good. Bdellium and onyx stone are also there.
translation: Kabili golide wa muli cilya calo musuma. Elyo mulasangwa ne finyamuti ifyanunka ubusaka na mabwe ya onikisi.

english: The name of the second river is Gihon. It is the same river that flows through the whole land of Cush.
translation: Ishina lya mumana walenga ibili ni Gihoni. Uyu mumana wapita uwashokana mu calo conse ica Kushi.

english: The name of the third river is Hiddekel. This is the one which flows in front of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
translation: Ishina lya mumana walenga itatu ni Tigilisi. Uyu wena wapita lwa ku kabanga ka musumba wa Ashuri. Elyo umumana walenga ine ni Yufurate.

english: The LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
translation: Yawe Lesa abuulile umuntu amubika na mwibala lya Edeni pakuti alelimamo no kulalisunga.

english: The LORD God commanded the man, saying, “You may freely eat of every tree of the garden;
translation: Elyo Yawe Lesa akonkomesha umuntu ati, “Kuti walyako ku miti yonse iya mwibala,

english: but you shall not eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”
translation: lelo umuti wakwishiba ifisuma ne fibi, wena wikalyako, pantu ubushiku ukalyakofye ninshi ukafwa.”

english: The LORD God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make him a helper comparable to him.”
translation: Elyo Yawe Lesa asosele ati, “Taciweme ukuti umuntu abe eka. Nalamubumbila uwakumwafwa uumulingile.”

english: Out of the ground the LORD God formed every animal of the field, and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the man to see what he would call them. Whatever the man called every living creature became its name.
translation: Kanshi Yawe Lesa abumbile ukufuma ku mushili inama shonse isha mu mpanga ne fyuni fyonse ifya mu lwelele. Elyo afitwala fyonse ku muntu pakuti amone amashina alefinika. Kanshi ishina lintu aitile conse icabumi, elyali e shina lyaciko.

english: On the seventh day God finished his work which he had done; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
translation: Pa bushiku bwalenga cine lubali Lesa ninshi napwisha imilimo alebomba. Kanshi pa bushiku bwalenga cine lubali Lesa alituushishe, aleka imilimo yakwe yonse.

english: The man gave names to all livestock, and to the birds of the sky, and to every animal of the field; but for man there was not found a helper comparable to him.
translation: Kanshi umuntu epakwinika amashina ifitekwa fyonse, ifyuni fyonse ifya mu lwelele, elyo ne nama sha mpanga shonse. Lelo pali ifi fyonse tapali cakwafwa Adamu icamulingile.

english: The LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. As the man slept, he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
translation: Kanshi Yawe Lesa epakulenga umuntu apone mu tulo utwingi. Ilyo umuntu acili mu tulo, Yawe Lesa afumya ulubafu lumo ku muntu, abwesesha no munofu apo alufumishe.

english: The LORD God made a woman from the rib which he had taken from the man, and brought her to the man.
translation: Ku lubafu afumishe ku muntu umwaume, Yawe Lesa abumbako umwanakashi, amutwala na ku mwaume.

english: The man said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh. She will be called ‘woman,’ because she was taken out of Man.”
translation: Elyo umwaume asosa ati,

english: Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.
translation: Kanshi eco umwaume ashiila wishi na nyina auminkana no mukashi wakwe, elyo aba babili baba umubili umo.

english: The man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.
translation: Umwaume no mukashi wakwe bali ubwamba, lelo tabaleumfwa insoni.

english: God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy, because he rested in it from all his work of creation which he had done.
translation: Elyo Lesa apaala ubushiku bwalenga cine lubali, kabili abucita ukuba ubwamushilo. Pantu pali ubu bushiku epo atuushishe ku milimo yonse iya bubumbo.

english: This is the history of the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens.
translation: Bahi 4:4

english: No plant of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up; for the LORD God had not caused it to rain on the earth. There was not a man to till the ground,
translation: pesonde tapali icimpusa nelyo cimo kabili tapali nelyo cimo icamenenepo, pantu Yawe Lesa ali talalokeshapo imfula pesonde. Elyo takwali umuntu uwakulima umushili.

english: but a mist went up from the earth, and watered the whole surface of the ground.
translation: Lelo kwali amenshi ayalefuma mu mushili no kulatapilila umushili mpanga yonse.

english: The LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
translation: Elyo Yawe Lesa abumba umuntu ukufuma ku lukungu lwa kwiloba. Kabili amuputilisha umupu wabumi mu myona no muntu aba umumi.

english: The LORD God planted a garden eastward, in Eden, and there he put the man whom he had formed.
translation: Kabili Yawe Lesa alima ibala lwa ku kabanga mu Edeni. Elyo mulya mwine abikamo no muntu uo abumbile.

english: Out of the ground the LORD God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
translation: Yawe Lesa amesha pa mushili imiti iya misango yonse, imiti iyisuma mukumoneka, kabili iya fitwalo ifyawama ukulyako. Pakati ke bala pali umuti wabumi no muti wakwishiba ifisuma ne fibi.

english: When Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister. She said to Jacob, “Give me children, or else I will die.”
translation: Ilyo Rakeli amwene ukuti tafyalile Yakobo umwana nelyo umo, afimbila nkashimbiye Leya. Kanshi alaeba Yakobo ati, “Mpeela abana, nga teifyo ndi nokufwa!”

english: Zilpah, Leah’s servant, bore Jacob a son.
translation: Elyo Silipa umusha wakwa Leya afyalila Yakobo umwana umwaume.

english: Leah said, “How fortunate!” She named him Gad.
translation: Leya epakutila, “Yangu we shuko busuma!” Kanshi Leya epakwinika umwana ishina lya Gadi.

english: Zilpah, Leah’s servant, bore Jacob a second son.
translation: Kabili Silipa umusha wakwa Leya epakufyalila Yakobo umwana mwaume uwabubili.

english: Leah said, “Happy am I, for the daughters will call me happy.” She named him Asher.
translation: Lyena Leya epakutila, “Yangu ifyo nasansamuka! Abanakashi bakalanjita, insansa.” Kanshi Leya epakumwinika ishina lya Asheri.

english: Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother, Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”
translation: Pa nshita yakuseepa iŋanu, Rubeni aile ku mabala. Ku mabala asangako ifimpusa fya mandarake aletela nyina Leya. Rakeli epakweba Leya ati, “Napapata mpeelako tumishila twa mandarake tumo twa mwana obe.”

english: Leah said to her, “Is it a small matter that you have taken away my husband? Would you take away my son’s mandrakes, also?” Rachel said, “Therefore he will lie with you tonight for your son’s mandrakes.”
translation: Lelo Leya amwasuka ati, “Bushe ukumpoka umulume wandi kwalicepa icakuti ulefwaya upoke na mandarake wa mwana wandi?” Rakeli epakusosa ati, “Cisuma nga wampeelako mandarake wa mwana obe, ninshi lelo ubushiku kuti wasendama na Yakobo.”

english: Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, “You must come in to me; for I have surely hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” He lay with her that night.
translation: Kanshi icungulo ilyo Yakobo abwela ku mabala, Leya aya kukumukumanya, amweba ati, “Lelo uleisa sendama na ine. Ine nindipila pali iwe na mandarake wa mwana wandi.” Kanshi Yakobo nao epakusendama na Leya ubo bushiku.

english: God listened to Leah, and she conceived, and bore Jacob a fifth son.
translation: Lesa nao aumfwa imipapatile yakwa Leya. Leya epakuba pabukulu, afyalila na Yakobo umwana umwaume uwalengele basano.

english: Leah said, “God has given me my hire, because I gave my servant to my husband.” She named him Issachar.
translation: Elyo Leya asosa ati, “Lesa anambula pakupeela umusha wandi ku mulume wandi.” Kanshi Leya epakwinika umwana ishina lya Isaka.

english: Leah conceived again, and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
translation: Leya nakabili aisa ba pabukulu, afyalila na Yakobo umwana umwaume uwalengele mutanda.

english: Jacob’s anger burned against Rachel, and he said, “Am I in God’s place, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?”
translation: Yakobo asuka amufulilwa, amweba ati, “Bushe ine ndi Lesa uushakupeela bufyashi bwakufyala abana?”

english: Leah said, “God has endowed me with a good dowry. Now my husband will live with me, because I have borne him six sons.” She named him Zebulun.
translation: Leya epakusosa ati, “Lesa nampeela ubupe ubukankala. Ili lyena umulume wandi akulancindika, pantu nimufyalila abana abaume mutanda.” Kanshi Leya epakwinika umwana ishina lya Sebuloni.

english: Afterwards, she bore a daughter, and named her Dinah.
translation: Panuma Leya afyele umwana umwanakashi, wena amwinika ishina lya Dina.

english: God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her, and opened her womb.
translation: Elyo Lesa aibukisha Rakeli, aumfwa nefyo alepapata, epakumupeela ubufyashi.

english: She conceived, bore a son, and said, “God has taken away my reproach.”
translation: Rakeli aba pabukulu, apaapa no mwana umwaume, epakusosa ati, “Lesa namfumya insoni pa mubili.”

english: She named him Joseph, saying, “May the LORD add another son to me.”
translation: Kanshi Rakeli epakwinika umwana ishina lya Yosefu. Kabili asosa nokuti, “Cawama nga Yawe enganundilapo umwana umwaume na umbi.”

english: When Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me away, that I may go to my own place, and to my country.
translation: Panuma Rakeli afyele Yosefu, Yakobo aebele Labani ati, “Nomba lekeni ndeya, mbwelelemo ku calo kumwesu.

english: Give me my wives and my children for whom I have served you, and let me go; for you know my service with which I have served you.”
translation: Mpeeleni abakashi bandi na bana, pantu ni pa mulandu wa aba bantu eco nalemubombela. Kanshi lekenifye ndeya. Namwishiba imilimo namubombela.”

english: Laban said to him, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, stay here, for I have divined that the LORD has blessed me for your sake.”
translation: Lelo Labani aebele Yakobo ati, “Nga cingamusekesha, namupapata mwikale kuno kwine. Ni mukupendula emo naishibila ukuti Yawe alimpaala pa mulandu wa iwe.”

english: He said, “Appoint me your wages, and I will give it.”
translation: Elyo Labani alundapo nokuti, “Iwe njebafye amalipilo ulefwaya, na ine nalakulipila.”

english: Jacob said to him, “You know how I have served you, and how your livestock have fared with me.
translation: Yakobo amweba ati, “Imwe namwishiba imilimo namubombela, nefyo ifitekwa fyenu fisandile ico nine mfisunga.

english: She said, “Behold, my maid Bilhah. Go in to her, that she may bear on my knees, and I also may obtain children by her.”
translation: Elyo Rakeli amweba ati, “Bilua uyu, umusha wandi umwanakashi, usendame nankwe, pakuti akamfyalileko abana, na ine nkakwate abana kuli uyu.”

english: For it was little which you had before I came, and it has increased to a multitude. The LORD has blessed you wherever I turned. Now when will I provide for my own house also?”
translation: Ilyo nshilaisa kuno mwakwete ifitekwa ifinono, nomba nafisanda nganshi. Kabili konse uko naleba Yawe alemupaala. Nga nomba ine, ni lilali nkatampa ukubombela aba mu ŋanda yandi?”

english: Laban said, “What shall I give you?” Jacob said, “You shall not give me anything. If you will do this thing for me, I will again feed your flock and keep it.
translation: Labani epakwipusha Yakobo ati, “Bushe finshi ndi nokukupeela?” Yakobo amwasuka ati, “Awe mwimpeela nelyo cimo. Lelo nga mwancitila ici cintu cimofye, lyena ndekonkanyapo ukucema ifitekwa fyenu no kulafisunga.

english: I will pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. This will be my hire.
translation: Kanshi lekeni lelo mpite mu fitekwa fyenu fyonse no kufumyamo impaanga shonse isha fisemba nangu isha mabala, utwana twa mpaanga tonse utwafiita, ne mbushi shonse isha mabala nangu isha fisemba, efili nokuba amalipilo yandi.

english: So my righteousness will answer for me hereafter, when you come concerning my hire that is before you. Every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the sheep, that might be with me, will be considered stolen.”
translation: No bufumacumi bwandi bukamonekela kuntanshi, ilyo lyonse mukalaisa mukupituluka mu malipilo mwandipila. Imbushi yonse iyo nkakwata nga taili na fisemba nelyo amabala nangu akana ka mpaanga konse akashili kafiita ninshi kuti mwatila fyaibwafye.”

english: Laban said, “Behold, let it be according to your word.”
translation: Labani asuminisha ati, “Cisuma natulecita ifyo fine walanda.”

english: That day, he removed the male goats that were streaked and spotted, and all the female goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had white in it, and all the black ones among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons.
translation: Ubo bwine bushiku, Labani wena afumyapo imbushi shonse ishilume isha mindoloshi nangu isha mabala, imbushi shonse ishikota isha fisemba nangu isha mabala (shonse ishakwete ifisemba fyabuuta), elyo no twana twa mpaanga tonse utwafiita. Apeela na bana bakwe abaume ukuti ebo baleshisunga.

english: He set three days’ journey between himself and Jacob, and Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.
translation: Elyo ashitalusha kuli Yakobo ubulendo bwa nshiku shitatu. Mu nshiku isho Yakobo wena ashele alecema ifitekwa fyakwa Labani fyonse ifyashelepo.

english: Jacob took to himself rods of fresh poplar, almond, and plane tree, peeled white streaks in them, and made the white appear which was in the rods.
translation: Elyo Yakobo abuulile imisambo ibishi iya muti wa popula, uwa alumondi no wa pulane. Asukulako ifipapa fya misambo apangamo ifisemba ifyabuuta no kusha icimuti ca mukati cilemoneka. Kanshi imisambo yalamoneka iya fisemba ifyabuuta.

english: He set the rods which he had peeled opposite the flocks in the watering troughs where the flocks came to drink. They conceived when they came to drink.
translation: Elyo Yakobo abika iyi misambo asukwileko mu milimba pakuti fibe intanshi ilyo ifitekwa fileisa kukunwa amenshi. Alecita ifyo pantu ni pakwisa kukunwa amenshi elyo ishilume shaletamfya ishikota.

english: The flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks produced streaked, speckled, and spotted.
translation: Kanshi ico ifitekwa fyaletamfya pantanshi ya misambo iyo asukwileko, epakulafyala utwana utwa mindoloshi nangu utwa fisemba nangu utwa mabala.

english: She gave him Bilhah her servant as wife, and Jacob went in to her.
translation: Kanshi Rakeli epakubuula Bilua, amupeela kuli Yakobo ukuti abe umukashi wakwe. Yakobo epakusendama na Bilua.

english: Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the streaked and all the black in Laban’s flock. He put his own droves apart, and didn’t put them into Laban’s flock.
translation: Elyo Yakobo apatulapo utwana twa mpaanga twaba tweka, lelo alenga ishashele shonse shiloleshanye ne mpaanga shakwa Labani isha mindoloshi ne shafiita. Mukucita ifi alesunga ifitekwa fyakwe fyeka, kabili taleleka ukuti fisankane ne fyakwa Labani.

english: Whenever the stronger of the flock conceived, Jacob laid the rods in front of the eyes of the flock in the watering troughs, that they might conceive among the rods;
translation: Ilyo lyonse ifitekwa filume ifyatuuluka fyaletamfya ifitekwa ifikota ifyatuuluka, Yakobo alebika imisambo ya fisemba mu milimba pantanshi ya fitekwa ilyo filetamfiwa, pakuti fitamfiwe ilyo fili mu mupepi ne misambo ya fisemba

english: but when the flock were feeble, he didn’t put them in. So the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.
