english: Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were bound, and he was there in custody.
translation: Shikulu wakwa Yosefu amuposa mu cifungo, mu ncende umo balefungila abafungwa ba mfumu. Awe nao emo alaikala.

english: But the LORD was with Joseph, and showed kindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
translation: Lelo Yawe ali na Yosefu kabili amukwatila icitemwiko icishipwa. Alenga nokuti atemwikwe ku cinso cakwa kasunga wa bafungwa.

english: The keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison. Whatever they did there, he was responsible for it.
translation: Kanshi nomba kasunga wa bafungwa apeela Yosefu umulimo wakulaangalila bonse abali mu cifungo, kabili ewalemona pali fyonse ifyalecitika mulya.

english: The keeper of the prison didn’t look after anything that was under his hand, because the LORD was with him; and that which he did, the LORD made it prosper.
translation: Kasunga wa bafungwa aleka no kulasakamana pa milimo iyo apeele Yosefu ukulabomba, pantu Yawe ali na Yosefu, kabili alemupeela ishuko muli fyonse ifyo alebomba.

english: His master saw that the LORD was with him, and that the LORD made all that he did prosper in his hand.
translation: Shikulu wakwe alimwene ukuti Yawe ali na Yosefu, kabili nokuti ni Yawe alemupeela ishuko muli fyonse alebomba.

english: Joseph found favor in his sight. He ministered to him, and Potiphar made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.
translation: Kanshi Yosefu epakusanga ukutemwikwa pa cinso cakwa shikulu wakwe, amucita no mutumishi wakwe. Potifa amusonta ukuba kangalila wa ŋanda yakwe, amupa na maka yakusunga ifintu fyonse akwete.

english: From the time that he made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake. The LORD’s blessing was on all that he had, in the house and in the field.
translation: Ukufumafye pa nshita Potifa abikile Yosefu ukuba kangalila wa ŋanda ne fintu fyonse Potifa akwete, Yawe apaala iŋanda ya mwina Egupto pa mulandu wakwa Yosefu. Ipaalo lyakwa Yawe lyali pa fintu fyonse Potifa akwete, mu ŋanda elyo na mu mabala.

english: He left all that he had in Joseph’s hand. He didn’t concern himself with anything, except for the food which he ate. Joseph was well-built and handsome.
translation: Potifa asuka abika fyonse ifyakwete mu maboko yakwa Yosefu. Apo Yosefu ewalefisunga, wena talesakamana nelyo cimo, kanofye icakulya alelya.

english: After these things, his master’s wife set her eyes on Joseph; and she said, “Lie with me.”
translation: Awe umuila inshiku, muka shikulu wakwe alakumbwa Yosefu. Asuka amweba ati, “Isa tulale nobe.”

english: But he refused, and said to his master’s wife, “Behold, my master doesn’t know what is with me in the house, and he has put all that he has into my hand.
translation: Lelo Yosefu akaana. Aeba muka shikulu wakwe ati, “Shikulu tasakamana ku cintu nelyo cimo pa ŋanda apo ine epo ndi. Fyonse ifyo akwata abika mu maboko yandi.

english: No one is greater in this house than I am, and he has not kept back anything from me but you, because you are his wife. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?”
translation: Imili 2:9

english: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which the LORD God had made. He said to the woman, “Has God really said, ‘You shall not eat of any tree of the garden’?”
translation: Nomba insoka yali incenjeshi nganshi ukucila pa nama shonse isha mpanga isho Yawe Lesa apangile. Elyo yaipusha umwanakashi aiti, “Bushe cine cine Lesa atile mwilalyako ku muti onse uwa mwibala?”

english: The man said, “I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid myself.”
translation: Umwaume ayasuka ati, “Nacumfwa uko uleenda mwibala, elyo nakwata umwenso, ico ndi ubwamba, epakubelama.”

english: God said, “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?”
translation: Elyo Yawe Lesa amwipusha ati, “Nga nani akwebele ati uli ubwamba? Bushe naulya icitwalo ca muti ico nakuleseshe ukulyako?”

english: The man said, “The woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”
translation: Umwaume ayasuka ati, “Umwanakashi wampeele ukuba nankwe kuno, eumpeele icitwalo ca muti, na ine nalya.”

english: The LORD God said to the woman, “What have you done?” The woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”
translation: Elyo Yawe Lesa aipusha umwanakashi ati, “Nga ici ucitile cinshi?” Umwanakashi ayasuka ati, “Ni nsoka eimbepele, na ine elyo nalya.”

english: The LORD God said to the serpent, “Because you have done this, you are cursed above all livestock, and above every animal of the field. You shall go on your belly and you shall eat dust all the days of your life.
translation: Timo 2:14

english: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”
translation: Nkabika ukupatana pakati ka iwe no mwanakashi,

english: To the woman he said, “I will greatly multiply your pain in childbirth. You will bear children in pain. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation: Ku mwanakashi atile,

english: To Adam he said, “Because you have listened to your wife’s voice, and have eaten from the tree, about which I commanded you, saying, ‘You shall not eat of it,’ the ground is cursed for your sake. You will eat from it with much labor all the days of your life.
translation: Kuli Adamu atile, “Pantu wacumfwila umukashi obe, elyo walya na ku muti nakukonkomeshe ukuti, ‘Taufwile ukulyako,’

english: It will yield thorns and thistles to you; and you will eat the herb of the field.
translation: Umushili wakulamesha imyunga na bacilasa,

english: You will eat bread by the sweat of your face until you return to the ground, for you were taken out of it. For you are dust, and you shall return to dust.”
translation: Kwilibe lya pa mpumi yobe eko ukalamwena icakulya,

english: The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat fruit from the trees of the garden,
translation: Umwanakashi ayasuka insoka ati, “Kuti twalya ifitwalo fya muti onse uwa mwibala,

english: The man called his wife Eve because she would be the mother of all the living.
translation: Adamu ainike umukashi wakwe ishina lya Efa , pantu e nyina wa bantu bonse.

english: The LORD God made garments of animal skins for Adam and for his wife, and clothed them.
translation: Yawe Lesa epakupangila Adamu na Efa ifyakufwala ifyampapa, elyo abafwika no kubafwika.

english: The LORD God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever—”
translation: Elyo Yawe Lesa asosele ati, “Umuntu ali kwati ni umo pali ifwe, kukwishiba ifisuma ne fibi. Kanshi tewakuleka ukuti akasabe ifitwalo ku muti upeela ubumi akalye kabili akabelele umumi.”

english: Therefore the LORD God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken.
translation: Kanshi Yawe Lesa epakutamfya umuntu mwibala lya Edeni pakuti alelima umushili uo amufumisheko.

english: So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life.
translation: Panuma yakutamfyamo umuntu, Yawe Lesa abika mwibala lya Edeni ku kabanga bakerubi elyo no lupanga ulwalebilima umulilo, ulwaleyafye konse konse pakulesha umuntu ukuya ku muti wabumi.

english: but not the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the garden. God has said, ‘You shall not eat of it. You shall not touch it, lest you die.’”
translation: lelo Lesa atile, ‘Tamufwile ukulyako ifitwalo fya muti waba pakati ke bala, kabili tamufwile na kwikatako, pantu mukafwa.’”

english: The serpent said to the woman, “You won’t really die,
translation: Insoka yayasuka umwanakashi aiti, “Awe cinefye tamwakafwe nakalya.

english: for God knows that in the day you eat it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”
translation: Pantu Lesa alishiba ukuti ilyo mukalyako, amenso yenu yakesuka elyo mukaba nga Lesa, mukeshiba ifisuma ne fibi.”

english: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate. Then she gave some to her husband with her, and he ate it, too.
translation: Ilyo umwanakashi amona ukuti ifitwalo fya muti fisuma ukulya, ifyayemba mukumoneka kabili kuti fyafwaikwa pakukwata amano, asabako ifitwalo fimo alya. Elyo fimbi apeelako umulume uo bali nankwe, nao alya.

english: Their eyes were opened, and they both knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves.
translation: Elyo bonse babili amenso yabo yaisuka, baishiba nokuti bali ubwamba. Kanshi epakubilinkanya amabula ya mukunyu, eyo bafwala.

english: They heard the LORD God’s voice walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
translation: Cilya caba ku cungulo umwaume no mukashi wakwe baumfwa uko Yawe Lesa aleenda mwibala. Batiina Yawe Lesa babelama mu miti ya mwibala.

english: The LORD God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”
translation: Lelo Yawe Lesa epakwita umwaume ati, “Bushe uli kwi?”

english: After these things, the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
translation: Ilyo papitile inshita, katumika wa lukombo lwa mfumu ya mu Egupto no walepanga umukate balilufyenye kuli shikulwibo Farao, imfumu ya mu Egupto.

english: and in the vine were three branches. It was as though it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters produced ripe grapes.
translation: uyu mwangashi waciba ne misambo itatu. Cilya amabula yafuma, apopene na maluba yabalula yatwala ne fisansangu fya myangashi iyapya.

english: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.”
translation: Ulukombo lwakwa Farao lwaciba mu minwe, elyo nabuula imyangashi nakamina mu lukombo lwakwa Farao, nabika no lukombo mu minwe yakwe.”

english: Joseph said to him, “This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.
translation: Yosefu amweba ati, “Nalakwilwila iciloto cobe. Imisambo iyo itatu, ni nshiku shitatu.

english: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head, and restore you to your office. You will give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, the way you did when you were his cup bearer.
translation: Mu nshikufye shitatu, Farao akakufumya mu cifungo, akakubwesha na ku mulimo walebomba. Ukabika ulukombo mu minwe yakwa Farao, nga filya fine walecita ilyo walebomba umulimo wa bukatumika wa lukombo lwa mfumu.

english: But remember me when it is well with you. Please show kindness to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.
translation: Lelo ilyo ukekala bwino, wikandabako, ukankwatile uluse. Ukansoseleko kuli Farao pakuti akamfumye muno mu cifungo.

english: For indeed, I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also I have done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.”
translation: Pantu ine bamfumishefye ku maka mu calo ca Bahibulu, elyo na kuno kwine nshacitapo mulandu uwakumposela mu cifungo.”

english: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, “I also was in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.
translation: Ilyo umukalamba wa balepanga imikate amona ukuti Yosefu ailwila umunankwe ifyakumuwamina, aeba Yosefu ati, “Na ine ninkwata iciloto. Nacilota ninsenda pa mutwe imiseke itatu iya mikate.

english: In the uppermost basket there were all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my head.”
translation: Mu museke waciba pamulu, mwaciba ifyakulya fya misango yonse ifyaocewa ifyakutwalila Farao. Lelo ifyuni fyacilalya mu museke wine nsendele pa mutwe.”

english: Joseph answered, “This is its interpretation. The three baskets are three days.
translation: Yosefu amweba ati, “Nalakwilwila iciloto cobe. Iyo miseke itatu, ni nshiku shitatu.

english: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head from off you, and will hang you on a tree; and the birds will eat your flesh from off you.”
translation: Mu nshiku shitatu, Farao akakufumya mu cifungo, akakuputuleko umutwe no kukukulika ku cimuti. Elyo ifyuni fikesa lya iminofu yobe.”

english: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cup bearer and the chief baker.
translation: Farao epakufulilwa aba babomfi babili, umukalamba wa bakatumika ba lukombo lwa mfumu, no mukalamba wa balepangila imfumu umukate.

english: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cup bearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.
translation: Nomba ubushiku bwalengele shitatu bwali e bushiku Farao afyelwemo. Kanshi Farao acitila ababomfi bakwe imitebeto. Afumya mu cifungo, pa cinso ca babomfi bakwe bonse, umukalamba wa bakatumika ba lukombo lwa mfumu no mukalamba wa balepangila imfumu imikate.

english: He restored the chief cup bearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand;
translation: Umukalamba wa bakatumika ba lukombo lwa mfumu amubwesesha ku mulimo wakwe, pakuti nakabili abike ulukombo mu minwe yakwa Farao.

english: but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.
translation: Lelo umukalamba wa balepanga imikate wena, alimukulikile nga mulya mwine Yosefu abelwilile ifiloto fyabo.

english: Yet the chief cup bearer didn’t remember Joseph, but forgot him.
translation: Umukalamba wa bakatumika ba lukombo lwa mfumu wena taibukishe kuli Yosefu iyoo, amulabako.

english: He put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.
translation: Kanshi epakubaposa mu cifungo mu ŋanda ya waleyangalila ifita fyalelonda kwisano, nakabili umo mwine emo na Yosefu afungilwe.

english: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he took care of them. They stayed in prison many days.
translation: Kangalila wa bamalonda apeela Yosefu umulimo wakubasunga, no kubatumika ewalebatumika. Elyo kabili balikokwelemo mu cifungo.

english: They both dreamed a dream, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cup bearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.
translation: Ubushiku bumo, katumika wa lukombo lwa mfumu no walepangila imfumu imikate, abali mu cifungo, cila umo alilotele iciloto pa bushiku bumo bwine. Kabili cila ciloto cali nomo calolele.

english: Joseph came in to them in the morning, and saw them, and saw that they were sad.
translation: Ulucelo cilya Yosefu aingilamo asanga ukuti bali abasakamana.

english: He asked Pharaoh’s officers who were with him in custody in his master’s house, saying, “Why do you look so sad today?”
translation: Kanshi aipusha ababomfi bakwa Farao abo ali nabo mu cifungo mu ŋanda yakwa shikulu wakwe ati, “Cinshi ico mwalamonekela bulanda bulanda lelo?”

english: They said to him, “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it.” Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Please tell it to me.”
translation: Bamwasuka abati, “Nico ifwe bonse babili natulota ifiloto, lelo tapali nelyo umo uwakutwilwilako.” Elyo Yosefu abeba ati, “Bushe ukwilula ifiloto te mulimo wakwa Lesa? Aleni njebeniko ifiloto fyenu.”

english: The chief cup bearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, “In my dream, behold, a vine was in front of me,
translation: Kanshi umukalamba wa bakatumika aebele Yosefu iciloto cakwe. Amweba ati, “Mu ciloto candi, nacimona umwangashi pantanshi yandi,

english: At the end of two full years, Pharaoh dreamed, and behold, he stood by the river.
translation: Ilyo papitile imyaka ibili iyituntulu Farao alotele iciloto. Alotele eminine pa lulamba lwa mumana wa Nailo.

english: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, with the chief baker.
translation: Limo Farao alifulilwe ababomfi bakwe, aposa ine no mukalamba wa balepanga imikate mu cifungo mu ŋanda yakwa kangalila wa fita ifilonda kwisano.

english: We dreamed a dream in one night, he and I. Each man dreamed according to the interpretation of his dream.
translation: Cila umo pali ifwe babili alilotele iciloto pa bushiku bumo bwinefye. Cila ciloto cali nomo calolele.

english: There was with us there a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard, and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams. He interpreted to each man according to his dream.
translation: Twalimo no mulumendo umo Umuhibulu, umusha wakwa kangalila wa bamalonda. Twalyebeleko uyo mulumendo ifiloto fyesu. Alitwilwilile filoto fyesu, cila umo amwilwila umwalolele iciloto cakwe.

english: As he interpreted to us, so it was. He restored me to my office, and he hanged him.”
translation: Kabili ifintu fyaishile citikafye ngomo mwine atwilwilile. Ine nalibwelele pa mulimo wandi, lelo umunandi wena alikulikwe.”

english: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon. He shaved himself, changed his clothing, and came in to Pharaoh.
translation: Kanshi Farao alitumine abakwita Yosefu. Baya mufumya mu cifungo bamuletafye bwangu bwangu. Yosefu atala abeya, afwala ne fyakufwala fimbi elyo aisa pa cinso cakwa Farao.

english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. I have heard it said of you, that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”
translation: Farao aebele Yosefu ati, “Ine nalilota iciloto, lelo tapali nelyo umo uwakunjilwilako. Lelo nalyumfwa uko balanda pali iwe ukuti, nga umo akweba ifyo alotele, kuti wamwilwila.”

english: Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “It isn’t in me. God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”
translation: Yosefu amwasuka ati, “Teine ndeilula, lelo ni Lesa euleilwila Farao ifyakumuwamina.”

english: Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, “In my dream, behold, I stood on the brink of the river;
translation: Elyo Farao aebele Yosefu ati, “Ine nalotele ninjiminina pa lulamba lwa mumana wa Nailo.

english: and behold, seven fat and sleek cattle came up out of the river. They fed in the marsh grass;
translation: Elyo mu mumana mwafuma iŋombe ishikota cine lubali ishatuuluka kabili ishaina ubusaka, shalalya ne cani ca mu lulamba lwa mumana.

english: and behold, seven other cattle came up after them, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.
translation: Elyo panuma ya ishi, mu mumana mwafuma iŋombe shimbi ishikota cine lubali ishapampauka, ishibi nganshi kabili ishaonda. Nshatala mona iŋombe ishabipa ngesho mu calo conse ca Egupto.

english: Behold, seven cattle came up out of the river. They were sleek and fat, and they fed in the marsh grass.
translation: Awe iŋombe ishikota cine lubali ishatuuluka kabili ishaina ubusaka shafuma mu mumana, elyo shalalya icani ca mu lulamba lwa mumana.

english: The thin and ugly cattle ate up the first seven fat cattle;
translation: Isho iŋombe ishaonda kabili ishibi shalya iŋombe cine lubali ishaina, ishabalilepo ukufuma mu mumana.

english: and when they had eaten them up, it couldn’t be known that they had eaten them, but they were still ugly, as at the beginning. So I awoke.
translation: Lelo panuma yakulya iŋombe ishaina, nalyo line shashalafye ishibi nga kale. Umuntu nelyo umo tekuti eshibe ukuti nashilya iŋombe shaina. Elyo nabuuka.

english: I saw in my dream, and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, full and good;
translation: Kabili mu ciloto candi namona imisonso ya ŋanu cine lubali iyaisulamo inseke ishisuma ishatuuluka, naimena ku lupimbili lumofye.

english: and behold, seven heads of grain, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.
translation: Elyo panuma lwatwala imisonso imbi cine lubali, iyi yena yali iyapapa kabili iyauminina ku mwela uwakaba uwa ku kabanga.

english: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads of grain. I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”
translation: Iyo misonso iyapapa yamina imisonso cine lubali iya nseke ishisuma. Nalishimikila abacita amalele ifi filoto, lelo tapaba uwakuti anjilwileko.”

english: Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God is about to do he has declared to Pharaoh.
translation: Elyo Yosefu aebele Farao ati, “Ifiloto fyakwa Farao filolelefye ku cintu cimo cine. Lesa nasokolwela Farao ifyo alaswa acite.

english: The seven good cattle are seven years; and the seven good heads of grain are seven years. The dream is one.
translation: Isho ŋombe ishikota ishisuma cine lubali myaka cine lubali, elyo ne misonso iyisuma iya ŋanu, nayo myaka cine lubali. Kanshi ifi filoto fyonse filolelefye ku cintu cimo cine.

english: The seven thin and ugly cattle that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty heads of grain blasted with the east wind; they will be seven years of famine.
translation: Elyo ne ŋombe ishikota isho cine lubali ishaonda kabili ishibi ishafumine mu mumana panuma, nasho myaka cine lubali. Elyo ne misonso iyapapa cine lubali iyauminina ku mwela wa ku kabanga uwakaba, e myaka cine lubali iya cipowe.

english: That is the thing which I have spoken to Pharaoh. God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.
translation: Kanshi efilya nacilanda kuli Farao ukuti, Lesa nalanga Farao ifyo alaswa acite.

english: Behold, seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt are coming.
translation: Imyaka cine lubali iyalaisa, mukaba ifyakulya ifingi nganshi mu calo conse ica Egupto.

english: Behold, seven other cattle came up after them out of the river, ugly and thin, and stood by the other cattle on the brink of the river.
translation: Kabili panuma, mu mumana wa Nailo mwafuma iŋombe ishikota cine lubali ishaonda kabili ishibi. Nasho shaya iminina apali ishibiye pa lulamba lwa mumana.

english: Seven years of famine will arise after them, and all the plenty will be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine will consume the land,
translation: Lelo panuma, pakakonka imyaka cine lubali iya cipowe. Abantu bakalaba nokuti mwali ifyakulya ifingi mu calo ca Egupto, pantu icipowe cikonaula icalo.

english: and the plenty will not be known in the land by reason of that famine which follows; for it will be very grievous.
translation: Abantu tabakebukishe ukuti mu calo mwali ifyakulya ifingi, pantu icipowe cikakonkapo, cikabipisha nganshi.

english: The dream was doubled to Pharaoh, because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.
translation: Umulandu Farao alotele iciloto cimo cine imiku ibili, nico Lesa cine cine napanga ukucita ici cintu, kabili takokole ukucicita.”

english: “Now therefore let Pharaoh look for a discreet and wise man, and set him over the land of Egypt.
translation: “Kanshi nomba Farao nafwaye umuntu uwacenjela kabili uwamano, amupeele amaka yakwangalila icalo conse ica Egupto.

english: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt’s produce in the seven plenteous years.
translation: Farao nasonte na bakangalila mu calo abakupoka icipande ca fisabo cimo pa fipande fisano fya fisabo bakalasombola mu myaka cine lubali ilyo kukaba ifisabo ifingi.

english: Let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and store grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.
translation: Farao abapeele amaka yakulonganika ifyakulya fya myaka iyi isuma no kututila iŋanu mu misumba umo bakalasungila ifyakulya.

english: The food will be to supply the land against the seven years of famine, which will be in the land of Egypt; so that the land will not perish through the famine.”
translation: Ifi fyakulya fyakubika mu matala ya misumba, fyakwisa mukubomfya mu myaka cine lubali iya cipowe ico cikapona pa calo ca Egupto. Epakuti icalo cikonaulwa ku cipowe.”

english: The thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
translation: Aya matontonkanyo yamoneke bwino kuli Farao na babomfi bakwe bonse.

english: Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?”
translation: Elyo Farao asosele ku babomfi bakwe ati, “Bushe ni kwi twingasanga umuntu uwaba ngoyu, umwaba umupashi wakwa Lesa?”

english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Because God has shown you all of this, there is no one so discreet and wise as you.
translation: Farao epakweba Yosefu ati, “Apo ni Lesa uulengele ukuti wishibe ifi fyonse, tapali muntu nelyo umo uwacenjela kabili uwamano nga iwe.

english: The ugly and thin cattle ate up the seven sleek and fat cattle. So Pharaoh awoke.
translation: Elyo iŋombe isho ishibi kabili ishaonda shalya iŋombe ishatuuluka kabili ishaina ubusaka. Awe Farao ashibuka mu tulo.

english: You shall be over my house. All my people will be ruled according to your word. Only in the throne I will be greater than you.”
translation: Kanshi niwe wine walaba cilolo mukalamba we sano lyandi, na bantu bandi bonse bakulabeela ifyo wabakonkomesha. Ninefye nakulakucilako ico ine ndi mfumu.”

english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Behold, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”
translation: Elyo Farao aebele Yosefu ati, “Kanshi nomba, ine niwe nasonta ukuba cilolo mukalamba wa calo conse ica Egupto.”

english: Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.
translation: Farao epakufuula imbalaminwe yakwe iyabufumu iyakufwatikilako, afwika na Yosefu ku munwe. Amufwika ne nsalu ishabuuta ubusaka kabili amufwika no munyololo wa golide mu mukoshi.

english: He made him ride in the second chariot which he had. They cried before him, “Bow the knee!” He set him over all the land of Egypt.
translation: Amuninika mwiceleta lyakwe ilyabubili nge nkonkani yakwe, na bantu bali pantanshi yakwe balepunda abati, “Mufukamineni!” Kanshi efyo amupeele amaka yakuba cilolo mukalamba wakwe uwa calo conse ica Egupto.

english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh. Without you, no man shall lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”
translation: Elyo Farao aebele Yosefu ati, “Ine nine Farao imfumu, lelo mu calo conse ica Egupto tamwakabe nelyo umo uwakucita cimo, ukwabula ukuti iwe usuminishe.”

english: Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-Paneah. He gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On as a wife. Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
translation: Farao ainika Yosefu ishina lya Sefenati Panea. Kabili apeela Yosefu umukashana Asenati umwana wakwa Potifera shimapepo wa ku Oni ukuti abe umukashi wakwe. Yosefu nao aya alepitana mu calo conse ica Egupto.

english: Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.
translation: Yosefu ali ne myaka amakumi yatatu (30) ilyo atampile ukulabombela Farao imfumu ya calo ca Egupto. Yosefu epakusha Farao aya aletandala mu calo conse ica Egupto.

english: In the seven plenteous years the earth produced abundantly.
translation: Mu myaka ilya cine lubali iya fisabo ifingi, umushili wameseshe ifisabo ifingi nganshi.

english: He gathered up all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities. He stored food in each city from the fields around that city.
translation: Yosefu alongenye ifyakulya fyonse ifyasombwelwe mu Egupto muli iyo myaka ya fisabo ifingi, afitutila mu misumba. Muli cila musumba atutilamo ifyakulya basombwele mu mabala yashingulwike uyo musumba.

english: Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting, for it was without number.
translation: Yosefu atutile iŋanu ishingi nganshi, shafulilefye kwati musensenga wa muli bemba. Shalifulishe icakuti aleka no kupenda ku mulandu wa bwingi.

english: He slept and dreamed a second time; and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, healthy and good.
translation: Kabili Farao apona mu tulo, alota iciloto na cimbi. Awe amona imisonso cine lubali iyaisulamo inseke ishisuma ishatuuluka ilemena pa lupimbili lumofye.

english: To Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.
translation: Ilyo imyaka ya cipowe tailaisa, Yosefu afyele abana babili abaume muli Asenati mwana Potifera, shimapepo wa ku Oni.

english: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, “For”, he said, “God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.”
translation: Yosefu ainike ibeli lyakwe ishina lya Manase nokusosa ati, “Pantu Lesa nalenga ukuti ndabe amacushi yandi yonse na kuli bonse aba mu ŋanda yakwa tata.”

english: The name of the second, he called Ephraim: “For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
translation: Cikonkebeli wena amwinike ishina lya Efulemu, nokusosa ati, “Pantu Lesa nalenga ukuti nsanduluke mu calo umo nalecula.”

english: The seven years of plenty, that were in the land of Egypt, came to an end.
translation: Cilya imyaka cine lubali iya fyakulya ifingi yapita,

english: The seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
translation: elyo imyaka cine lubali iya cipowe nayo yatampa ngefyo Yosefu asosele. Mu fyalo fyonse fimbi mwapona icipowe, lelo mu calo conse ica Egupto mwena ifyakulya emo fyali.

english: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”
translation: Cilya abena Egupto bonse batampa ukumfwa icipowe, abantu balalomba Farao ukuti abapeeleko ifyakulya. Elyo Farao aeba abena Egupto bonse ati, “Kabiyeni kuli Yosefu, mucite ifyo alemweba.”

english: The famine was over all the surface of the earth. Joseph opened all the store houses, and sold to the Egyptians. The famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
translation: Cilya icipowe cakumana icalo conse elyo Yosefu aisula amayanda yonse batutilemo iŋanu, alashitisha na ku bena Egupto pantu mu calo conse mwaponene icipowe icibi.

english: All countries came into Egypt, to Joseph, to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all the earth.
translation: Abantu mu fyalo fyonse nabo balaisa kukushita iŋanu kuli Yosefu pantu icipowe icibi caponene pesonde lyonse.

english: Behold, seven heads of grain, thin and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.
translation: Elyo panuma ulupimbili lwatwala imisonso imbi cine lubali, iyi yena yali iyapapa iyauminina ku mwela uwakaba uwa ku kabanga.

english: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven healthy and full ears. Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.
translation: Imisonso iyapapa yamina imisonso cine lubali iya nseke ishatuuluka ishisuma. Farao elyo ashibuka mu tulo, aishiba ukuti aciba alelotafye.

english: In the morning, his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all of Egypt’s magicians and wise men. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but there was no one who could interpret them to Pharaoh.
translation: Ulucelo Farao alifye uwasakamana. Kanshi epakwita abalecita amalele na bamano bonse mu Egupto. Farao abebako ifiloto alotele, lelo tapali nelyo umo uwakuti amwilwile.

english: Then the chief cup bearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my faults today.
translation: Elyo umukalamba wa bakatumika ba lukombo lwa mfumu aebele Farao ati, “Ilelo naibukisha ifyo nalufyanya.

english: Now Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you look at one another?”
translation: Ilyo Yakobo aumfwile ukuti mu Egupto mwena iŋanu emo shali, aebele bamwane abaume ati, “Bushe cinshi mwikalile muleloleshanyafye?

english: They said to him, “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.
translation: Nabo bamwasuka abati, “Iyoo shikulu, ifwe fwe babomfi bobe twishilefye kukushita ifyakulya.

english: We are all one man’s sons; we are honest men. Your servants are not spies.”
translation: Kabili ifwe bonse pano tuli bana ba muntufye umo. Fwe babomfi bobe tuli bantu bacishinka, tatuli nengu iyoo.”

english: He said to them, “No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land!”
translation: Imili 7:12

english: They said, “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is today with our father, and one is no more.”
translation: Bamwasuka abati, “Fwe babomfi bobe tuli bamunyina. Twaba ikumi limo na babili, abana abaume aba muntufye umo uwikala mu calo ca Kenani. Kasuli ena ali na shifwe, lelo umbi ena tabapo.”

english: Joseph said to them, “It is like I told you, saying, ‘You are spies!’
translation: Yosefu abeba ati, “Ala nifyo fine nandile ukuti imwe muli nengu.

english: By this you shall be tested. By the life of Pharaoh, you shall not go out from here, unless your youngest brother comes here.
translation: Kabili muleeshiwa muli ici cintu. Napali Farao umumi! Imwe tamwakafume kuno kano kasuli wenu akese kuno.

english: Send one of you, and let him get your brother, and you shall be bound, that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you, or else by the life of Pharaoh surely you are spies.”
translation: Tumenipo umo pali imwe uwakuya buula munyinenwe. Imwe bonse mulesungwa mu cifungo epakuti tumone nga ifyo mulelanda cine cine fyacishinka, lelo nga teifyo na pali Farao ninshi muli nengu.”

english: He put them all together into custody for three days.
translation: Elyo ababika mu cifungo pa nshiku shitatu.

english: Joseph said to them the third day, “Do this, and live, for I fear God.
translation: Pa bushiku bwalengele shitatu Yosefu abeba ati, “Citeni ici nga mube abomi, pantu ine naliba na katiina kuli Lesa.

english: If you are honest men, then let one of your brothers be bound in your prison; but you go, carry grain for the famine of your houses.
translation: Imwe nga muli bantu bacishinka, lekeni munyinenwe umo ashale kuno mu cifungo. Elyo imwe bambi bonse mubwelelemo, mutwale iŋanu ku ndupwa shenu ishili mu cipowe.

english: He said, “Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there, and buy for us from there, so that we may live, and not die.”
translation: Ine nalyumfwa ukuti mu Egupto mwena iŋanu emo shili. Kanshi eko muye, mukaye tushitilako shimo, epakuti tukabe abomi twikafwa ku nsala.”

english: Bring your youngest brother to me; so will your words be verified, and you won’t die.” They did so.
translation: Lelo muli nokuleta kasuli wenu kuli ine pakuti nkashininkishe amashiwi yenu, no kufwa ninshi tamwakafwe.” Awe nabo efyo bacita.

english: They said to one another, “We are certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he begged us, and we wouldn’t listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”
translation: Balalanshanya abati, “Cine cine tulekandilwa pa mulandu wakwa munyinefwe. Twalimwene ifyo ali no bulanda ilyo aletupapata ukuti twimulofya, lelo ifwe tatwamumfwile nakalya. E mulandu wine ili shamo litwishile.”

english: Reuben answered them, saying, “Didn’t I tell you, saying, ‘Don’t sin against the child,’ and you wouldn’t listen? Therefore also, behold, his blood is required.”
translation: Rubeni epakubeba ati, “Bushe nshamwebele ukuti mwicita mwaice cibi nelyo cimo? Lelo tamwateseshe nakalya. Awe nomba tuli nokukandwa pa mulandu wakumwipaya.”

english: They didn’t know that Joseph understood them; for there was an interpreter between them.
translation: Bamunyina bena tabaishibe ukuti Yosefu aletesha ifyo balelanda umo filolele, pantu pali uwalemwalwila ifyo balanda.

english: He turned himself away from them, and wept. Then he returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.
translation: Yosefu afuma apo bali, aya mukulila. Elyo kabili abwela uko bali, alalanda nabo. Afumya Simeoni apo bali, amukaka ninshi balemonako.

english: Then Joseph gave a command to fill their bags with grain, and to restore each man’s money into his sack, and to give them food for the way. So it was done to them.
translation: Yosefu akonkomeshe ukwisusha iŋanu mu mifuko ya bamunyina, no kubwesesha cila umo indalama shabo mu mufuko wakwe. Kabili akonkomesha ukubapeelako ifyakulya fya pa bulendo. Awe fyonse ifyo fyalicitilwe.

english: They loaded their donkeys with their grain, and departed from there.
translation: Bamunyina kwa Yosefu bakakila imifuko ya ŋanu pali bapunda babo, balaya nokuya.

english: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging place, he saw his money. Behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.
translation: Apo basendeme, umo pali bamunyina akakula umufuko wakwe pakuti abuulemo ifyakulisha punda wakwe, elyo amona indalama shakwe pa mulu wa ŋanu.

english: He said to his brothers, “My money is restored! Behold, it is in my sack!” Their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling to one another, saying, “What is this that God has done to us?”
translation: Aebele bamunyina ati, “Ine nabambwesesha indalama shandi, ishi shili pamulu mu mufuko.” Awe imitima yafuma, balaipushanya balekankafye ku mwenso abati, “Cinshi ici ico Lesa atucitila ifi?”

english: They came to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and told him all that had happened to them, saying,
translation: Ilyo bafikile kuli shibo Yakobo mu calo ca Kenani, bamushimikileko fyonse ifyabacitikile. Bamweba abati,

english: Joseph’s ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
translation: Kanshi bamunyina kwa Yosefu ikumi limo epakwima balaya ku Egupto kukushita iŋanu.

english: “The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly with us, and took us for spies of the country.
translation: “Umuntu uteeka icalo ca Egupto alandile kuli ifwe bukali bukali, atucitile kwati ifwe tuli nengu sha calo.

english: We said to him, ‘We are honest men. We are no spies.
translation: Lelo ifwe twamwebele twati, ‘Ifwe tuli bantu bacishinka, tatuli nengu iyoo.

english: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is today with our father in the land of Canaan.’
translation: Tuli bamunyina ikumi limo na babili (12) na shifwe umofye. Umo wena tabapo, elyo kasuli ali na shifwe mu calo ca Kenani.’

english: The man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I will know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, and take grain for the famine of your houses, and go your way.
translation: Elyo uyo muntu ateeka icalo ca Egupto atweba ati, ‘Pakuti njishibe ukuti muli bantu bacishinka, mulenshila munyinenwe kuno, elyo bambi musende iŋanu ku ndupwa shenu ishili mu cipowe, nokuya muleya.

english: Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you are not spies, but that you are honest men. So I will deliver your brother to you, and you shall trade in the land.’”
translation: Lelo muli nokuleta kuli ine munyinenwe kasuli wenu, lyena elyo nkeshiba ukuti tamuli nengu, muli bantu bacishinka. Elyo na ine nkamubwesesha munyinenwe, lyena kuti mwacita amakwebo muli cino calo.’”

english: As they emptied their sacks, behold, each man’s bundle of money was in his sack. When they and their father saw their bundles of money, they were afraid.
translation: Ilyo batampile ukufukumuna iŋanu mu mifuko yabo, cila muntu asangamo akafunda ka ndalama shakwe mu mufuko wakwe. Cilya shibo na bamwane bamona utufunda twa ndalama, awe baikatwa no mwenso.

english: Jacob, their father, said to them, “You have bereaved me of my children! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you want to take Benjamin away. All these things are against me.”
translation: Shibo Yakobo abeba ati, “Imwe namumpwila abana bandi. Yosefu tabapo, elyo na Simeoni nao talipo, kabili nomba mulefwaya ukusenda Benjamini. Fyonse nafimbipila!”

english: Reuben spoke to his father, saying, “Kill my two sons, if I don’t bring him to you. Entrust him to my care, and I will bring him to you again.”
translation: Elyo Rubeni aeba wishi ati, “Ine nga nshibweseshe Benjamini kuli imwe, ninshi mukepaye abana bandi abaume babili. Mubikeni mu minwe yandi, nkamubwesha kuli imwe.”

english: He said, “My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he only is left. If harm happens to him along the way in which you go, then you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.”
translation: Lelo Yakobo abeba ati, “Umwana wandi wena tamwakaye nankwe. Munyina alifwa, elyo uyu wine eka ewashalapo. Pantu nga aponena mu busanso pa bulendo bwenu ninshi nimwe mukalenga nkaya ku calo ca bafwa ne cikonko mu bukote bwandi.”

english: But Jacob didn’t send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with his brothers; for he said, “Lest perhaps harm happen to him.”
translation: Lelo Yakobo talekele Benjamini, umwaice wakwa Yosefu, ukuti aye na bamunyina. Aletiina ukuti epali icibi cimo camuponena.

english: The sons of Israel came to buy among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
translation: Kanshi bamwana Israeli pamo na bantu bambi balile kukushita iŋanu, pantu na mu Kenani mwine mwaliponene icipowe.

english: Joseph was the governor over the land. It was he who sold to all the people of the land. Joseph’s brothers came, and bowed themselves down to him with their faces to the earth.
translation: Nomba Yosefu ewapeelwe amaka yakuteeka icalo conse ica Egupto. Kanshi ewaleshitisha iŋanu ku bena Egupto bonse. Awe bamunyina kwa Yosefu ilyo bafika, bamufukamina, bakontamina panshi.

english: Joseph saw his brothers, and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them. He said to them, “Where did you come from?” They said, “From the land of Canaan, to buy food.”
translation: Cilya Yosefu abamona, abeshiba apopene, lelo acita kwati tabeshibe iyoo. Abalansha bukali bukali, abepusha ati, “Bushe imwe mwafuma kwi?” Bamwasuka abati, “Twafuma ku calo ca Kenani, twaisa kukushita ifyakulya.”

english: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they didn’t recognize him.
translation: Nangu Yosefu wena aishibe bamunyina, bena tabamwishibe iyoo.

english: Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed about them, and said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”
translation: Elyo Yosefu aibukisha ifiloto alotele pali bena, elyo abeba ati, “Muli nengu imwe! Mwishilefye kukulengula apakusanshila icalo cesu.”

english: The famine was severe in the land.
translation: Nomba icipowe calibipile nganshi mu calo ca Kenani.

english: for if we hadn’t delayed, surely we would have returned a second time by now.”
translation: Atukanashingashinga nga twaliyako no kubwelako imiku ibili.”

english: Their father, Israel, said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Take from the choice fruits of the land in your bags, and carry down a present for the man, a little balm, a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;
translation: Elyo shibo Israeli abeba ati, “Kanshi nga nifyo cili nokuba, ninshi mucite ifi. Mubuule ifintu ifyawamisha ifyo twakwata muli cino calo kuno, mubike mu mifuko yenu. Elyo mukafitwale ngo bupe kuli uyo muntu. Mukasende utumafuta twakupangilako umuti, utubuci, ifinyamuti ifyanunka ubusaka, amafuta yalesha ifitumbi ukubola muri, ne nseke sha kamuti ka pisitakio na ka alumondi.

english: and take double money in your hand, and take back the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.
translation: Musende indalama ishakushitamo, elyo ne shakubweseshamo pali shilya babikile mu mifuko yenu, limbi balufyenyefye.

english: Take your brother also, get up, and return to the man.
translation: Sendeni na munyinenwe muleya nombaline ukuli uyo muntu.

english: May God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. If I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.”
translation: Lesa Umwine wa maka yonse enganasha uyo muntu ku mutima akamukwatile uluse, akaleke mukabwele na ulya munyinenwe umbi elyo na Benjamini. Kwena nga efyo ndi nokufwilwa, kacikabe ifyo fine.”

english: The men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and got up, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
translation: Kanshi bamwana Yakobo balisendele ifyabupe, indalama shakushitamo ne shakubweseshamo, kabili basendele na Benjamini wine. Baima balaya ku Egupto, baya ituula na kuli Yosefu.

english: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and prepare; for the men will dine with me at noon.”
translation: Cilya Yosefu amona ukuti Benjamini ali nabo, aeba kasunga wa ŋanda yakwe ati, “Senda aba bantu kumwandi. Wipayepo inama imo wipike. Aba bantu tulelya nabo akasuba.”

english: The man did as Joseph commanded, and the man brought the men to Joseph’s house.
translation: Awe umubomfi acita ngefyo Yosefu amwebele, atwala na bantu ku ŋanda kwa Yosefu.

english: The men were afraid, because they were brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, “Because of the money that was returned in our sacks the first time, we’re brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”
translation: Kanshi abo bantu epakwikatwa no mwenso ico babatwala ku ŋanda kwa Yosefu. Bena balatontonkanya abati, “Ico batuletela kuno, mulandu wa ndalama shilya babikile mu mifuko yesu pa bulendo bwakubalilapo. Alefwaya ukuti atucimfye, atwikate, atucite abasha bakwe, elyo abuule na bapunda besu.”

english: They came near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and they spoke to him at the door of the house,
translation: Kanshi epakuya kuli kasunga wa ŋanda yakwa Yosefu, balanda nao ilyo bacili pa mwinshi wa ŋanda.

english: When they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again, buy us a little more food.”
translation: Kanshi ilyo bapwile ukulya iŋanu baile shita ku Egupto, shibo Yakobo abebele ati, “Kabiyeni nakabili, muye tushitilako utwakulya na tumbi.”

english: and said, “Oh, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.
translation: Bamweba abati, “Twapapata mukwai, ifwe twalishile kuno kale kukushita ifyakulya.

english: When we came to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and behold, each man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. We have brought it back in our hand.
translation: Lelo apo twasendeme, ilyo twakakwile imifuko yesu, cila muntu asangile indalama shakwe shonse apo shapelele mu mufuko wakwe pa mulu wa ŋanu. Kanshi natushibwesha, tuli nasho.

english: We have brought down other money in our hand to buy food. We don’t know who put our money in our sacks.”
translation: Kabili natwisa na shimbi ishakushitamo icakulya. Tatwaishiba uwabikile indalama shesu mu mifuko yesu.”

english: He said, “Peace be to you. Don’t be afraid. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your money.” He brought Simeon out to them.
translation: Umubomfi wakwa Yosefu ati, “Tekeni imitima, mwitiina. Lesa wenu, Lesa wakwa shinwe, ewamupeele isho ndalama mu mifuko yenu. Ine nalipokele indalama mwampeele.” Elyo aya fumya Simeoni amuleta kuli bamunyina.

english: The man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet. He gave their donkeys fodder.
translation: Kasunga wa ŋanda abuulile abo bantu no kubengisha mu ŋanda yakwa Yosefu. Abapeela amenshi yakusamba amakasa, elyo apeela bapunda babo icakulya.

english: They prepared the present for Joseph’s coming at noon, for they heard that they should eat bread there.
translation: Bamunyina bapekanya ubupe bwabo ubwakwisa peela Yosefu nga aisa ilyo akasuba kaba pakati ka mutwe. Pantu balyumfwile ukuti bali nokulya kulya kwine.

english: When Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves down to the earth before him.
translation: Cilya Yosefu aisa mumwakwe, bamunyina bamupeela ifyabupe ifyo baishile nafyo mu ŋanda, elyo bamukontamina no kumukontamina.

english: He asked them of their welfare, and said, “Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he yet alive?”
translation: Yosefu abepusha nga bali umutende, elyo atila, “Nga shinwe umukote mwanjebeleko, bushe ali umutende? Bushe ali umumi?”

english: They said, “Your servant, our father, is well. He is still alive.” They bowed down humbly.
translation: Nabo bamwasuka abati, “Ee, shifwe umubomfi wenu acili umumi kabili ali umutende.” Awe bamukontamina nganshi pakulanga umucinshi.

english: He lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin, his brother, his mother’s son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” He said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”
translation: Ilyo alebalolesha, amona Benjamini munyina uo afyelwe nao inda imo. Abepusha ati, “Bushe uyu e munyinenwe kasuli, ulya mwanjebeleko?” Elyo aeba Benjamini ati, “Lesa akupaale mwana wandi.”

english: Judah spoke to him, saying, “The man solemnly warned us, saying, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’
translation: Lelo Yuda amweba ati, “Ulya muntu alitukonkomeshe ati, ‘Tatwakamonane na imwe nga tamwishile na munyinenwe.’

english: Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.
translation: Ico amona munyina, Yosefu aumfwa icikonko, bwangu bwangu afumapo aya alefwaya incende ukwakulilila. Awe aya ku muputule wakwe eko alalilila.

english: He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “Serve the meal.”
translation: Panuma yakusamba pa menso, afuma ashipikisha, asosa nokuti, “Leteni icakulya.”

english: They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because the Egyptians don’t eat with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
translation: Yosefu bamutwalila ifyakulya eka, na bamunyina nabo beka, na bena Egupto abalelya nankwe nabo babatwalila icakulya beka, pantu abena Egupto tabafwaya nelyo panono kulya pamo na Bahibulu, cintu ico bapata.

english: They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marveled with one another.
translation: Bamunyina babateka pantanshi yakwa Yosefu. Baikala ukukonka umo bafyalilwe, ukufuma kwibeli ukufika na kuli kasuli. Elyo bamunyina baloleshanya, bapapa pakumona ifyo baikala.

english: He sent portions to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as any of theirs. They drank, and were merry with him.
translation: Icakulya balabapeela ukufuma kwitebulo lyakwa Yosefu. Ifyakulya bapeele Benjamini fyali ifingi imiku isano ukucila umuntu onse umbi. Kanshi balya no kunwa, basansamuka pamo na Yosefu.

english: If you’ll send our brother with us, we’ll go down and buy you food;
translation: Kanshi nga cakuti mwaleka munyinefwe aye na ifwe, lyena tuleya kukumushitilako icakulya.

english: but if you don’t send him, we won’t go down, for the man said to us, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’”
translation: Lelo nga tamulekele ukuti aye na ifwe, awe ninshi na ifwe tatwaye. Pantu ulya muntu atwebele ati, ‘Tatwakese monana na imwe, kano mwaisa na munyinenwe.’”

english: Israel said, “Why did you treat me so badly, telling the man that you had another brother?”
translation: Israeli epakubepusha ati, “Nga cinshi mwambikila mu bucushi pakweba uyo muntu ukuti mwalikwata munyinenwe na umbi?”

english: They said, “The man asked directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?’ We just answered his questions. Is there any way we could know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother down’?”
translation: Bamwasuka abati, “Ala uyo muntu, mwinefye wabikilepo ukutwipusha pali ifwe bene na pa lupwa lwesu. Atwipwishe ati, ‘Bushe shinwe epo acili? Bushe mwalikwatapo na munyinenwe na umbi?’ Kanshi ifwe twayaswikefye ifyo atwipwishe. Bushe nga kuti twaishiba shani ukuti aletweba ati, ‘Mukalete munyinenwe kuno?’”

english: Judah said to Israel, his father, “Send the boy with me, and we’ll get up and go, so that we may live, and not die, both we, and you, and also our little ones.
translation: Elyo Yuda aeba Israeli wishi ati, “Lekeni kanshi nine nsende umwaice, kabili twalaimafye nombaline, pakuti imwe na ifwe na bana besu tube abomi, twifwa ku cipowe.

english: I’ll be collateral for him. From my hand will you require him. If I don’t bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever;
translation: Ine ne mwine nkasakamana ukusunga ubumi bwakwe. Muli nokubika umulandu wa pali Benjamini pali ine. Nga nshimubweseshe kuli imwe, no kumuteka apa pa cinso cenu, ninshi nkaba no mulandu kuli imwe inshiku shonse isha bumi bwandi.

english: He commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in his sack’s mouth.
translation: Elyo Yosefu akonkomeshe kasunga wa ŋanda yakwe ati, “Buula imifuko ya aba bantu, wisushemo ifyakulya ukulingana na papelele amaka yabo ayakufisenda. Kabili ubike indalama shakwa cila muntu lwa pa mulu wa fyakulya mu mufuko wakwe.

english: He said, “Now also let it be according to your words. He with whom it is found will be my slave; and you will be blameless.”
translation: Kasunga wa iŋanda yakwa Yosefu asosa ati, “Cisuma kacibe ifyo fine mwalanda. Lelo uo ndesanga no lukombo, euleba umusha wandi, bambi bonse tababe na mulandu.”

english: Then they hurried, and each man took his sack down to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
translation: Bwangu bwangu cila muntu atuula umufuko wakwe panshi, no kukakula akakulapo.

english: He searched, beginning with the oldest, and ending at the youngest. The cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
translation: Elyo kasunga wa ŋanda yakwa Yosefu atampa ukulafwailisha, atampilapo umufuko wa mukalamba pali bonse alekeleshako umufuko wakwa kasuli. Asanga ulukombo mu mufuko wakwa Benjamini.

english: Then they tore their clothes, and each man loaded his donkey, and returned to the city.
translation: Pakumona ifi bamunyina balepula insalu shabo. Elyo babike ifipe pali bapunda babo, babwelela na ku musumba.

english: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, and he was still there. They fell on the ground before him.
translation: Ilyo Yuda na bamunyina babwelele ku ŋanda, basangile Yosefu acili mu ŋanda. Awe bonse balambalala panshi pa cinso cakwe.

english: Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Don’t you know that such a man as I can indeed do divination?”
translation: Yosefu abepusha ati, “Cinshi ici mwacita? Bushe tamwishibe ukuti umuntu uuli nga ine kuti aishiba mukupendula.”

english: Judah said, “What will we tell my lord? What will we speak? How will we clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are my lord’s slaves, both we and he also in whose hand the cup is found.”
translation: Yuda ayasuka ati, “Nga finshi twingalanda shikulu? Finshi twingasosapo? Nga kuti twatila tatuli na cilubo shani? Lesa nasokolola icilubo ca babomfi benu. Ifwe bonse nomba tuli basha benu, ifwe bene bonse noyu wine basangileko ulukombo.”

english: He said, “Far be it from me that I should do so. The man in whose hand the cup is found, he will be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.”
translation: Lelo Yosefu ayasuka ati, “Awe ico cena ine tekuti ncicite! Umuntu wine uyo uo basangile nakwata ulukombo, ewalaba umusha wandi. Imwe bambi bonse bwelelenimo kuli shinwe umutende.”

english: Then Judah came near to him, and said, “Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and don’t let your anger burn against your servant; for you are even as Pharaoh.
translation: Elyo Yuda aile palama kuli Yosefu amweba ati, “Napapata shikulu kutikeni bwino kufyo umubomfi wenu alalanda. Mwifulilwa mubomfi wenu, nangu imwe mwalinganafye na Farao umwine wine.

english: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father, or a brother?’
translation: Shikulu nimwe mwaipwishe ababomfi benu amuti ‘Bushe mwalikwata shinwe nangu munyinenwe umbi?’

english: Put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, with his grain money.” He did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
translation: Elyo ubike ulukombo lwandi, lulya ulwa silifa, mu mufuko wakwa kasuli. Ulubike lwa pa mulu wa fyakulya pamo ne ndalama shakwe ishakushitamo iŋanu.” Nao acita fyonse ngefyo Yosefu amwebele.

english: We said to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.’
translation: Elyo ifwe twayaswike atuti, ‘Twalikwata shifwe, nomba mukote, elyo na munyinefwe umbi umwaice umwaume uo shifwe afyele mu bukote. Munyina wa uyu mwaice alifwa nomba ashalapofye eka pali bamunyina abaume afyelwe nabo inda imo. Kabili wishi alimutemwa nganshi.’

english: You said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.’
translation: Kabili nimwe mwaebele ababomfi benu amuti, ‘Mukamulete kuli ine pakuti na ine nkese mumona.’

english: We said to my lord, ‘The boy can’t leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’
translation: Elyo ifwe shikulu twamwebele atuti, ‘Uyo mwaice tekuti afume pali bawishi, pantu nga afumapo kuti bawishi bafwa.’

english: You said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will see my face no more.’
translation: Lelo mwaebele ababomfi benu amuti, ‘Nga cakuti tamwishile na munyinenwe kasuli ninshi tatwakamonane na imwe nakabili.’

english: When we came up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
translation: Ilyo twabwelelemo kuli shifwe, umubomfi wenu, twaile mushimikilako ifyo imwe shikulu mwalandile.

english: Our father said, ‘Go again and buy us a little food.’
translation: “Kabili shifwe aishile tweba ati, ‘Bwelelenimo muye shitako na tumbi utwakulya.’

english: We said, ‘We can’t go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down: for we may not see the man’s face, unless our youngest brother is with us.’
translation: Lelo ifwe twamwebele ukuti, ‘Awe iyoo, tekuti tuyeko, kanofye ninshi nga tuli na munyinefwe kasuli, lyena tuleyako. Pantu tatwakaye monana na ulya muntu kanofye tuli na munyinefwe kasuli.’

english: Your servant, my father, said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.
translation: Kabili umubomfi wenu, shifwe atwebele ati, ‘Namwishiba ukuti umukashi wandi amfyalilefye abana abaume babili epela.

english: One went out from me, and I said, “Surely he is torn in pieces;” and I haven’t seen him since.
translation: Umo tatwaba nankwe aliya. Ine nasosele nati cine cine ciswango ca mpanga ecimulepawile. Ukufuma ilyo line nshatala mumona.

english: If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.’
translation: Nga cakuti nao mwamusenda, elyo aponena mu busanso, ninshi nimwe mukalenga nkaya ku calo ca bafwa ne cikonko mu bukote bwandi.’

english: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
translation: Cilya bwaca ulucelo babaleka balaya na bapunda babo.

english: Now therefore when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us; since his life is bound up in the boy’s life;
translation: “Kanshi nomba nga cakuti nabwelelemo kuli batata umubomfi wenu no mwaice tatuli nankwe, kabili nga cakuti batata bakamona ukuti tatuli na mwaice, ninshi bakafwafye apopene.

english: it will happen, when he sees that the boy is no more, that he will die. Your servants will bring down the gray hairs of your servant, our father, with sorrow to Sheol.
translation: Pantu batata no mwaice balikatana nganshi mu bumi bwabo, ninshi ifwe fwe babomfi benu tukalenga shifwe akaye ku calo ca bafwa ne cikonko mu bukote bwakwe.

english: For your servant became collateral for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I don’t bring him to you, then I will bear the blame to my father forever.’
translation: Ne mubomfi wenu nalaile kuli batata ukuti te cakutwishika nkabwesha umwaice umumi. Nasosele nati, ‘Nga cakuti nshimubweseshe kuli imwe, ninshi nkaba no mulandu kuli imwe tata wandi inshiku shonse isha bumi bwandi.’

english: Now therefore, please let your servant stay instead of the boy, my lord’s slave; and let the boy go up with his brothers.
translation: Eico nomba napapata, lekeni ne mubomfi wenu nshale umusha wenu shikulu mu cifulo ca mwaice pakuti wena abwelelemo na bamunyina.

english: For how will I go up to my father, if the boy isn’t with me?—lest I see the evil that will come on my father.”
translation: Nga ine kuti nabwekelamo shani kuli batata nga nshili na mwaice? Awe iyoo! Mwikaleka nkamoneko ubulanda bukeshila batata.”

english: When they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, “Up, follow after the men. When you overtake them, ask them, ‘Why have you rewarded evil for good?
translation: Kutifye cilya baya, tabalati bafike ukutali no musumba, Yosefu aeba kasunga wa ŋanda yakwe ati, “Ima konka balya bantu nombalinefye. Ilyo ulebasanga ubebe auti, ‘Bushe cinshi mwancitila ifibi pa fisuma mucitile?

english: Isn’t this that from which my lord drinks, and by which he indeed divines? You have done evil in so doing.’”
translation: Cinshi mwaibila ulukombo lwandi ulwa silifa? Bushe lulya lukombo telo shikulu wandi anwenamo no kupendwilamo? Ici cintu mwacita cibi.’”

english: He overtook them, and he spoke these words to them.
translation: Kanshi ilyo umubomfi abasangile nao abebele aya yene mashiwi.

english: They said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants that they should do such a thing!
translation: Nabo bamweba abati, “Shikulu bushe cinshi mwalandila ifyo? Awe cakaana, ababomfi benu tekuti bacite ica musango uyo!

english: Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks’ mouths, we brought again to you out of the land of Canaan. How then should we steal silver or gold out of your lord’s house?
translation: Moneni, twaendele ukufuma ku Kenani twamubwesesha indalama twasangile pa mulu wa ŋanu mu mifuko. Bushe cinshi ico twingebila silifa nangu golide mu ŋanda ya basokulu?

english: With whomever of your servants it is found, let him die, and we also will be my lord’s slaves.”
translation: Kanshi nga cakuti umo pali ifwe, fwe babomfi benu, nga asangwa nakwata ulukombo ninshi ali nokufwa. Elyo na ifwe bonse tukaba abasha bakwa shikulu.”

english: Then Joseph couldn’t control himself before all those who stood before him, and he called out, “Cause everyone to go out from me!” No one else stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
translation: Kanshi Yosefu asukile afilwa ukushipikisha pa cinso ca bantu abalemubombela. Elyo aikatisha ishiwi ati, “Bonse abali muno bafumemo.” Kanshi tamwali nelyo umo na Yosefu ilyo aisokolwele kuli bamunyina.

english: You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you will be near to me, you, your children, your children’s children, your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.
translation: Mukesa ikala mu mpanga ya Gosheni. Kabili mukabafye mupepi na ine, imwe bene, abana benu na beshikulu benu, impaanga ne mbushi shenu, iŋombe shenu na fyonsefye ifyo mwakwata.

english: There I will provide for you; for there are yet five years of famine; lest you come to poverty, you, and your household, and all that you have.”’
translation: Nine wine nkalamufwaila ifyakulya mu Gosheni pantu kucili na imbi imyaka isano iya cipowe iyili nokwisa. Pantu nga teifyo ninshi imwe na bantu muli nabo ne fitekwa fyenu fyonse mukaponena mu bupina.’

english: Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
translation: “Awe mwaimwena mwe bene, na iwe munyinane Benjamini waimwena, ukuti icine cine nine Yosefu ne ulelanda na imwe.

english: You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my father down here.”
translation: Imili 7:13

english: He fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
translation: Imili 7:14

english: He kissed all his brothers, and wept on them. After that his brothers talked with him.
translation: Kabili Yosefu alatomona bamunyina pakubaposha, ninshi alelila nokulila. Panuma ya ifi elyo bamunyina balanda nankwe.

english: The report of it was heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” It pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.
translation: Ilyo ilyashi lyafikile kwisano kwa Farao ukuti bamunyina bakwa Yosefu nabesa, Farao na bacilolo bakwe bonse balisansamwike.

english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do this: Load your animals, and go, travel to the land of Canaan.
translation: Farao epakweba Yosefu ati, “Webe bamunonko auti, ‘Mucite ifi. Twikeni inama shenu ifipe mubwelelemo ku calo ca Kenani.

english: Take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.’
translation: Mukaye buula bawiso ne ndupwa shenu, mukabalete kuno. Ine nkesa mupeela impanga yawamisha muno mu Egupto elyo mukaleipakisha ku fisabo ifisuma fya muno calo.’

english: Now you are commanded to do this: Take wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.
translation: Kabili ubakonkomeshe nokuti, ‘Sendeni amaceleta ya muno Egupto pakusendelamo abana benu na bakashi benu. Kabili mukasende shinwe nokwisa kuno.

english: He wept aloud. The Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.
translation: Kabili alikatishe nganshi pakulila icakuti na bena Egupto balyumfwile uko alelila. Neci cintu casukile caumfwika na kwisano kwa Farao.

english: Also, don’t concern yourselves about your belongings, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.”
translation: Mwikasakamana pa fipe fyenu mukasha, pantu fyonse ifyawamisha mu calo conse ica Egupto fikaba fyenu.’”

english: The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.
translation: Kanshi bamwana Israeli nabo efyo bacitile. Yosefu abapeele amaceleta ngefyo Farao akonkomeshe. Kabili abapeele ne fyakulya pa bulendo.

english: He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
translation: Yosefu apeele cila muntu icakufwala icipya, lelo Benjamini wena amupeele indalama sha silifa imyanda itatu (300) ne fyakufwala ifipya fisano.

english: He sent the following to his father: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provision for his father by the way.
translation: Wishi ena amutumine bapunda ikumi limo abamusendele ifintu ifyawamisha ifya mu calo ca Egupto, elyo na bapunda abakota ikumi abasendele iŋanu, imikate ne fyakulya fimbi ifya pa bulendo.

english: So he sent his brothers away, and they departed. He said to them, “See that you don’t quarrel on the way.”
translation: Elyo Yosefu abaleka ukuti baleya. Cilya balaya abeba ati, “Mwilaumana mu nshila!”

english: They went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
translation: Kanshi balimine bafuma mu Egupto baisa kuli shibo Yakobo mu calo ca Kenani.

english: They told him, saying, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” His heart fainted, for he didn’t believe them.
translation: Elyo baeba shibo abati, “Ala Yosefu epo acili umumi! Kabili euteeka ne calo conse ica Egupto.” Yakobo asunguka, afilwa nokusumina ifyo bamweba.

english: They told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them. When he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob, their father, revived.
translation: Lelo ilyo bamweba fyonse ifyo Yosefu abebele, kabili amona na maceleta Yosefu atumine ayakumutwala ku Egupto, lyena umutima wakwa shibo Yakobo waikala.

english: Israel said, “It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”
translation: Elyo Israeli asosa ati, “Nashininkisha kanshi! Umwana wandi Yosefu acili umumi. Ndifye nokuya mumona ilyo nshilafwa.”

english: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Does my father still live?” His brothers couldn’t answer him; for they were terrified at his presence.
translation: Elyo Yosefu aeba bamunyina ati, “Nine Yosefu! Bushe batata bacili abomi?” Lelo bamunyina baikatwa no mwenso pakumumona, bafilwa nokumwasuka.

english: Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” They came near. He said, “I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
translation: Elyo Yosefu aeba bamunyina ati, “Palameni kuno.” Awe bamupalama. Elyo asosa ati, “Nine Yosefu munyinenwe uo mwashitishe ku Egupto.

english: Now don’t be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
translation: Nomba mwiba na bulanda, kabili mwiifulilwa mwe bene pali ico mwanshitishe bandeta kuno, pantu ni Lesa ewantangishe pakuti mpusushe ubumi bwa bantu.

english: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in which there will be no plowing and no harvest.
translation: Nomba imyaka yaba ibili iya cipowe mu calo, kabili kushele imyaka imbi isano iyo kushakabe kulima nelyo ukusombola.

english: God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant in the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.
translation: Lelo Lesa antumine ukumutangilila pakumupusushishako ku cipowe abakashala pano isonde, elyo no kupususha ubumi bwenu apakalamba.

english: So now it wasn’t you who sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
translation: Kanshi teimwe mwandetele kuno iyoo, ni Lesa. Lesa alincita cilolo wakupanda Farao amano, mushika wa kwisano lyakwe lyonse na kateeka wa calo conse ica Egupto.

english: Hurry, and go up to my father, and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says, “God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me. Don’t wait.
translation: “Kanshi kabiyeni bwangu bwangu kuli batata, muli nokuya beba amuti, ‘Umwana wenu Yosefu aleti, Lesa alincita kateeka wa calo conse ica Egupto. Kanshi mwise kuno ndi, mwikokola.

english: Israel traveled with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.
translation: Kanshi Israeli alimine asenda na fyonse ifyo akwete. Ilyo afikile ku Beresheba atuula amalambo kuli Lesa wakwa Isaki wishi.

english: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation: Bamwana Simeoni abaume ni Yemueli, Yamini, Ohadi, Yakini, Sohari

english: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
translation: Bamwana Levi abaume ni Geshoni, Koati na Merari.

english: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
translation: Bamwana Yuda abaume ni Ere, Onani, Shela, Peresi na Sera,

english: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.
translation: Bamwana Isaka abaume, ni Tola, Pua, Yashubu na Shimuroni.

english: The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
translation: Bamwana Sebuloni abaume ni Seredi, Eloni na Yaleeli.

english: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, with his daughter Dinah. All the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.
translation: Imili 17:15

english: The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
translation: Bamwana Gadi abaume, ni Sefoni, Hagi, Shuni, Esiboni, Eri, Arodi na Areli.

english: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah their sister. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
translation: Bamwana Asheri abaume ni Imina, Ishifa, Ishifi na Beriya, elyo nkashi yabo ni Sera.

english: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob, even sixteen souls.
translation: Aba e bana na beshikulu abakwa Yakobo na Silipa. Silipa eulya musha Labani apeele kuli mwane Leya. Bonse pamo bali ikumi limo na mutanda (16).

english: The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
translation: Yosefu na Benjamini e bana abaume bakwa Rakeli umukashi wakwa Yakobo.

english: God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, “Jacob, Jacob!” He said, “Here I am.”
translation: Elyo ubushiku mu cimonwa Lesa alandile kuli Israeli ati, “Yakobo, Yakobo!” Nao ayasuka ati, “Epo ndi.”

english: To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.
translation: Mu calo ca Egupto, Yosefu afyele abana abaume babili, Manase na Efulemu muli Asenati mwana Potifera shimapepo wa ku Oni.

english: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
translation: Bamwana Benjamini abaume, ni Bela, Bekeri, Ashibeli, Gera, Namani,

english: These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.
translation: Aba e bana abaume na beshikulupo abakwa Rakeli na Yakobo. Bonse pamo bali ikumi limo na bane (14).

english: The son of Dan: Hushim.
translation: Mwana Dani umwaume, ni Hushimu.

english: The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation: Bamwana Naftali abaume, ni Yaseeli, Guni, Yesa na Shilemu.

english: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob: all the souls were seven.
translation: Aba e bana abaume na beshikulu abakwa Yakobo na Bilua. Bilua eulya musha Labani apeele kuli mwane Rakeli. Bonse bali pamo cine lubali.

english: All the souls who came with Jacob into Egypt, who were his direct offspring, in addition to Jacob’s sons’ wives, all the souls were sixty-six.
translation: Kanshi aba mu lupwa lwakwa Yakobo, emukuti bamwane na beshikulu bakwe abo aile nabo ku Egupto ukwabula ukupendelako abakashi ba bana bakwe, bali bonse pamo amakumi mutanda na mutanda (66).

english: The sons of Joseph, who were born to him in Egypt, were two souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob, who came into Egypt, were seventy.
translation: Yosefu afyele abana abaume babili mu Egupto. Kanshi bonse pamo, ba lupwa lwakwa Yakobo abaile ku Egupto, bali amakumi cine lubali (70).

english: Jacob sent Judah before him to Joseph, to show the way before him to Goshen, and they came into the land of Goshen.
translation: Nomba Yakobo atangishe Yuda kuli Yosefu pakuti abatangilile mu nshila ya ku Gosheni. Ilyo bafikile mu mpanga ya Gosheni,

english: Joseph prepared his chariot, and went up to meet Israel, his father, in Goshen. He presented himself to him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.
translation: Yosefu apekanye iceleta lyakwe, aima kukwisa kumanya wishi Israeli ku Gosheni. Kutifye cilya afika pali wishi, Yosefu akumbatila wishi, alalila no kulila pa nshita ikalamba.

english: He said, “I am God, the God of your father. Don’t be afraid to go down into Egypt, for there I will make of you a great nation.
translation: Lesa amweba ati, “Nine Lesa, Lesa wakwa wiso. Witiina ukuya ku Egupto, pantu eko nkakulenga ukabe umushobo ukalamba.

english: Israel said to Joseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive.”
translation: Israeli aeba Yosefu ati, “Awe nomba kuti nafwa, apo naimwena ukuti ucili umumi.”

english: Joseph said to his brothers, and to his father’s house, “I will go up, and speak with Pharaoh, and will tell him, ‘My brothers, and my father’s house, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
translation: Elyo Yosefu aebele bamunyina na ba mu ŋanda yakwa wishi ati, “Ine nalaya kuli Farao nje mweba nati, ‘Bamunyinane na ba mu ŋanda ya batata, abaleikala mu calo ca Kenani, nabesa kuli ine.

english: These men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock, and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.’
translation: Aba bantu ni bakacema balateka ifitekwa. Kanshi beshile ne mpaanga ne mbushi, iŋombe na fyonse fintu bakwata.’

english: It will happen, when Pharaoh summons you, and will say, ‘What is your occupation?’
translation: Ilyo Farao akamwita, nga aipusha ati, ‘Mulimo nshi mubomba?’

english: that you shall say, ‘Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we, and our fathers:’ that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.”
translation: Mukasuke amuti, ‘Ukufumafye ku bwaice ababomfi bobe bateka ifitekwa ngefyo ifikolwe fyabo fyalecita.’ Elyo lyena akamusuminisha ukwikala mu mpanga ya Gosheni. Pantu bakacema bonse balipatwa ku bena Egupto.”

english: I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph’s hand will close your eyes.”
translation: Ine nkaya nobe ku Egupto kabili nine wine nkakubwesesha muli cino calo. Elyo kabili ni Yosefu wine eukakonga pakufwa.”

english: Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob, their father, their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
translation: Elyo Yakobo afumine ku Beresheba. Bamwana Israeli abaume baninika Yakobo na bana babo na bakashi babo mu maceleta Farao atumine kukwisa basenda.

english: They took their livestock, and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt—Jacob, and all his offspring with him,
translation: Basendela kumo ne fitekwa fyabo ne fyuma banonkele mu calo ca Kenani. Yakobo epakuya ku Egupto pamo no lupwa lwakwe lonse.

english: his sons, and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and he brought all his offspring with him into Egypt.
translation: Akukile ku Egupto pamo na bamwane abaume na beshikulu abaume, abana bakwe abanakashi na beshikulu abanakashi, kanshi emukuti ulupwa lwakwe lonsefye.

english: These are the names of the children of Israel, who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.
translation: Aya e mashina ya bena Israeli, Yakobo no lupwa lwakwe, abakukile ku Egupto.

english: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation: Abana abaume abakwa Rubeni, ni Hanoki, Palu, Hesroni na Kami.

english: Then Joseph went in and told Pharaoh, and said, “My father and my brothers, with their flocks, their herds, and all that they own, have come out of the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.”
translation: Kanshi Yosefu aile kuli Farao amweba ati, “Batata na bamunyinane nabesa ukufuma ku calo ca Kenani. Beshile ne mikuni ya mpaanga, imbushi ne ŋombe pamo ne fintu fyabo fyonse. Bali nomba ku Gosheni.”

english: Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from the presence of Pharaoh.
translation: Elyo Yakobo apaala Farao, afumako, aya nokuya.

english: Joseph placed his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
