english: so that they go around naked without clothing. Being hungry, they carry the sheaves.
translation: Balenga abalanda ukwenda ubwamba ukwabula ifyakufwala,

english: They make oil within the walls of these men. They tread wine presses, and suffer thirst.
translation: Abalanda ebengela bambi amafuta ya miolifa no kulabakamina umwangashi,

english: From out of the populous city, men groan. The soul of the wounded cries out, yet God doesn’t regard the folly.
translation: Mu musumba muleumfwika ukuteta kwa bantu abalefwa,

english: “These are of those who rebel against the light. They don’t know its ways, nor stay in its paths.
translation: “Eko bali abantu babi bambi abashifwaya ulubuuto,

english: The murderer rises with the light. He kills the poor and needy. In the night he is like a thief.
translation: Icipondo cima ubushiku,

english: The eye also of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying, ‘No eye will see me.’ He disguises his face.
translation: Ilinso lya wabulalelale lilolela pali muntungulya,

english: In the dark they dig through houses. They shut themselves up in the daytime. They don’t know the light.
translation: Aba bantu bashifwaya ulubuuto,

english: For the morning is to all of them like thick darkness, for they know the terrors of the thick darkness.
translation: Imfifi e cibusa wabo, kwati kasuba kuli bena,

english: “They are foam on the surface of the waters. Their portion is cursed in the earth. They don’t turn into the way of the vineyards.
translation: “Lelo abantu babi balasendwa ne lyeshi lya menshi,

english: Drought and heat consume the snow waters, so does Sheol those who have sinned.
translation: Nga filya icikabilila ne cilala cikamya ubunga bwa mfula ,

english: There are people who remove the landmarks. They violently take away flocks, and feed them.
translation: Ababi balasesha impopo sha mipaka,

english: The womb will forget him. The worm will feed sweetly on him. He will be no more remembered. Unrighteousness will be broken as a tree.
translation: Nyina uwamufyala asuka alabako,

english: He devours the barren who don’t bear. He shows no kindness to the widow.
translation: Pantu abantu babi balacusha iŋumba ishishakwata abana,

english: Yet God preserves the mighty by his power. He rises up who has no assurance of life.
translation: Lelo Lesa ku bulamba bwakwe alonaula abamaka,

english: God gives them security, and they rest in it. His eyes are on their ways.
translation: Limo Lesa alaleka abantu babi baikalafye umutende,

english: They are exalted; yet a little while, and they are gone. Yes, they are brought low, they are taken out of the way as all others, and are cut off as the tops of the ears of grain.
translation: Ababi balacindama pa kashita akanono,

english: If it isn’t so now, who will prove me a liar, and make my speech worth nothing?”
translation: Bushe kwena nga cakuti teifyo fine,

english: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless, and they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.
translation: Balasenda bapunda wa bakashiwa,

english: They turn the needy out of the way. The poor of the earth all hide themselves.
translation: Mu nshila balatamfulamo abapina,

english: Behold, as wild donkeys in the desert, they go out to their work, seeking diligently for food. The wilderness yields them bread for their children.
translation: Abapina balafumina mu mpanga kwati ni bapunda ba mpanga abaikala mu matololo,

english: They cut their food in the field. They glean the vineyard of the wicked.
translation: Baya mukulaseepa ifyakulya mu mabala,

english: They lie all night naked without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.
translation: Ubushiku aba balanda basendamafye ubwamba,

english: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for lack of a shelter.
translation: Imfula ya mu mpili ilabaloka,

english: There are those who pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor,
translation: “Abantu babi bapokolola utwana twanshiwa ukufuma kwibele,

english: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,
translation: Elyo Biludadi umwina Shuha nao alandilepo ati,

english: “Dominion and fear are with him. He makes peace in his high places.
translation: “Ubufumu no bucindami fyakwa Lesa,

english: Can his armies be counted? On whom does his light not arise?
translation: Nani uwingapenda ifita fyakwa Lesa ifimubombela?

english: How then can man be just with God? Or how can he who is born of a woman be clean?
translation: Bushe umuntunse kuti aba shani uwalungama pa cinso cakwa Lesa,

english: Behold, even the moon has no brightness, and the stars are not pure in his sight;
translation: Ngefyo no mweshi wine taubalikisha,

english: How much less man, who is a worm, and the son of man, who is a worm!”
translation: nga palibufi umuntunse uwabafye umutiti,

english: Then Job answered,
translation: Elyo Yobo ayasuka ati,

english: He has described a boundary on the surface of the waters, and to the confines of light and darkness.
translation: Lesa alishingulusha icishilwa pa menshi,

english: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.
translation: Apaikala umulu palasunkana,

english: He stirs up the sea with his power, and by his understanding he strikes through Rahab.
translation: Amaka yakwa Lesa eyatalalika bemba,

english: By his Spirit the heavens are garnished. His hand has pierced the swift serpent.
translation: Umupu wakwa Lesa ewalengele ukuti umulu uwame,

english: Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways. How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?”
translation: Nomba ifi fyonse fya ku nse ya micitile yakwe,

english: “How have you helped him who is without power! How have you saved the arm that has no strength!
translation: “Yangu iwe ifyo wampokololako ine ne wabula amaka,

english: How have you counseled him who has no wisdom, and plentifully declared sound knowledge!
translation: Cine cine iwe walishiba ukufunda impelwamano iyaba nga ine,

english: To whom have you uttered words? Whose spirit came out of you?
translation: Nomba aya mashiwi yobe yalefunda ani,

english: “The departed spirits tremble, those beneath the waters and all that live in them.
translation: “Imilungulwa iyaba mu calo ca bafwa ilatutuma,

english: Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.
translation: Icalo ca bafwa caba ubwamba ku mulola wakwa Lesa,

english: He stretches out the north over empty space, and hangs the earth on nothing.
translation: Ayansa mu lwelele umulu wa ku kapinda ka kuso

english: He binds up the waters in his thick clouds, and the cloud is not burst under them.
translation: Alibika amenshi mu makumbi yakwe ayatikama,

english: He encloses the face of his throne, and spreads his cloud on it.
translation: Afimba pa mweshi ilyo wabulungana,

english: Job again took up his parable, and said,
translation: Elyo Yobo akonkanyapo ukulanda ati,

english: Will he delight himself in the Almighty, and call on God at all times?
translation: Bushe kuti alasansamukila Umwine wa maka yonse?

english: I will teach you about the hand of God. I will not conceal that which is with the Almighty.
translation: Ndi nokumufunda pafyo amaka yakwa Lesa yaba,

english: Behold, all of you have seen it yourselves; why then have you become altogether vain?
translation: Mwe bene nga mwaliimwena,

english: “This is the portion of a wicked man with God, the heritage of oppressors, which they receive from the Almighty.
translation: “Ifi efyo Lesa ali nokucita ku bantu ababifi,

english: If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword. His offspring will not be satisfied with bread.
translation: Abana bakwe nangu bafule shani, bonse bakalafwafye mu nkondo,

english: Those who remain of him will be buried in death. His widows will make no lamentation.
translation: Abakashalapo bakafwa ku cikuko,

english: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare clothing as the clay;
translation: Umubi nangu atulumanike icuma ngo musensenga,

english: he may prepare it, but the just will put it on, and the innocent will divide the silver.
translation: lelo fyonse ifyo atulumanika abalungami ebakesa mukufifwala,

english: He builds his house as the moth, as a booth which the watchman makes.
translation: Umubi alaikuulila amayanda kwati ni tunakantebele,

english: He lies down rich, but he will not do so again. He opens his eyes, and he is not.
translation: Ubushiku pakusendama ninshi ali umukankala, lelo takonkanyapo.

english: “As God lives, who has taken away my right, the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter
translation: “Ine nalapa mu cishinka cakwa Lesa umumi, uwakaana ukunjebelapo,

english: Terrors overtake him like waters. A storm steals him away in the night.
translation: Ifinkunka filamupumikisha nga filya ilyeshi licita,

english: The east wind carries him away, and he departs. It sweeps him out of his place.
translation: Umwela wa ku kabanga nao ulamukumpula, nao ninshi e miile,

english: For it hurls at him, and does not spare, as he flees away from his hand.
translation: Umwela ulamuposa na maka ukwabula uluse,

english: Men will clap their hands at him, and will hiss him out of his place.
translation: Lelo pa nshita alefulumuka, kankungwe amuseka,

english: (for the length of my life is still in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils);
translation: Apo ine ncili ndepema,

english: surely my lips will not speak unrighteousness, neither will my tongue utter deceit.
translation: nakaana ndai ukuti akanwa kandi takakatale akalanda ifyabubifi,

english: Far be it from me that I should justify you. Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me.
translation: Nshasumine nangu pamo ukuti imwe mulelungika mu kulanda kwenu,

english: I hold fast to my righteousness, and will not let it go. My heart will not reproach me so long as I live.
translation: Ndi nokwikatilila kuli bukaele bwandi, nshakalekeko iyoo,

english: “Let my enemy be as the wicked. Let him who rises up against me be as the unrighteous.
translation: “Lekeni umulwani wandi abe ngo mubifi,

english: For what is the hope of the godless, when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
translation: Ngo muntu ushaishiba Lesa, alolela finshi ilyo akafumishiwapo,

english: Will God hear his cry when trouble comes on him?
translation: Bushe Lesa kuti aumfwa ku kulila kwakwe,

english: “Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold which they refine.
translation: “Eko yaba imikoti umo abantu bemba silifa,

english: He cuts out channels among the rocks. His eye sees every precious thing.
translation: Abantu bena balatulinkanya amendo mu fimabwe,

english: He binds the streams that they don’t trickle. The thing that is hidden he brings out to light.
translation: Bena balacilika intulo sha mimana,

english: “But where will wisdom be found? Where is the place of understanding?
translation: “Nomba amano, bushe ni kwisa uko yatula?

english: Man doesn’t know its price, and it isn’t found in the land of the living.
translation: Takulaba umuntu uwaishiba ubucindami bwa mano,

english: The deep says, ‘It isn’t in me.’ The sea says, ‘It isn’t with me.’
translation: Umuyenge usosa auti, ‘Awe temuli ine amano yaba,’

english: It can’t be gotten for gold, neither will silver be weighed for its price.
translation: Amano tayashitwa na golide uwalopololwa,

english: It can’t be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
translation: Ukucindama kwa mano kwalicila pa mutengo wa golide uwine wine uwa ku Ofiri,

english: Gold and glass can’t equal it, neither will it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.
translation: Ukucindama kwa mano kwalicila ukucindama kwa golide na kilistali,

english: No mention will be made of coral or of crystal. Yes, the price of wisdom is above rubies.
translation: Utumabwe utwa kolali na yasipeli, twena tetwakwesha no kulumbula,

english: The topaz of Ethiopia will not equal it. It won’t be valued with pure gold.
translation: Kwalicila ukucindama kwa tumabwe utwa topasi wa ku Kushi,

english: Iron is taken out of the earth, and copper is smelted out of the ore.
translation: Ifyela fipangwa ukufuma ku mushili,

english: Where then does wisdom come from? Where is the place of understanding?
translation: “Nomba amano bushe ni kwi yatula?

english: Seeing it is hidden from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the birds of the sky.
translation: Yalibelama ku menso ya fyabumi fyonse,

english: Destruction and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor of it with our ears.’
translation: Ukuloba ne mfwa kuti fyatila,

english: “God understands its way, and he knows its place.
translation: “Ni Lesa fye eka ewaishiba inshila iyalola ukwaba amano,

english: For he looks to the ends of the earth, and sees under the whole sky.
translation: Pantu ena alamona noko isonde lyashinta,

english: He establishes the force of the wind. Yes, he measures out the waters by measure.
translation: Ilyo apimine umwela amaka,

english: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder,
translation: ilyo apimine imfula apakulokela,

english: then he saw it, and declared it. He established it, yes, and searched it out.
translation: elyo amwene amano no kuyalondolola,

english: To man he said, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.’”
translation: Lesa epakweba umuntu ati,

english: Man sets an end to darkness, and searches out, to the furthest bound, the stones of obscurity and of thick darkness.
translation: Abantu balasanika pakupwisha imfifi,

english: He breaks open a shaft away from where people live. They are forgotten by the foot. They hang far from men, they swing back and forth.
translation: Bemba amendo mu ncende ishishabamo abantu,

english: As for the earth, out of it comes bread. Underneath it is turned up as it were by fire.
translation: Ni mu mushili emumena ifyakulya,

english: Sapphires come from its rocks. It has dust of gold.
translation: Tusafile, utumabwe utwauma umutengo, tusangwa mu mabwe ya mu mushili,

english: That path no bird of prey knows, neither has the falcon’s eye seen it.
translation: “Kapumpe teshiba inshila yakwingilila pa mikoti,

english: The proud animals have not trodden it, nor has the fierce lion passed by there.
translation: Ifiswango ifikangasa tafyendamo,

english: He puts his hand on the flinty rock, and he overturns the mountains by the roots.
translation: Nomba abantu bena balatoba amabwe ayakosa nganshi,

english: Job again took up his parable, and said,
translation: Kabili Yobo abwekeshapo ukulanda ati,

english: The voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.
translation: Na bakateeka nabo baleikala tondolo nga epo ndi,

english: For when the ear heard me, then it blessed me, and when the eye saw me, it commended me,
translation: Kale bonse abaleumfwa ukucindama kwandi baletasha,

english: because I delivered the poor who cried, and the fatherless also, who had no one to help him,
translation: Pantu nalepususha umulanda uwalekuuta,

english: the blessing of him who was ready to perish came on me, and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.
translation: Umuntu uuli pakufwa, nine alesha apaala,

english: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me. My justice was as a robe and a diadem.
translation: Ubulungami naleenda nabo kwati cakufwala ca ku mubili,

english: I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame.
translation: Nali ilinso lya mpofu,

english: I was a father to the needy. I researched the cause of him whom I didn’t know.
translation: Nali wishi wa balekabila,

english: I broke the jaws of the unrighteous and plucked the prey out of his teeth.
translation: Kale naletobaula insekete sha bantu balufyengo,

english: Then I said, ‘I will die in my own house, I will count my days as the sand.
translation: “Ine kale naletifye, ‘Awe nkafwa no mucinshi wandi,

english: My root is spread out to the waters. The dew lies all night on my branch.
translation: Kale nali ngo muti uwashinta imishila yaiko pa menshi,

english: “Oh that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me;
translation: “Yangu ifyo nafuluka imyeshi yakale,

english: My glory is fresh in me. My bow is renewed in my hand.’
translation: Kale naleti ubucindami bwandi tabwakapwe,

english: “Men listened to me, waited, and kept silence for my counsel.
translation: “Nga ndelanda, abantu baleikala tondolo,

english: After my words they didn’t speak again. My speech fell on them.
translation: Nelyo naleka ukulanda, tapaleba na umbi uwakulandapo,

english: They waited for me as for the rain. Their mouths drank as with the spring rain.
translation: Bonse balendolela filya balolela imfula,

english: I smiled on them when they had no confidence. They didn’t reject the light of my face.
translation: Ilyo nabasekela, tabalesumina ukuti cacine,

english: I chose out their way, and sat as chief. I lived as a king in the army, as one who comforts the mourners.
translation: Nine nalepingula abantu no kubeba ifyakucita,

english: when his lamp shone on my head, and by his light I walked through darkness,
translation: Yangu ifyo caweme ilyo cisaniko cakwe calesanika pa mutwe wandi,

english: as I was in my prime, when the friendship of God was in my tent,
translation: Yangu ifyo kale nalesansamuka mu nshiku sha bulumendo bwandi,

english: when the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were around me,
translation: Kale Umwine wa maka yonse twaleenda nankwe,

english: when my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me,
translation: Kale amakasa yandi yaleowa mwishiba ilyatikama,

english: when I went out to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street.
translation: “Kale naleya ku mpongolo ya musumba,

english: The young men saw me and hid themselves. The aged rose up and stood.
translation: Kale abalumendo baletifye cilya bamona, awe bamfumina mu nshila,

english: The princes refrained from talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.
translation: Bacilolo baleleka ukulanda,

english: Again, on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before the LORD, Satan came also among them to present himself before the LORD.
translation: Nakabili kwali ubushiku bumo ilyo abana bakwa Lesa abaume aba ku mulu baile longana pa cinso cakwa Yawe. Satana nao epakwisa monekela ku cinso cakwa Yawe.

english: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this Job didn’t sin with his lips.
translation: Lelo Yobo ayasuka umukashi wakwe ati, “Walanda ifyo umwanakashi onse uushakwata amano engalanda, bushe nga tulapokelela ifisuma kuli Yawe tekuti tupokelele ne fyakutucusha fine?”

english: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.
translation: Kanshi elyo bacibusa bakwa Yobo batatu baumfwile amacushi yonse ayamuponene, baya mukumupempula cila muntu ukufuma kumwakwe. Amashina yabo ni aya: Elifasi umwina Temani, na Biludadi umwina Shuha, na Sofari umwina Namati. Baumfwana bonse pamo ukwisa mukoselesha no kumutalalika umutima.

english: When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.
translation: Bacili akatalamukila bamumona, nomba bafilwa ukumwishiba. Awe bafilwa ukushipikisha, basansula amashiwi yabo balaloosha mu misowa iyikalamba, balepula ne mingila yabo baikuba no lukungu pa mitwe yabo.

english: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.
translation: Baikala nankwe panshi ukulingana ne nshiku cine lubali, akasuba no bushiku, ukwabula ukumusoshamo ishiwi nelyo limo, pantu balimwene ukuti ukucula kwakwe kwalikulishe nganshi.

english: The LORD said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered the LORD, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”
translation: Kabili Yawe aipusha Satana ati, “Wafuma kwisa?” Satana ayasuka Yawe ati, “Nacilaendaukafye nafuma uku naya uku, nacilalulumbafye mu calo.”

english: The LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.”
translation: Yawe amwipusha ati, “Bushe wamona umubomfi wandi Yobo ifyo aba? Tapaba pa calo uwalingana nankwe, muntu uwakaele, umololoke kabili uutiina Lesa no kutaluka kukucita ifyabipa. Taumwene ukuti nashipikisha, nasunga ubufumacumi bwakwe, nangu line wampatikishe ukuti monaule apabula umulandu.”

english: Satan answered the LORD, and said, “Skin for skin. Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.
translation: Elyo Satana ayasuka Yawe ati, “Bakabushanya inkanda ne nkanda. Umuntu kuti asumina ukuposa fyonse ifyo akwata pakupususha ubumi bwakwe.

english: But stretch out your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce you to your face.”
translation: Nomba fungulula ukuboko kobe no kwikata kwifupa no munofu wakwe. Akakulapisha pa cinso cobe.”

english: The LORD said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand. Only spare his life.”
translation: Yawe epakweba Satana ati, “Cisuma kanshi nimupeela mu minwe yobe, lelo wiesha kwikata ku mweo wakwe.”

english: So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.
translation: Kanshi Satana epakufuma pa cinso cakwa Yawe no kuya lwalika Yobo ifilonda ifyabipisha nganshi umubili onse, ukufuma ku tukondo ukufika na ku mutwe.

english: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
translation: Yobo epakubuula iciinga eco alafopolweko ifilonda, aikala na mu mito.

english: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die.”
translation: Elyo umukashi wakwe aisa mweba ati, “Bushe na nomba ucili uletwalilila mukusunga ubufumacumi bobe? Mutuke Lesa no kufwa ufwe, cipwe!”

english: “But now those who are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I considered unworthy to put with my sheep dogs.
translation: “Nomba balenseka,

english: They abhor me, they stand aloof from me, and don’t hesitate to spit in my face.
translation: Balimpata kabili balantaluka,

english: For he has untied his cord, and afflicted me; and they have thrown off restraint before me.
translation: Ico bamwene ukuti Lesa nomba nandimuna,

english: On my right hand rise the rabble. They thrust aside my feet. They cast their ways of destruction up against me.
translation: Uluko lwabo lwanjimina ku kulyo,

english: They mar my path. They promote my destruction without anyone’s help.
translation: Nabancilikila inshila konse konse pakuti nikwata ukwakubutukila,

english: As through a wide breach they come. They roll themselves in amid the ruin.
translation: Baisa ingila nga pa cipunda ce linga icamokoka,

english: Terrors have turned on me. They chase my honor as the wind. My welfare has passed away as a cloud.
translation: Ifyakutiina fyanjishila,

english: “Now my soul is poured out within me. Days of affliction have taken hold of me.
translation: “Ine nomba ndi mupepi ne mfwa,

english: In the night season my bones are pierced in me, and the pains that gnaw me take no rest.
translation: Nga bwaila ndeumfwa mu mafupa mulekokota,

english: My garment is disfigured by great force. It binds me about as the collar of my tunic.
translation: Cili kwati Lesa nankama mu mukoshi we laya lyandi,

english: He has cast me into the mire. I have become like dust and ashes.
translation: Cili kwati Lesa amfubwile mu matipa,

english: Of what use is the strength of their hands to me, men in whom ripe age has perished?
translation: Amaka ya mu maboko yabo tayalemombela nangu cimo,

english: I cry to you, and you do not answer me. I stand up, and you gaze at me.
translation: Nalilila kuli iwe we Lesa mukulu, nomba taulenjasuka,

english: You have turned to be cruel to me. With the might of your hand you persecute me.
translation: Naunjalukila bunkalwe bunkalwe,

english: You lift me up to the wind, and drive me with it. You dissolve me in the storm.
translation: Naunjimya no kumposa mu mwela,

english: For I know that you will bring me to death, to the house appointed for all living.
translation: Ninjishiba ukuti alentwalafye ukwakuti nje mfwile,

english: “However doesn’t one stretch out a hand in his fall? Or in his calamity therefore cry for help?
translation: “Lelo bushe uuli mu bucushi tatambika ukuboko kwakwe?

english: Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble? Wasn’t my soul grieved for the needy?
translation: Bushe kale ine nshalelililako abantu abalecula,

english: When I looked for good, then evil came. When I waited for light, darkness came.
translation: Ilyo nasubila ishuko, ninshi paleisa ububi.

english: My heart is troubled, and doesn’t rest. Days of affliction have come on me.
translation: Mu mala yandi mulepota ukwabula ukuleka,

english: I go mourning without the sun. I stand up in the assembly, and cry for help.
translation: Inkanda yandi naifita lelo te kasuba kalengele iyoo,

english: I am a brother to jackals, and a companion to ostriches.
translation: Bamumbwe ebasangwike bamunyinane,

english: They are gaunt from lack and famine. They gnaw the dry ground, in the gloom of waste and desolation.
translation: Bashelefye imipalapata ku mulandu wa bupina ne cipowe,

english: My skin grows black and peels from me. My bones are burned with heat.
translation: Inkanda yandi yalwike iyafiita

english: Therefore my harp has turned to mourning, and my pipe into the voice of those who weep.
translation: Eico peseese lyandi ndelishapofye inyimbo sha ndoosha,

english: They pluck salt herbs by the bushes. The roots of the broom tree are their food.
translation: Baleya mu mpanga mukusaba amabula ya mu mpanga,

english: They are driven out from among men. They cry after them as after a thief,
translation: Abanabo balebatamfisha ukutali,

english: so that they live in frightful valleys, and in holes of the earth and of the rocks.
translation: Baleikala mu ncena sha mikonko,

english: They bray among the bushes. They are gathered together under the nettles.
translation: Epakulapundila mu fimpusa kwati ni mpunda,

english: They are children of fools, yes, children of wicked men. They were flogged out of the land.
translation: Abantu abalifye ifiwelewele,

english: “Now I have become their song. Yes, I am a byword to them.
translation: “Kabili ni aba bene ebanseka mu nyimbo,

english: “I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?
translation: “Ine nalipangana na menso yandi,

english: then let my wife grind for another, and let others sleep with her.
translation: lyena ninshi umukashi wandi naye mukutebeta bambi,

english: For that would be a heinous crime. Yes, it would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges,
translation: Pantu nga nalicita ububi ubwabipisha,

english: for it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and would root out all my increase.
translation: Caba ngo mulilo uwoca mpaka waonaula,

english: “If I have despised the cause of my male servant or of my female servant, when they contended with me,
translation: “Ine nga nalifyengele ababomfi bandi abaume nangu abanakashi,

english: what then will I do when God rises up? When he visits, what will I answer him?
translation: ninshi kuti nacita shani ilyo Lesa akema?

english: Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?
translation: Lesa ewamumbile, na babomfi bandi ni Lesa ewababumbile,

english: “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
translation: “Ine nshatala nkaana ukwafwa abalanda mufyo bakabila,

english: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it
translation: Ine nshatala ndya umukate neka,

english: (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, I have guided her from my mother’s womb);
translation: Pantu ukufuma ku bwaice bwandi ndela abalanda ngo mufyashi,

english: if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering;
translation: Ilyo nalemona umuntu uushikwete icakufwala,

english: For what is the portion from God above, and the heritage from the Almighty on high?
translation: Nomba kwena bushe fintu nshi ifyo Lesa uwa mu mulu alambula abantu?

english: if his heart hasn’t blessed me, if he hasn’t been warmed with my sheep’s fleece;
translation: ine nalemupeelako icakufwala icisuma icapikulwa ku masako ya mpaanga shandi.

english: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, because I saw my help in the gate;
translation: Nga cakuti nalimishe amaboko yandi pa bana banshiwa,

english: then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade, and my arm be broken from the bone.
translation: ninshi ukuboko kwandi kupapukile pa kubeya,

english: For calamity from God is a terror to me. Because of his majesty, I can do nothing.
translation: Umwenso wanjikata pantu ubukali bwakwa Lesa kuti bwanjishila,

english: “If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’
translation: “Nga cakuti natetekela muli golide,

english: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gotten much;
translation: Nga cakuti nacita icilumba pa mulandu wa cuma candi icafulisha,

english: if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,
translation: Nga cakuti namona ubucindami bwa kasuba ilyo kabalika,

english: and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth;
translation: Bushe ifi efyakukubula umutima wandi,

english: this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges, for I would have denied the God who is above.
translation: Ifi fyonse kuti fyaba ububifi ubukalamba ubwakupingwilwapo,

english: “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him
translation: “Nga cakuti ndasansamuka pakumona ifyo abalwani bandi basheme,

english: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, and disaster to the workers of iniquity?
translation: Bushe tasungila abalufyengo ishamo,

english: (I have certainly not allowed my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse);
translation: awe ine nshatala ndeka ululimi lwandi ukuti lulebifya,

english: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who can find one who has not been filled with his meat?’
translation: Nga cakuti abantu ba mwitenti lyandi tabatala abasosa abati,

english: (the foreigner has not camped in the street, but I have opened my doors to the traveler);
translation: Takwatala akuba umweni uwasendama panse,

english: if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart,
translation: Nga cakuti ndafisa abantu bumpulamafunde bwandi nge ficita bambi,

english: because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and didn’t go out of the door—
translation: pa mulandu wakutiina icintubwingi,

english: oh that I had one to hear me! Behold, here is my signature! Let the Almighty answer me! Let the accuser write my indictment!
translation: Iye bushe nani uwingansoselako pakuti Lesa aŋumfwe,

english: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder, and I would bind it to me as a crown.
translation: Ilyo ipepala kuti nalibika pa kubeya kwandi,

english: I would declare to him the number of my steps. I would go near to him like a prince.
translation: Ndi nokuya londolola kuli ena pa myendele yandi yonse,

english: If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;
translation: “Nga cakuti impanga yandi yalandubulwisha,

english: if I have eaten its fruits without money, or have caused its owners to lose their life,
translation: nangu nga cakuti ndya ifisabo fyabamo ukwabula ukulipila ababomfi,

english: Doesn’t he see my ways, and count all my steps?
translation: Bushe Lesa tamona imyendele yandi,

english: let briers grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.
translation: ninshi lyena lekeni imyunga eyo yamenemo mu cifulo ca ŋanu,

english: “If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit
translation: “Nalapa ine ukuti nshatala mbepa bufi,

english: (let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);
translation: Lekeni Lesa ampime pa cipimo icishibepa,

english: if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands,
translation: Nga cakuti amakasa yandi yatala yafuma mu nshila,

english: then let me sow, and let another eat. Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.
translation: lyena lekeni bambi ebo balye icuma candi,

english: “If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door,
translation: “Nga cakuti ine nalitala nkumbwa umwanakashi,

english: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
translation: Kanshi abantu aba batatu epakuleka ukulanda na Yobo, ico Yobo alishininkishe bukaele bwakwe mu kumona kwakwe.

english: Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me; I also will show my opinion.’
translation: Kanshi nomba na imwe kutikeniko na kuli ine,

english: “Behold, I waited for your words, and I listened for your reasoning, while you searched out what to say.
translation: “Moneni, naciba ndelolela ilyo mwaciba mulelanda,

english: Yes, I gave you my full attention, but there was no one who convinced Job, or who answered his words, among you.
translation: Nacilakutumaninamo nganshi mufyo mulesosa,

english: Beware lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom. God may refute him, not man;’
translation: Eico mwilaibepa amuti, ‘Ifwe twalikwata amano.’

english: for he has not directed his words against me; neither will I answer him with your speeches.
translation: Pantu Yobo tasosele amashiwi ayakupinkana na ine,

english: “They are amazed. They answer no more. They don’t have a word to say.
translation: “Ala aba bantu nacibasungusha, tabakwete ne fyakwasuka,

english: Shall I wait, because they don’t speak, because they stand still, and answer no more?
translation: Bushe na nomba kuti nalolela apo nabaleka ukulanda,

english: I also will answer my part, and I also will show my opinion.
translation: Kanshi nomba nine nalalandapo,

english: For I am full of words. The spirit within me constrains me.
translation: Pantu ndi ne fingi ifyakulanda,

english: Behold, my breast is as wine which has no vent; like new wineskins it is ready to burst.
translation: Munda yandi muli kwati muli umwangashi upya,

english: Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled against Job. His wrath was kindled because he justified himself rather than God.
translation: Elyo Elihu mwana Barakeli, umwina Busi, uwa mu mukowa wakwa Ramu afulilwe Yobo nganshi. Afulilwe Yobo pa mulandu wakuilungamika ukucila Lesa.

english: I will speak, that I may be refreshed. I will open my lips and answer.
translation: Na pakuti mpeme kanofye ntale nande,

english: Please don’t let me respect any man’s person, neither will I give flattering titles to any man.
translation: Ine nshacite mucishacinani ku muntu nelyo umo,

english: For I don’t know how to give flattering titles, or else my Maker would soon take me away.
translation: Ine nshaishiba no kusembeleka nakalya,

english: Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
translation: Afulilwe na bacibusa bakwe bonse batatu, ico bashakwete ifyakumwasuka lelo nabamuseka.

english: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were older than he.
translation: Ilyo balelanda, Elihu aikele tondolo, pantu abalelanda bantu abakalamba.

english: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was kindled.
translation: Nomba ilyo amwene ukuti aba bantu batatu tabakwete icakwasuka, icipyu camwikata.

english: Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered, “I am young, and you are very old. Therefore I held back, and didn’t dare show you my opinion.
translation: Kanshi Elihu, mwana Barakeli epakusosa ati,

english: I said, ‘Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.’
translation: Ine mu mutima wandi nacilatontonkanya ati,

english: But there is a spirit in man, and the Spirit of the Almighty gives them understanding.
translation: Nomba ine nalishiba ukuti umupu uwaba mu muntu,

english: It is not the great who are wise, nor the aged who understand justice.
translation: Ala ubukote tabulenga ukuti umuntu abe na mano,

english: “However, Job, please hear my speech, and listen to all my words.
translation: “Kanshi nomba iwe Yobo, umfwa kufyo ine nalakweba.

english: Behold, he finds occasions against me. He counts me for his enemy.
translation: Nomba Lesa alafwailishafye icakumpeelelapo umulandu,

english: He puts my feet in the stocks. He marks all my paths.’
translation: Abikile amakasa yandi mwikoli,

english: “Behold, I will answer you. In this you are not just, for God is greater than man.
translation: “Eico nakweba ukuti pakusosa ifi nauluba,

english: Why do you strive against him, because he doesn’t give account of any of his matters?
translation: Nga cinshi ico uleebawila Lesa,

english: For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention.
translation: Pantu Lesa alalanda mu musango umo,

english: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, in slumbering on the bed,
translation: Kuti alandila mu ciloto na mu fimonwa mu nshita ya bushiku,

english: then he opens the ears of men, and seals their instruction,
translation: Limbi kuti amutotoshafye,

english: that he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.
translation: pakwalula umuntu ukufuma ku fyabipa,

english: He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.
translation: Pakuti apusushe umweo wakwe ku nindi,

english: “He is chastened also with pain on his bed, with continual strife in his bones,
translation: “Limbi Lesa alakalipila umuntu ilyo alecula ku bulwele,

english: See now, I have opened my mouth. My tongue has spoken in my mouth.
translation: Mona, ine nomba natampa ukulanda,

english: so that his life abhors bread, and his soul dainty food.
translation: Ilyo umutima wakwe taulefwaya kulya,

english: His flesh is so consumed away that it can’t be seen. His bones that were not seen stick out.
translation: Ilyo umubili wakwe waonda umupwilapo,

english: Yes, his soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.
translation: Ilyo ubumi bwakwe bwapalama ku nindi,

english: “If there is beside him an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to show to man what is right for him,
translation: “Lelo nga cakuti malaika ali mupepi,

english: then God is gracious to him, and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom.’
translation: Uwakumulangulukila no kumweba ati,

english: His flesh will be fresher than a child’s. He returns to the days of his youth.
translation: Lyena ninshi kuti umubili wakwe wapuputulwa,

english: He prays to God, and he is favorable to him, so that he sees his face with joy. He restores to man his righteousness.
translation: Lyena kuti apepa Lesa ico amukwatila uluse,

english: He sings before men, and says, ‘I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it didn’t profit me.
translation: Yobo 13:27

english: He has redeemed my soul from going into the pit. My life will see the light.’
translation: Alubula umweo wandi ukufuma mukuya ku nindi,

english: “Behold, God does all these things, twice, yes three times, with a man,
translation: “Ifi fyonse efyo Lesa acitila umuntu,

english: My words will utter the uprightness of my heart. That which my lips know they will speak sincerely.
translation: Mu mutima wandi mwalafuma insoso ishaololoka,

english: to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of the living.
translation: pakuti apusushe umweo wakwe ku nindi,

english: Mark well, Job, and listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will speak.
translation: “Eico iwe Yobo, bika amano kuli ine uŋumfwe bwino,

english: If you have anything to say, answer me. Speak, for I desire to justify you.
translation: Nga naukwata ifyakulanda unjasuke,

english: If not, listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom.”
translation: Nga taukwete fyakwasukapo, kanshi kutika kufyo ine ndesosa,

english: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
translation: Pantu Umupashi wakwa Lesa ewabumba ine,

english: If you can, answer me. Set your words in order before me, and stand up.
translation: Nga wafwaya ukunjasuka, wasuke,

english: Behold, I am toward God even as you are. I am also formed out of the clay.
translation: Ine nshili Lesa, ndi muntu munobefye,

english: Behold, my terror will not make you afraid, neither will my pressure be heavy on you.
translation: Peba nangu cimo icakulenga ukuti untiine,

english: “Surely you have spoken in my hearing, I have heard the voice of your words, saying,
translation: “Lelo ine ninjumfwila fyonse ifyo ulandile,

english: ‘I am clean, without disobedience. I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me.
translation: ‘Ndi wakaele uwabula ububifi,

english: Moreover Elihu answered,
translation: Kabili Elihu akonkanyapo ukulanda ati,

english: “Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.
translation: “Kanshi nkutikeni nganshi imwe mwe bantu bamano.

english: For the work of a man he will render to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.
translation: Yobo 12:11

english: Yes surely, God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert justice.
translation: Amalu 62:12

english: Who put him in charge of the earth? Or who has appointed him over the whole world?
translation: Takwatala akuba na umbi uyo uwalashika Lesa pano isonde,

english: If he set his heart on himself, if he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,
translation: Nga cakuti Lesa afumyapo umupashi wakwe pano isonde,

english: all flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust.
translation: ala ifintu fyonse ifipema kuti fyafwafye pa muku umo,

english: “If now you have understanding, hear this. Listen to the voice of my words.
translation: “Kanshi iwe Yobo nga uli wamano kutika,

english: Should even one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him who is righteous and mighty,
translation: Bushe uwapata umulinganya kuti ateeka?

english: who says to a king, ‘Vile!’ or to nobles, ‘Wicked!’?
translation: Bushe te uwingeba bashamfumu ukuti, ‘Muli bafye,’

english: He doesn’t respect the persons of princes, nor respect the rich more than the poor, for they all are the work of his hands.
translation: Bushe te uushakwatila intungulushi umucishacinani,

english: “Hear my words, you wise men. Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.
translation: “Kutikeni ku mashiwi yandi mwe bantu bamano,

english: In a moment they die, even at midnight. The people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are taken away without a hand.
translation: Akashita akali konse kuti bafwa nangu ni pakati ka bushiku,

english: “For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings.
translation: “Pantu Lesa alalengula imyendele ya muntu,

english: There is no darkness, nor thick gloom, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
translation: Takwaba ukwafisama, nangu ukwashika,

english: For he doesn’t need to consider a man further, that he should go before God in judgment.
translation: Pantu Lesa talefwaya ukuceceta umuntu nakabili,

english: He breaks mighty men in pieces in ways past finding out, and sets others in their place.
translation: Alofya abacindami apabula ukwipusha umulandu,

english: Therefore he takes knowledge of their works. He overturns them in the night, so that they are destroyed.
translation: Pantu Lesa alishiba ifibi fyonse ifyo bacita,

english: He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others;
translation: Abakandila pa bubi bwabo,

english: because they turned away from following him, and wouldn’t pay attention to any of his ways,
translation: Pantu bena balimukene,

english: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him. He heard the cry of the afflicted.
translation: Ebalengele inkuuta sha balanda ukumfwika kuli Lesa,

english: When he gives quietness, who then can condemn? When he hides his face, who then can see him? He is over a nation or a man alike,
translation: Bushe Lesa nga atalala tondolo, ni nani engamwebaula?

english: For the ear tries words, as the palate tastes food.
translation: Ala amatwi eyapima ifilelandwa,

english: that the godless man may not reign, that there be no one to ensnare the people.
translation: eulesha umubi ukuba kateeka,

english: “For has any said to God, ‘I am guilty, but I will not offend any more.
translation: “Nomba umuntu nga aeba Lesa ati,

english: Teach me that which I don’t see. If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more’?
translation: Unsambilishe ifyo nafilwa ukwishiba.

english: Shall his recompense be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. Therefore speak what you know.
translation: Bushe iwe, emukuti ulefwaya Lesa akucitile ifintu umo ulefwaila,

english: Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man who hears me:
translation: “Abantu bonse abamano na bonse abasalapuka,

english: ‘Job speaks without knowledge. His words are without wisdom.’
translation: ‘Cacine Yobo alanda ukwabula amano,

english: I wish that Job were tried to the end, because of his answering like wicked men.
translation: Kanshi mwesheni Yobo apakalamba,

english: For he adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God.”
translation: Pantu ena ku fyabubifi fyakwe alundilepo na bucisanguka,

english: Let us choose for us that which is right. Let us know among ourselves what is good.
translation: Natufwailishe bonse capamo icilungeme,

english: For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, God has taken away my right.
translation: Yobo alesosa ati, ‘Ine ndi wakaele,

english: Notwithstanding my right I am considered a liar. My wound is incurable, though I am without disobedience.’
translation: Nangu nshamonapo icibi ico nacita,

english: What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water,
translation: Bushe kwalibapo umuntu uwaba nga Yobo,

english: who goes in company with the workers of iniquity, and walks with wicked men?
translation: Aenda na bacita ifibi,

english: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.’
translation: Bushe tasosele ati,

english: Moreover Elihu answered,
translation: Kabili Elihu akonkanyapo ukulanda ati,

english: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
translation: Lelo tapaba uutontonkanya no kwipusha ati,

english: who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’
translation: Ni Lesa ewalenga ukuti tucenjele ukucila inama sha mu mpanga,

english: There they cry, but no one answers, because of the pride of evil men.
translation: Nelyo abantu bakuuta mutuule, nomba ena tabasuka,

english: Surely God will not hear an empty cry, neither will the Almighty regard it.
translation: Cine cine Lesa tomfwako ku kukuuta kwa aba bantu,

english: How much less when you say you don’t see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!
translation: Pali bufi bushe Lesa kuti akumfwa nga wasosa auti, ‘Awe ine nalifilwa ukumona Lesa!

english: But now, because he has not visited in his anger, neither does he greatly regard arrogance,
translation: Kabili ulesosa auti, ‘Nangu Lesa afulwa, takanda abantu.

english: therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge.”
translation: Kanshi Yobo asosafye amashiwi yacilandelande,

english: “Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’
translation: “Bushe iwe Yobo, emukuti ulemona ukuti naciwama ici ulelanda icakuti,

english: that you ask, ‘What advantage will it be to you? What profit will I have, more than if I had sinned?’
translation: Kabili uleipusha auti, ‘Ni cinshi mwenamo,

english: I will answer you, and your companions with you.
translation: Kanshi ine nalakwasuka,

english: Look to the skies, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you.
translation: “Inwina amenso ku mulu umone,

english: If you have sinned, what effect do you have against him? If your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to him?
translation: Nga wacita ububifi, ninshi bubi nshi wacita kuli Lesa?

english: If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?
translation: Nangu nga wawamya, bushe fisuma nshi wamupeela?

english: Your wickedness may hurt a man as you are, and your righteousness may profit a son of man.
translation: Ukubifya kobe kuletelela umuntu nga iwe wine,

english: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.
translation: “Pa mulandu wa cisendo cakutitikishiwa abantu balailishanya,

english: Elihu also continued, and said,
translation: Elihu akonkanyapo ukusosa ati,

english: He also opens their ears to instruction, and commands that they return from iniquity.
translation: Epakubakomona amatwi pakuti bomfwishe ifyo Lesa alebasoka,

english: If they listen and serve him, they will spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
translation: Nga cakuti baumfwa no kwamba ukumubombela,

english: But if they don’t listen, they will perish by the sword; they will die without knowledge.
translation: Lelo nga bakaana ukumfwa, ninshi bakaloba ku lupanga,

english: “But those who are godless in heart lay up anger. They don’t cry for help when he binds them.
translation: “Lelo abaumalala imitima, bekala abafulwa,

english: They die in youth. Their life perishes among the unclean.
translation: Bafwa ilyo bacili imisepela,

english: He delivers the afflicted by their affliction, and opens their ear in oppression.
translation: Apususha abalanda mu nshita shabo ishabulanda,

english: Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a wide place, where there is no restriction. That which is set on your table would be full of fatness.
translation: Nobe wine afwaya ukukupususha mu bulanda bobe,

english: “But you are full of the judgment of the wicked. Judgment and justice take hold of you.
translation: “Lelo iwe nawisulamo ubupingushi bwa babifi,

english: Don’t let riches entice you to wrath, neither let the great size of a bribe turn you aside.
translation: Kanshi nomba ulecenjela, epali ubwingi bwa fyuma bwakukubula,

english: Would your wealth sustain you in distress, or all the might of your strength?
translation: Bushe icuma cobe, nangu ukutulukusha kwa maka yobe,

english: “Bear with me a little, and I will show you; for I still have something to say on God’s behalf.
translation: “Ntekelafye umutima, uleke nkulondolwele,

english: Don’t desire the night, when people are cut off in their place.
translation: Wilafuluka inshita ya bushiku,

english: Take heed, don’t regard iniquity; for you have chosen this rather than affliction.
translation: Ulecenjela wiyalukila kukucita ifyabipa,

english: Behold, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
translation: “Tontonkanya ifyo Lesa aba umucindami pa mulandu wa maka yakwe.

english: Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness’?
translation: Nani uwingamulangilila ifyakucita?

english: “Remember that you magnify his work, about which men have sung.
translation: “Ibukishafye ukulumbanya Lesa pa milimo yakwe,

english: All men have looked on it. Man sees it afar off.
translation: Abantu bonse balatamba ifyo Lesa acita,

english: Behold, God is great, and we don’t know him. The number of his years is unsearchable.
translation: Icacine Lesa alikulisha, icakuti twalifilwa no kumwishiba,

english: For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor,
translation: “Ni Lesa eubuula amenshi muli bemba,

english: which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.
translation: Imfula nayo epakulafumfumuka ukufuma mu makumbi,

english: Indeed, can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds and the thunderings of his pavilion?
translation: Takwaba nelyo umo uwaishiba ifyo Lesa atandanya amakumbi mu lwelele,

english: I will get my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
translation: Amano yandi ine yafuma ukutali,

english: Behold, he spreads his light around him. He covers the bottom of the sea.
translation: Ulemona ifyo umwele wa nkuba umushinguluka,

english: For by these he judges the people. He gives food in abundance.
translation: Ifi fyonse efyo Lesa abomfya pakupingula abantu,

english: He covers his hands with the lightning, and commands it to strike the mark.
translation: Afumbata umwele wa nkuba mu minwe yakwe,

english: Its noise tells about him, and the livestock also, concerning the storm that comes up.
translation: Icibulukutu cisobela ukwisa kwa mfula,

english: For truly my words are not false. One who is perfect in knowledge is with you.
translation: Pantu icine cine ifyo ine ndesosa te fyabufi iyoo,

english: “Behold, God is mighty, and doesn’t despise anyone. He is mighty in strength of understanding.
translation: “Mona ni Lesa e wamaka lelo tasuusha umuntu nangu umo,

english: He doesn’t preserve the life of the wicked, but gives justice to the afflicted.
translation: Taleka abantu babi baleikalilila,

english: He doesn’t withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne, he sets them forever, and they are exalted.
translation: Lesa tafumya amenso yakwe pa bantu abaololoka imitima,

english: If they are bound in fetters, and are taken in the cords of afflictions,
translation: Asuka abakaka mu minyololo,

english: then he shows them their work, and their transgressions, that they have behaved themselves proudly.
translation: Epakubalanga fyonse ifyo balecita,

english: “Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.
translation: “Ecalenga ukuti umutima wandi ututume,

english: By the breath of God, ice is given, and the width of the waters is frozen.
translation: Umupu wakwa Lesa ulapanga amenshi makasa,

english: Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his lightning.
translation: Lesa ewisusha amenshi mu makumbi,

english: It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he commands them on the surface of the habitable world,
translation: Lesa umwine ewensha amakumbi

english: whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.
translation: Ico Lesa aletela amakumbi ne mfula pano calo,

english: “Listen to this, Job. Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
translation: “Umfwa bwino aya mashiwi iwe Yobo, wikalefye tondolo,

english: Do you know how God controls them, and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?
translation: Bushe iwe Yobo, walishiba ifyo Lesa asesha ifi fintu,

english: Do you know the workings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?
translation: Bushe iwe walishiba icilenga amakumbi ukulaenda mu lwelele,

english: You whose clothing is warm when the earth is still by reason of the south wind?
translation: Wamona ifyo ifyakufwala ifi ufwele fikabile ku cipuki,

english: Can you, with him, spread out the sky, which is strong as a cast metal mirror?
translation: Bushe iwe kuti wayafwako Lesa ukufungulula umutenge wa mulu,

english: Teach us what we will tell him, for we can’t make our case by reason of darkness.
translation: “Bushe iwe ulefwaya tulande shani pali Lesa?

english: Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.
translation: Kutikeni imwe bonse. Umfweni ishiwi lyakwa Lesa ifyo lilepanta,

english: Will it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?
translation: Ine nshaebe Lesa nati, ‘Leka nine ndelanda,’ awe,

english: Now men don’t see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.
translation: Takuli muntu nangu umo uwingalolesha pa kasuba

english: Out of the north comes golden splendor. With God is awesome majesty.
translation: Na ku kapinda ka ku kuso kwaisuka kwabuuta,

english: We can’t reach the Almighty. He is exalted in power. In justice and great righteousness, he will not oppress.
translation: Ifwe teti tufike apaikala Umwine wa maka yonse,

english: Therefore men revere him. He doesn’t regard any who are wise of heart.”
translation: Ecilenga nokuti abantu balemukwatila akatiina,

english: He sends it out under the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.
translation: Alebyashisha umwele wa nkuba pano pesamba lya mulu,

english: After it a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He doesn’t hold back anything when his voice is heard.
translation: Pakonkapo icibulumo ce shiwi lyakwe,

english: God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.
translation: Cine cine Lesa alatusungusha pafyo acita ifikulu,

english: For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.
translation: Ifyo eba ubunga bwa mfula ati, ‘Ponena pa mushili.’

english: He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it.
translation: Ninshi ne milimo ya bantu yatala yalala,

english: Then the animals take cover, and remain in their dens.
translation: Ninshi lyena ne nama sha mpanga shabwelelamo uko shikala,

english: Out of its room comes the storm, and cold out of the north.
translation: Kankungwe afuma kumwakwe ku kapinda ka ku kulyo,

english: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind,
translation: Elyo Yawe ayasuka Yobo, ukufuma mu cimwela ati,

english: marked out for it my bound, set bars and doors,
translation: Nine napimine bemba apakupelela,

english: and said, ‘You may come here, but no further. Your proud waves shall be stopped here’?
translation: No kumweba nati, ‘Apa epo wakulapelela, amatamba yobe yelapulapo.

english: “Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place,
translation: “Bushe mu bumi bobe, walitala aukonkomesha ukuti buce ulucelo,

english: that it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and shake the wicked out of it?
translation: Bushe walitala awebapo ulucelo ukuti lwikatilile impela she sonde,

english: It is changed as clay under the seal, and presented as a garment.
translation: Ulubuuto lwa pa macaca lulalenga impili ne mikonko ukwaluka,

english: From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.
translation: Ulubuuto lwapa macaca lulashibatika abantu babi,

english: “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?
translation: “Bushe iwe walitala aufika apatula amenshi ya muli bemba?

english: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
translation: Bushe kwalitala akubako umo uwakulanga apabela impongolo sha mfwa?

english: Have you comprehended the earth in its width? Declare, if you know it all.
translation: Bushe walishiba apafika ubukulu bwe sonde lyonse?

english: “What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,
translation: “Bushe iwe walishibako uko ulubuuto lwaikalila,

english: “Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?
translation: “Bushe iwe niwe nani we ulefulunganya ifyo ine napingula,

english: that you should take it to its bound, that you should discern the paths to its house?
translation: Bushe kuti watungulula ulubuuto ne mfifi,

english: Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!
translation: Ee, nga cakuti walishiba ifi fyonse,

english: Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,
translation: Yere 5:22

english: which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?
translation: Ifi fintu ne mwine ndafisunga pakuti filebomba pa nshita ya bucushi,

english: By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?
translation: Bushe iwe walishiba uko akasuba katula,

english: Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm,
translation: Nani uwaimbile icikonkwa umwakupita mulamba wa mfula uwa mukuku,

english: to cause it to rain on a land where there is no man, on the wilderness, in which there is no man,
translation: Nani alenga imfula ukuloka mu fifulo umushaba bantu,

english: to satisfy the waste and desolate ground, to cause the tender grass to grow?
translation: Nani uutapilila amatololo,

english: Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?
translation: “Bushe imfula yalikwata wishi?

english: Whose womb did the ice come out of? Who has given birth to the gray frost of the sky?
translation: Nyina wa menshi yalya ayatalalisha nani?

english: Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me!
translation: Eico kakisha umushipi mu musana nge mpalume ya bulwi,

english: The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.
translation: Ni nani uulenga amenshi ukukosa nge libwe,

english: “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?
translation: “Bushe niwe wakakanya iminyololo iyakaka intanda sha Pileiyadesi,

english: Can you lead the constellations out in their season? Or can you guide the Bear with her cubs?
translation: Bushe niwe wingalenga mulanga ukumoneka pa nshita yakwe,

english: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?
translation: Bushe iwe walishiba icalenga ukuti ifya mu mulu fileenda?

english: “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover you?
translation: “Bushe iwe ishiwi lyobe kuti lyafika ku makumbi,

english: Can you send out lightnings, that they may go? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?
translation: Bushe iwe niwe wingeba umwele wa nkuba ukubyata,

english: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?
translation: Bushe nani uupanda ulwita mfula amano ayakusobela ukuti imfula yalaisa?

english: Who can count the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the containers of the sky,
translation: Nani uwakwata amano yakulonganya amakumbi,

english: when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?
translation: Mpaka ulukungu lwa pa mushili lwakambantana,

english: “Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
translation: “Bushe iwe niwe wikatila inkalamo inama shakulya?

english: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.
translation: “Bushe wali kwi ilyo nashimpile umufula wa pano isonde,

english: when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?
translation: lilya tubwatalala mu mimba yatuko,

english: Who provides for the raven his prey, when his young ones cry to God, and wander for lack of food?
translation: Nani uupekanisha mwankole ifyakulya,

english: Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it?
translation: Bushe iwe walishiba uwapimine ubukulu bwa pano pesonde? Icine cine walishiba,

english: What were its foundations fastened on? Or who laid its cornerstone,
translation: Nga nipi apo inceshi she sonde shashimpwa?

english: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
translation: Ilyo intanda sha pa macaca shaleimba ne nsansa,

english: “Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke out of the womb,
translation: “Nani uwaisalile amenshi ya muli bemba,

english: when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,
translation: Ilyo nabuulile fubefube no kukupa pali bemba,

english: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?
translation: “Bushe iwe walishiba ilyo ifibushi mabwe fifyala?

english: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?
translation: Bushe iwe kuti wabula umwando no kukaka imboo mu mukoshi,

english: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?
translation: Bushe kuti wasubila mu maka yakwata imboo,

english: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?
translation: Bushe kuti watontonkanya auti, ilebwelela kuli ine,

english: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly, but are they the feathers and plumage of love?
translation: “Amapindo ya mbuni yalangufyanya nganshi pakupampaila,

english: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,
translation: Itila nga yabikila amani pa mushili yayasha nefyo fine,

english: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.
translation: Imbuni yena yalaba nokuti ulukasa lwa muntu kuti lwanyantapo,

english: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,
translation: Yena icita ubunkalwe ku twana twaiko, kwati teine yatuko,

english: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.
translation: Icalenga, mulandu wakuti Lesa tapeelako imbuni amano,

english: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
translation: Nomba nga yati kambutuke,

english: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?
translation: “Bushe niwe walenga kabalwe ukuba uwalubilo?

english: Can you count the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?
translation: Bushe ulapenda imyeshi iyo inama sha mpanga shikwatilapo utwana,

english: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
translation: Bushe niwe walenga ukuti aletolauka amabaka nga makanta,

english: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.
translation: Kabalwe alafola nga ali mu nika no kulalishamo inshindo,

english: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.
translation: Alaseka umwenso, kabili tapaba ico atiina,

english: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
translation: Pa mbali yakwa kabalwe pali mufuko wa mifwi,

english: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
translation: Kabalwe alapwa imilundu uwabula ukutuushako,

english: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
translation: Lyonse ilyo ipenga lyalila, atila, ‘Eya!’

english: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?
translation: “Bushe iwe Yobo, niwe upanda pungwa amano yakulela,

english: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
translation: Bushe niwe weba kapumpe ukuti apupukile mu mulu apatali,

english: On the cliff he dwells and makes his home, on the point of the cliff and the stronghold.
translation: Ubushiku asendama pa mulu wa mabwe ayatali,

english: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.
translation: Palya pene epo wena alengwila akatalamukila,

english: They bow themselves. They bear their young. They end their labor pains.
translation: Bushe walimona ifyo shikontama pakukwata utwana,

english: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
translation: Aliisha utwana twakwe ifya mulopa,

english: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.
translation: Utwana twashiko tutila nga twakula twakwata amaka mulya mu matololo,

english: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,
translation: “Nani uulenga ukuti punda wa mpanga aleyendela?

english: whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?
translation: Nine ne mwine nalenga ukuti aleikala mu matololo,

english: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.
translation: Punda wa mpanga apata icibi icongo ca mu mushi,

english: The range of the mountains is his pasture. He searches after every green thing.
translation: Wena apitanafye mu mpili emwaba ifyakulya,

english: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?
translation: “Bushe iwe imboo kuti yasumina ukukubombela?

english: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.
translation: Panuma ya ifi, Yobo ayasamwine akanwa kakwe no kulapisha ubushiku afyelwemo.

english: because it didn’t shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.
translation: Pantu tabwanjisalile mwifumo lyakwa mayo

english: “Why didn’t I die from the womb? Why didn’t I give up the spirit when my mother bore me?
translation: Cinshi nshafwililefye pakufyalwa,

english: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?
translation: Cinshi kwabelele amakufi ayakumpokelela,

english: For now I should have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would have been at rest,
translation: Ne mwine fino nga ninambalala nga ndi mu mutelelwe,

english: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built up waste places for themselves;
translation: pamo ne shamfumu na bacilolo ba mu calo,

english: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver;
translation: Nga nindala utulo pamo pene na bana ba mfumu abakwete golide,

english: or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw light.
translation: Nelyo cinshi bashamposelefye nga kapopo,

english: There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.
translation: Kulya uko ababi baleka ukubilimuka,

english: There the prisoners are at ease together. They don’t hear the voice of the taskmaster.
translation: Uko abafungwa bekala pamo mu cibote,

english: The small and the great are there. The servant is free from his master.
translation: Abalanda na bakankala baba pamo,

english: Job answered:
translation: Elyo Yobo atile,

english: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,
translation: “Mulandu nshi ulubuuto lupeelelwa ku muntu uuli mu bulanda,

english: who long for death, but it doesn’t come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,
translation: Abo abafwaisha ukufwa, lelo imfwa nayo taimoneka,

english: who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?
translation: Bena balasamwa nganshi,

english: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
translation: Cinshi bengasanikila umuntu ulubuuto uushilemona inshila,

english: For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.
translation: Ukushinshimukila ekwisa nge cakulya candi,

english: For the thing which I fear comes on me, that which I am afraid of comes to me.
translation: Pantu icintu naletiina nganshi ecamponena,

english: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither do I have rest; but trouble comes.”
translation: Ine nshimona mutende, nangu umutelelwe,

english: “Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which said, ‘There is a boy conceived.’
translation: “Akasuba nafyelwemo kakalobelele

english: Let that day be darkness. Don’t let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.
translation: Kalya kasuba nakakaluke imfifi,

english: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes the day black terrify it.
translation: Lekeni imfifi ikalamba ne cinshingwa ca mfwa,

english: As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.
translation: Ala ubu bushiku bukupwe ne mfifi,

english: Behold, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come therein.
translation: Ee, lekeni mwiba nangu cimo muli ubu bushiku,

english: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan.
translation: Lekeni abo abatipwila inshiku batipwile ubu bushiku,

english: Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,
translation: Lekeni intanda sha ku macaca isha bulya bushiku shishime.

english: Moreover the LORD answered Job,
translation: Yawe epakweba Yobo ati,

english: “Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.
translation: Nga efyo caba, kanshi uifwike ubukankala no bucindami,

english: Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and bring him low.
translation: Uilange nefyo wakalipa,

english: Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in their place.
translation: Ushuluke no muntu onse uwacilumba,

english: Hide them in the dust together. Bind their faces in the hidden place.
translation: Ubashiike bonse mu lukungu,

english: Then I will also admit to you that your own right hand can save you.
translation: Nga wacita ifi, lyena ninshi nalakusuminisha,

english: “See now behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.
translation: “Tala, tamba bemoti , ine naibumba nga filya nabumba iwe,

english: Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.
translation: Kabili ubale umone ifyo yaba na maka mu musana,

english: He moves his tail like a cedar. The sinews of his thighs are knit together.
translation: Umucila waiko watonkomana nge cimuti ca keda,

english: His bones are like tubes of bronze. His limbs are like bars of iron.
translation: Amafupa mu mungololo waiko yaba kwati ni mpanda sha mukuba,

english: He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.
translation: “Bemoti yalicindama pa fibumbwa fyonse ifyakwa Lesa,

english: “Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty? He who argues with God, let him answer it.”
translation: “Bushe iwe we ulepashanya no Mwine wa maka yonse, kuti wamulanga ifyakucita?

english: Surely the mountains produce food for him, where all the animals of the field play.
translation: Impili eshiiletela icakulya

english: He lies under the lotus trees, in the covert of the reed, and the marsh.
translation: Bemoti isendama mu macinda,

english: The lotuses cover him with their shade. The willows of the brook surround him.
translation: Yatemwa ukuuba mu cintelelwe ca mpupunga sha macinda,

english: Behold, if a river overflows, he doesn’t tremble. He is confident, though the Jordan swells even to his mouth.
translation: Nangufye yaibila panshi ya menshi, awe yena taitunsha mutima,

english: Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?
translation: Nani engekata bemoti nga ilelolesha?

english: Then Job answered the LORD,
translation: Elyo Yobo ayasuka Yawe ati,

english: “Behold, I am of small account. What will I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
translation: “Tapali ifyo ndi ine uwakuti ningamwasuka,

english: I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”
translation: Ine ninanda umuku umo, kabili nafilwa ukwasuka.

english: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind:
translation: Elyo Yawe asosha Yobo ukufuma mu cimwela ati,

english: “Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.
translation: “Eico kakisha umushipi mu musana nge mpalume ya bulwi,

english: Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?
translation: “Bushe emukuti ulefwaya ukusuusha ubupingushi bwandi?

english: Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?
translation: Bushe na iwe, wakwata amaka nga yakwa Lesa?

english: “Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?
translation: “Bushe iwe kuti waloba cishimweshimwe ci Lefiatani ku bulobo?

english: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand before me?
translation: Takwaba uwingakwata amaka yakucibala,

english: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.
translation: Nga nani uwingesa ilishanya ukuti nalimukwatila imisha pakuti imulipile?

english: “I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.
translation: “Ine nshingafilwa ukukweba palwa myendo yakwe,

english: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who will come within his jaws?
translation: Nani uwingafunda umukupo wakwe,

english: Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
translation: Amalu 74:14

english: Strong scales are his pride, shut up together with a close seal.
translation: Panuma yaciko patantama imitande ya nkwela,

english: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.
translation: Shalikambantana

english: They are joined to one another. They stick together, so that they can’t be pulled apart.
translation: Shalikambatana

english: His sneezing flashes out light. His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
translation: Cena nga catesemuna palabyata insase,

english: Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap out.
translation: Mu kanwa kaciko mufuma ulubingu lwa mulilo,

english: Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?
translation: Bushe kuti wapisha umwando mu mona waciko,

english: Out of his nostrils a smoke goes, as of a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.
translation: Mu myona yaciko mufutumuka icushi,

english: His breath kindles coals. A flame goes out of his mouth.
translation: Umupu waciko ulasha amalasha,

english: There is strength in his neck. Terror dances before him.
translation: Mu mukoshi waciko emwaba amaka,

english: The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can’t be moved.
translation: Umutika wa munofu waciko walikambantana,

english: His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.
translation: Umutima waciko wakosa nge libwe,

english: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. They retreat before his thrashing.
translation: Ilyo caibuka, abamaka bonse baitutuminafye,

english: Will he make many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?
translation: Bushe kuti cishimweshimwe cakupapata iwe,

english: Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a servant forever?
translation: Bushe kuti waumfwana naco pakuti cilekubombela,

english: Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for your girls?
translation: Bushe kuti walacangasha nga akoni kalya umuntu ateeka,

english: Will traders barter for him? Will they part him among the merchants?
translation: Bushe abamakwebo kuti bapangana palwa kushitisha cishimweshimwe,

english: Can you fill his skin with barbed irons, or his head with fish spears?
