translation: Bushe kuti watulaula umubili waciko ku meela aya mabanga?

english: Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.
translation: Nga cakuti waesha ukucikumanya,

english: Behold, the hope of him is in vain. Won’t one be cast down even at the sight of him?
translation: Ukulwisha ukucikata ninshi uleibepafye,

english: Then Job answered the LORD:
translation: Elyo Yobo ayasuka Yawe ati,

english: The LORD restored Job’s prosperity when he prayed for his friends. The LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
translation: Ilyo Yobo apwile ukupepelako bacibusa bakwe, elyo Yawe abweseshe Yobo ifyuma nakabili, icakuti lyena fyacilapo imiku ibili pa fyuma akwete pakutendeka.

english: Then all his brothers, all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, came to him and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that the LORD had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money, and everyone a ring of gold.
translation: Bamunyina bonse na bankashi yakwe bonse abakwa Yobo, pamo na bacibusa bakwe bonse abakale epakwisa mukumona Yobo, no kwisa mukuipakisha nankwe mu ŋanda mumwakwe. Balamulangulukila no kumutalalika umutima pa macushi yonse ayo Yawe amuletele. Bonse umo umo basha bamupeelako indalama ne mbalaminwe ya golide.

english: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
translation: Yawe epakupaala imikalile yakwa Yobo ukucila na pafyo aikele kale. Yobo akwata impaanga amakana ikumi na yane (14,000), ingamila amakana mutanda (6,000), iŋombe ishilume ishakulima na pulao ikana limo (1,000), na bapunda abakota ikana limo (1,000).

english: He had also seven sons and three daughters.
translation: Akwata abana abaume cine lubali elyo na bana abanakashi batatu.

english: He called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren Happuch.
translation: Umwana wakwe umwanakashi uwapakubala amwinika ishina lya Yemima , uwabubili amwinika ishina lya Kesia no walenga butatu amwinika ishina lya Kereni Hapuki .

english: In all the land were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
translation: Mu calo conse tamwali abanakashi abali abasuma nga bamwana Yobo. Shibo nao alibaakenyeko ifyuma pamo pene na bandume shabo ifyo ali nokubashila pa kufwa kwakwe.

english: After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, to four generations.
translation: Ilyo amacushi yakwe yapwile, Yobo aikele pano calo imyaka umwanda umo na makumi yane (140). Amwene abana bakwe na beshikulu bakwe ukushinta na ku nkulo yalenga bune.

english: So Job died, being old and full of days.
translation: Asukile Yobo afwa ninshi ali umukote uwa nshiku ishingi.

english: “I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.
translation: “Ine nalishiba ukuti niwe we mwine uwingacita icili conse,

english: You asked, ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ therefore I have uttered that which I didn’t understand, things too wonderful for me, which I didn’t know.
translation: Nawipusha ukuti ni nani uyo uwingacila mu bupingushi bwandi ukwabula amano?

english: You said, ‘Listen, now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.’
translation: “Wacinjeba ati, ‘Ikala tondolo, pakuti nkwebe,

english: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
translation: Kale nakwishibe mukukumfwa kuli bambi,

english: Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”
translation: Eico nabwesha amashiwi yandi yonse ayo nalanda,

english: It was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.
translation: Panuma ilyo Yawe apwisha ukweba Yobo aya mashiwi, elyo aeba Elifasi umwina Temani ati, “Ine ninkufulilwa nganshi iwe pamo na babiyo bene babili, pantu tamwacilalanda ifyacishinka pali ine nga filya umubomfi wandi Yobo acilalanda.

english: Now therefore, take to yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept him, that I not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.”
translation: Kanshi imwe kabuuleni bacilume ba ŋombe cine lubali, na basukusuku nabo cine lubali, muye nabo ku mubomfi wandi Yobo, muye boca pakutuula ilambo lyakuipapatilako mwe bene. Elyo muli iyi ine nshila, no mubomfi wandi Yobo alaya mupapatilako pantu ena ndeisa umfwa ipepo lyakwe, elyo nsuuleko ku cilubo cenu icakukanalanda bwino nga filya Yobo acilanda.”

english: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what the LORD commanded them, and the LORD accepted Job.
translation: Elyo Elifasi umwina Temani, na Biludadi umwina Shuha, na Sofari umwina Namati bayacita ifyo Yawe abebele, na Yawe asumina ne pepo lyapepele Yobo.

english: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,
translation: Elifasi umwina Temani ayasuka ati,

english: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
translation: Ukubuluma kwa nkalamo

english: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.
translation: Inkalamo iyamaka nganshi naifwa pantu taikwete ifyakulya,

english: “Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.
translation: “Nomba kwalishile kulesokelela icebo kuli ine,

english: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
translation: Cali mu nshita ifiloto fipoka amano,

english: fear came on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.
translation: Kanshi naliketwe no mwenso uukalamba nalatutumafye,

english: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.
translation: Yobo 33:15

english: It stood still, but I couldn’t discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,
translation: Umupashi waiminina shika,

english: ‘Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?
translation: ‘Bushe umwinakufwa kuti aba umololoke pa cinso cakwa Lesa?

english: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.
translation: Nga cakuti na mu babomfi bakwe bene tapaba abo atetekela,

english: How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!
translation: nga palibufi abantu ababumbwa ukufuma ku lukungu,

english: “If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?
translation: “Umuntu nga akwebako ishiwi limo, bushe tacakukalipe?

english: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.
translation: Akacelo epo bali, icungulo baonaika,

english: Isn’t their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.’
translation: Na fyonse ifyo bakwata fyaonaikila pamo nabo ,

english: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.
translation: Mona walifunda abantu abengi,

english: Your words have supported him who was falling, you have made the feeble knees firm.
translation: Amashiwi yobe yatungilila nabo abalelubantika,

english: But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.
translation: Nomba na iwe cakufikila, wafilwa ukushipikisha,

english: Isn’t your piety your confidence? Isn’t the integrity of your ways your hope?
translation: Bushe akatiina kobe aka kuli Yawe temwaba ukutetekela kobe?

english: “Remember, now, who ever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?
translation: “Tala tontonkanya. Bushe walimonapo umuntu umo uwaololoka umutima aloba?

english: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity and sow trouble, reap the same.
translation: Ine ifyo namonapo nifi.

english: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.
translation: Ku mupu wakwa Lesa balaloba,

english: “Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
translation: “Kuuta we Yobo, bushe pali uulekwasuka mwa?

english: who gives rain on the earth, and sends waters on the fields;
translation: Eulosha imfula pa calo,

english: so that he sets up on high those who are low, those who mourn are exalted to safety.
translation: Eusansabalika abalanda,

english: He frustrates the plans of the crafty, so that their hands can’t perform their enterprise.
translation: Alonaula na mapange ya ncenjeshi,

english: He takes the wise in their own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.
translation: Abuula abamano no kubekatila mu bucenjeshi bwabo,

english: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.
translation: Akasuba bena baponenwa ne mfifi,

english: But he saves from the sword of their mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.
translation: Lelo ena apususha abalanda ku lupanga,

english: So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.
translation: Kanshi Lesa alalenga abalanda ukuti bakwate isubilo nakabili,

english: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.
translation: “Alishuka uo Lesa akalipila,

english: For he wounds and binds up. He injures and his hands make whole.
translation: Pantu Lesa alacena ifilonda, kabili afikakila

english: He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil will touch you.
translation: Kol 3:19

english: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.
translation: Pantu icipyu cipaya umuntu imbulwamano,

english: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.
translation: Mu nshita ya cipowe akakupususha ku mfwa,

english: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither will you be afraid of destruction when it comes.
translation: Lesa akakupokololako ku bukali bwa lwambo lwa lulimi,

english: You will laugh at destruction and famine, neither will you be afraid of the animals of the earth.
translation: Pa nshita ya bonaushi ne cipowe, iwe ukalaseka,

english: For you will be allied with the stones of the field. The animals of the field will be at peace with you.
translation: Ukacita icipangano camutende na mabwe ya mu cilime cobe,

english: You will know that your tent is in peace. You will visit your fold, and will miss nothing.
translation: Ukeshiba nokuti itenti lyobe lili umutelelwe,

english: You will know also that your offspring will be great, your offspring as the grass of the earth.
translation: Elyo ukeshiba nokuti abana ba bufyashi bobe bakaba abengi nganshi,

english: You will come to your grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.
translation: Ukaya mu nindi ninshi naukota nganshi ne mfwi tutu ku mutwe,

english: Behold, we have researched it. It is so. Hear it, and know it for your good.”
translation: “Wamona ifi fyonse twalifipitulukamo pa nshita itali no kumona ukuti fyacishinka,

english: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
translation: Nalimonapo umuntu imbulwamano uuleikala bwino,

english: His children are far from safety. They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver them,
translation: Abana bakwe bashala insansalila ukwabula ubucingo,

english: whose harvest the hungry eat up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their substance.
translation: Abantu abansala ebakalya ifisabo fyakwe,

english: For affliction doesn’t come out of the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground;
translation: Pantu ubucushi tabufuma ku lukungu iyoo,

english: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
translation: Lelo umuntunse ena nga afyalwa asanga ubucushi,

english: “But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,
translation: “Nga nine kuti nabutukila kuli Lesa.

english: who does great things that can’t be fathomed, marvelous things without number;
translation: Pantu Lesa eucita ifipapwa ifyo tushingeshiba,

english: Then Job answered,
translation: Elyo Yobo ayasuka ati,

english: Let it still be my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
translation: Ici ecingalenga ukuti mpemwineko,

english: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?
translation: Bushe ine ncili na maka yakushipikisha ukwikala pano calo?

english: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of bronze?
translation: Bushe amaka yandi kuti yalingana na mabwe ukukosa,

english: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, that wisdom is driven away from me?
translation: Mu cishinkafye amaka muli ine nayapwafye yonse ayakuti njafwilishe,

english: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
translation: “Umuntu uuli uwafupuka pa mulandu wakucula eukabila ukukoseleshiwa na banankwe,

english: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;
translation: Nomba imwe mwe bamunyinane namumbepa,

english: which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.
translation: Aya menshi yaba ayafundauka pantu yafuma ku menshi makasa ayalesunguluka

english: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
translation: Lelo mu nshita ya lusuba yalakama,

english: The caravans that travel beside them turn away. They go up into the waste, and perish.
translation: Abalendo abenda mu milongo ya ngamila balafuma mu nshila,

english: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.
translation: Abalendo abenda mu milongo ya ngamila ukufuma ku Tema balayafwaya,

english: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
translation: “Iyee nga cakuti ubulanda bwandi bwapimwa,

english: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.
translation: Nomba ukucetekela kwabo kuba kwakuicushafye,

english: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.
translation: Efyo nemwe bene muli kuli ine,

english: Did I ever say, ‘Give to me’? or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance’?
translation: Bushe nalitala mulomba icabupe,

english: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand’? or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors’?
translation: Atemwa, ukutila mpususheniko ku minwe ya balwani bandi,

english: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand my error.
translation: “Mfundeniko, ndebafye tondolo,

english: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?
translation: Amashiwi ya mu bufumacumi yalakalifya,

english: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?
translation: Bushe mulefwaya tuletalikana pa mashiwi ayafye,

english: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.
translation: Imwe kuti mwapendwila pa mwana wanshiwa,

english: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I will not lie to your face.
translation: “Aleni nomba pilibukeni no kundolesha mundoleshe,

english: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.
translation: Tontonkanyenipo nakabili. Ine nshilefwaya ulufyengo nakabili,

english: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore my words have been rash.
translation: Ala kuti fyafinapo ukucila umusensenga wa mu lulamba lwa bemba,

english: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?
translation: Bushe kwena muli ubufi mufyo ndelanda ine,

english: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.
translation: Pantu ine nalilaswa ne mifwi ya Mwine wa maka yonse,

english: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?
translation: Bushe punda wa mpanga alalila nga alelya icani,

english: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
translation: Nga kanshi nani engalya ifyakulya ifyatalala tondolo umwabula umucele?

english: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.
translation: Ine nshikwete nsala yakulya ifyakulya fya musango uyu.

english: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,
translation: “Iye, nga kuti nakwata ico ndelomba,

english: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
translation: Nangu nga kuti casekesha Lesa ukunjipaya,

english: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?
translation: “Bushe ubumi bwa muntu pano isonde tabwaba bwakubomba imilimo iyakosa,

english: He will return no more to his house, neither will his place know him any more.
translation: Takatale abwelela ku ŋanda yakwe,

english: “Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
translation: “Eico ine nshatalale tondolo iyoo,

english: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
translation: Bushe nine bemba nangu shimweshimwe wa muli bemba pakuti mulenonda?

english: When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me. My couch will ease my complaint,’
translation: Nga nalala pa musengele wandi nati, ‘Nalatuushako, no tulo twalantalalikako,

english: then you scare me with dreams and terrify me through visions,
translation: Elyo nomba iwe wandetela ifiloto ifyakuntiinya,

english: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.
translation: icakuti kuti natemwapo ukupwilila ku tulo no kufwa,

english: I loathe my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
translation: Ine napata ubumi bwandi, nshifwaya ukwikalilila pano calo,

english: What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,
translation: “Ngo muntu wanshi uwakuti ulemucindamika,

english: that you should visit him every morning, and test him every moment?
translation: uwakuti ulemupempula cila kacelo,

english: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow down my spittle?
translation: Bushe tekuti utale ufumyeko amenso kuli ine,

english: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,
translation: Kwati musha uulefwaya icintelelwe,

english: If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I am a burden to myself?
translation: Nga nalibifya, finshi nacita kuli iwe we umona imitima ya bantu?

english: Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now will I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I will not be.”
translation: Cinshi teti umbeleleko uluse pa fyabupulumushi fyandi,

english: so I am made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.
translation: Elyo na ine balimpimina imyeshi umushaba icakumwenamo,

english: When I lie down, I say, ‘When will I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
translation: Nga nasendama nati, ‘Yangu pakuti buce mbuuke!’

english: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.
translation: Mu mubili wandi namo mwiswile imititi ne nkuku.

english: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
translation: Inshiku shandi shilepita ulubilo ukucila na pa kakupikwilako insalu,

english: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye will no more see good.
translation: “Ibukisha we Lesa ukuti ubumi bwandi bwabafye ngo mupu,

english: The eye of him who sees me will see me no more. Your eyes will be on me, but I will not be.
translation: Ilinso ililendolesha nomba, talyakamone nakabili,

english: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol will come up no more.
translation: Nga filya fine ikumbi lisalangana no kupita,

english: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,
translation: Elyo Biludadi umwina Shuha nao alandapo ati,

english: Shall they not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of their heart?
translation: Bushe teti ifikolwe fyamano fikufundeko no kukweba?

english: “Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the rushes grow without water?
translation: “Bushe ifibale kuti fyamena apashili matipa?

english: While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other reed.
translation: Amenshi nga yakama, amatete nelyo tayalapakula ninshi kuma,

english: So are the paths of all who forget God. The hope of the godless man will perish,
translation: Efyo impela yaba na kuli abo abalaba Lesa,

english: whose confidence will break apart, whose trust is a spider’s web.
translation: Ico acetekelamo cintu icishakosa,

english: He will lean on his house, but it will not stand. He will cling to it, but it will not endure.
translation: Umuntu wa musango uyu nga ashintilila kwisumbu lyakwa tandabube,

english: He is green before the sun. His shoots go out along his garden.
translation: Umubi akula nge cilimwa icimena bwangu mu kasuba,

english: His roots are wrapped around the rock pile. He sees the place of stones.
translation: Imishila yaciko yapeka mu mwina wa mabwe,

english: If he is destroyed from his place, then it will deny him, saying, ‘I have not seen you.’
translation: Lelo nga mwanukula ici cilimwa,

english: Behold, this is the joy of his way. Out of the earth, others will spring.
translation: Efyo ubumi bwa cilimwa bupwa,

english: “How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?
translation: “Bushe iwe Yobo, ukafisha lilali ukulalanda ifi,

english: “Behold, God will not cast away a blameless man, neither will he uphold the evildoers.
translation: “Iwe Yobo wishibe ukuti Lesa talekelesha abololoke,

english: He will still fill your mouth with laughter, your lips with shouting.
translation: Lesa akalenga ukuti akanwa kobe kakesulemo inseko,

english: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame. The tent of the wicked will be no more.”
translation: Ala Lesa akalenga abalwani bobe ukwikatwa insoni,

english: Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
translation: Bushe Lesa kuti akaana ukucita umulinganya?

english: If your children have sinned against him, he has delivered them into the hand of their disobedience.
translation: Ilyo abana bobe babifishe kuli ena,

english: If you want to seek God diligently, make your supplication to the Almighty.
translation: Kanshi iwe pilibukila kuli Lesa,

english: If you were pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you, and make the habitation of your righteousness prosperous.
translation: Nga uli wakaele kabili umololoke,

english: Though your beginning was small, yet your latter end would greatly increase.
translation: Nangu imikalile yobe iya kunuma ishali iyafikapo nganshi,

english: “Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers.
translation: “Ipusha inkulo ishatangila,

english: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)
translation: Pantu ifwe fwe bana ba nomba tatwaishiba nangu cimo,

english: Then Job answered,
translation: Elyo Yobo ayasuka ati,

english: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.
translation: Kuti twafilwa ukutasha ubukulu bwa fintu ifyo Lesa acita,

english: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.
translation: Moneni nga apita apo ndi, teti mumone,

english: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’
translation: Nga aisa mukusenda ico alefwaya, nani engamulesha?

english: “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.
translation: Lesa tabwesha umutima nga afulwa,

english: How much less will I answer him, and choose my words to argue with him?
translation: “Nomba ine kuti namwasuka shani?

english: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.
translation: Nangufye ningaba uwakaele teti mwasuke,

english: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.
translation: Nangufye ningamwita nao nokwisa aisa,

english: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.
translation: Yobo 4:17

english: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
translation: Teti aleke nokuti mpemwineko,

english: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’
translation: Nga nati nande pa maka, owe ala alikwatisha amaka!

english: “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?
translation: “Ee cine cine ninjishiba ukuti efyo caba,

english: Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me. Though I am blameless, it will prove me perverse.
translation: Nelyo ningatontonkanya ukuti ndi wakaele,

english: I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.
translation: “Kwena kuti natila ndi wakaele,

english: “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.
translation: Ala eco nsosele nati, ‘Cimo cinefye,

english: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.
translation: Ubwembya nga bwaleta imfwa yakupumikisha,

english: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?
translation: Icalo nga caponena mu minwe ya bantu ababi,

english: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away. They see no good.
translation: “Inshiku shandi shilepita bwangu ukucila na pa balebutuka ulubilo,

english: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.
translation: Shileuluka kwati bwato bulya bapikula ku matete,

english: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up,’
translation: Nga natontonkanya nati, ‘Limbi kandekefye ukuilishanya,

english: I am afraid of all my sorrows. I know that you will not hold me innocent.
translation: Nomba nga naibukisha amacushi yandi, umwenso wanjikata,

english: I will be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
translation: Apo ndi wa milandu,

english: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.
translation: Nangu umuntu engapanga ukutalikana na Lesa,

english: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,
translation: Nangu ningasamba bwino mu menshi ya bunga bwa mfula ,

english: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes will abhor me.
translation: Yobo 38:31

english: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.
translation: Pantu Lesa te muntu nga ine uwakuti tulepashanya nankwe,

english: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.
translation: Nga cakuti kwali uwakukalulula pali ifwe babili,

english: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;
translation: uwingasesha icisendo cakwa Lesa icaba pali ine,

english: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.
translation: Lyena kuti nalanda ukwabula ukumutiina,

english: God is wise in heart, and mighty in strength. Who has hardened himself against him and prospered?
translation: Alikwatisha amano, kabili alikwatisha na maka ayengi,

english: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.
translation: Lesa alasesha impili ukwabula nokuti ishine shishibe,

english: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.
translation: Lesa alaleta icinkukuma no kusunkanya icalo,

english: He commands the sun and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.
translation: Ena kuti aeba akasuba ukukanatula,

english: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.
translation: Umwinefye eka ewayanshile umulu,

english: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.
translation: Ni Lesa ewasamika intanda mu mulu,

english: The LORD’s word that came to Joel, the son of Pethuel.
translation: Aya e mashiwi yakwa Yawe ayaishile kuli Yoeli mwana Petueli, ayakuti:

english: The field is laid waste. The land mourns, for the grain is destroyed, The new wine has dried up, and the oil languishes.
translation: Pantu mu mabala tamushele nelyo kamo.

english: Be confounded, you farmers! Wail, you vineyard keepers, for the wheat and for the barley; for the harvest of the field has perished.
translation: Kwateni insoni, imwe mwe balimi,

english: The vine has dried up, and the fig tree withered— the pomegranate tree, the palm tree also, and the apple tree, even all of the trees of the field are withered; for joy has withered away from the sons of men.
translation: Imishila ya myangashi nayuma,

english: Put on sackcloth and mourn, you priests! Wail, you ministers of the altar. Come, lie all night in sackcloth, you ministers of my God, for the meal offering and the drink offering are withheld from your God’s house.
translation: Mwe bashimapepo fwaleni insalu shabulanda,

english: Sanctify a fast. Call a solemn assembly. Gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land to the house of the LORD, your God, and cry to the LORD.
translation: Konkomesheni abantu ukuti bafunge ukulya,

english: Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is at hand, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
translation: Yangu ubushiku!

english: Isn’t the food cut off before our eyes, joy and gladness from the house of our God?
translation: Bushe ifyakulya fyesu tafisendelwe,

english: The seeds rot under their clods. The granaries are laid desolate. The barns are broken down, for the grain has withered.
translation: Imbuto nashuminina mu mushili ushilokelelwa ku mfula,

english: How the animals groan! The herds of livestock are perplexed, because they have no pasture. Yes, the flocks of sheep are made desolate.
translation: Yangu ifyo ifinama filelila ku nsala!

english: LORD, I cry to you, for the fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame has burned all the trees of the field.
translation: Ni kuli iwe we Yawe ndelilila,

english: Hear this, you elders, and listen, all you inhabitants of the land! Has this ever happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
translation: Umfweni kuno, imwe mwe bakalamba,

english: Yes, the animals of the field pant to you, for the water brooks have dried up, and the fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
translation: Ne nama sha mu mpanga nomba shilelililafye kuli imwe,

english: Tell your children about it, and have your children tell their children, and their children, another generation.
translation: Muleshimikilako abana benu,

english: What the swarming locust has left, the great locust has eaten. What the great locust has left, the grasshopper has eaten. What the grasshopper has left, the caterpillar has eaten.
translation: Ala ifintu ifyo makanta ulya aputaula ashileko,

english: Wake up, you drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you drinkers of wine, because of the sweet wine, for it is cut off from your mouth.
translation: Shibukeni imwe mwe bacakolwa nokulila.

english: For a nation has come up on my land, strong, and without number. His teeth are the teeth of a lion, and he has the fangs of a lioness.
translation: Pantu makanta uwingi nakupa icalo candi,

english: He has laid my vine waste, and stripped my fig tree. He has stripped its bark, and thrown it away. Its branches are made white.
translation: Uyu makanta naonaula imishila yandi iya myangashi,

english: Mourn like a virgin dressed in sackcloth for the husband of her youth!
translation: Ubuso 9:8

english: The meal offering and the drink offering are cut off from the LORD’s house. The priests, the LORD’s ministers, mourn.
translation: Takushele umutuulo wa cabunga nangu uwa fyakunwa,

english: Blow the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of the LORD comes, for it is close at hand:
translation: Lisheni ipenga mu Sioni,

english: The earth quakes before them. The heavens tremble. The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars withdraw their shining.
translation: Isonde lilatenkana pakumona uko baleisa,

english: The LORD thunders his voice before his army, for his forces are very great; for he is strong who obeys his command; for the day of the LORD is great and very awesome, and who can endure it?
translation: Yawe asansule shiwi ku ntanshi ya fita fyakwe,

english: “Yet even now,” says the LORD, “turn to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning.”
translation: Ubuso 8:12

english: Tear your heart and not your garments, and turn to the LORD, your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.
translation: Pakulanga ubulanda, lepuleni imitima yenu,

english: Who knows? He may turn and relent, and leave a blessing behind him, even a meal offering and a drink offering to the LORD, your God.
translation: Nga ni nani engeshiba nga cakuti Yawe Lesa wesu kuti abwesha umutima,

english: Blow the trumpet in Zion! Sanctify a fast. Call a solemn assembly.
translation: Lisheni ipenga mu Sioni,

english: Gather the people. Sanctify the assembly. Assemble the elders. Gather the children, and those who nurse from breasts. Let the bridegroom go out of his room, and the bride out of her chamber.
translation: Longanikeni abantu pamo,

english: Let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, “Spare your people, LORD, and don’t give your heritage to reproach, that the nations should rule over them. Why should they say among the peoples, ‘Where is their God?’”
translation: Ubuso 6:17

english: Then the LORD was jealous for his land, and had pity on his people.
translation: Elyo Yawe akakwata ubufuba pa calo cakwe,

english: The LORD answered his people, “Behold, I will send you grain, new wine, and oil, and you will be satisfied with them; and I will no more make you a reproach among the nations.
translation: Elyo pakwasuka abantu bakwe, Yawe akabeba ati,

english: A day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness. As the dawn spreading on the mountains, a great and strong people; there has never been the like, neither will there be any more after them, even to the years of many generations.
translation: Bukaba ubushiku bwa mfifi, nayo iyafiita fititi,

english: But I will remove the northern army far away from you, and will drive it into a barren and desolate land, its front into the eastern sea, and its back into the western sea; and its stench will come up, and its bad smell will rise.” Surely he has done great things.
translation: “Nalatalusha umulwani wa ku kapinda ka ku kuso ukufuma kuli imwe,

english: Land, don’t be afraid. Be glad and rejoice, for the LORD has done great things.
translation: Iwe we calo leka ukutiina!

english: Don’t be afraid, you animals of the field; for the pastures of the wilderness spring up, for the tree bears its fruit. The fig tree and the vine yield their strength.
translation: Na imwe mwe nama sha mu mpanga mwitiina,

english: “Be glad then, you children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD, your God; for he gives you the early rain in just measure, and he causes the rain to come down for you, the early rain and the latter rain, as before.
translation: Na imwe mwe bena Sioni sansamukeni,

english: The threshing floors will be full of wheat, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
translation: Apakupumina iŋanu pakaba imina iyikulu,

english: I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my great army, which I sent among you.
translation: “Ndi nokumubwesesha ifya pa myaka yonse

english: You will have plenty to eat and be satisfied, and will praise the name of the LORD, your God, who has dealt wondrously with you; and my people will never again be disappointed.
translation: Kanshi nomba mwakulakwata ifilyo ifingi,

english: You will know that I am among Israel, and that I am the LORD, your God, and there is no one else; and my people will never again be disappointed.
translation: Elyo mwe bena Israeli mukeshiba ukuti kanshi ine naba pakati kenu,

english: A fire devours before them, and behind them, a flame burns. The land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them, a desolate wilderness. Yes, and no one has escaped them.
translation: Ku ntanshi yabo fyonse fyaonaulwa ku mulilo ulepya.

english: Their appearance is as the appearance of horses, and they run as horsemen.
translation: Imimonekele yabo yaba kwati ni bakabalwe,

english: Like the noise of chariots on the tops of the mountains, they leap, like the noise of a flame of fire that devours the stubble, like a strong people set in battle array.
translation: Ilyo baletolauka pa mulu wa mpili,

english: At their presence the peoples are in anguish. All faces have grown pale.
translation: Abantu aba mitundu yonse balekatwa umwenso

english: They run like mighty men. They climb the wall like warriors. They each march in his line, and they don’t swerve off course.
translation: Ubuso 9:7-9

english: One doesn’t jostle another. They each march in their own path. They burst through the defenses and don’t break ranks.
translation: Takuba nelyo umo uwakupunka umubiye iyoo.

english: They rush on the city. They run on the wall. They climb up into the houses. They enter in at the windows like thieves.
translation: Nga balasansa umusumba,

english: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,
translation: “Pantu mu nshiku shine shilya, kabili pa nshita ine ilya, elyo nkabwesesha abena Yuda na bena Yerusalemu ishuko lyabo.

english: I will gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat; and I will execute judgment on them there for my people, and for my heritage, Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations. They have divided my land,
translation: Kabili elintu nkalonganika imishobo ya benafyalo yonse, no kubaleta mwishika lya Yehoshafati. Emo nkabalubulwisha bonse pali fyonse ifyo bacita ku bantu bandi abena Israeli ababa icikwatwa candi. Pantu ebabasalanganishishe mu fyalo fimbi ifya benafyalo, basha bayakana ne calo candi ica Israeli.

english: and have cast lots for my people, and have given a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine, that they may drink.
translation: Iyi ine imishobo eyalependula pakwakana bantu bandi. Yaleshitisha abalumendo pakuti ikwatilepo bacilende, kabili yaleshitisha abakashana pakuti inwenepo umwangashi.

english: “Yes, and what are you to me, Tyre and Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Will you repay me? And if you repay me, I will swiftly and speedily return your repayment on your own head.
translation: Nakuba ni cinshi ico imwe muli kuli ine, mwe bena Turi na bena Sidoni, na imwe bonse mwe ba mu ncende sha Bafilisiti? Bushe pali cimo ico mulefwaila ukucita icilandushi kuli ine? Nga efyo mulefwaya, ine nine nalalenga icilandushi ukuti cimwalukile bwangu bwangu mwe bene.

english: Because you have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried my finest treasures into your temples,
translation: Imwe nimwe mwanjibila silifa na golide, no kunsendela ifintu ifyamutengo, mwaya fibika na mu matempele yenu umo mupepela.

english: Now the LORD’s word came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
translation: Ishiwi lyakwa Yawe lyaishile kuli Yona mwana Amitai aliti,

english: Then the men were exceedingly afraid, and said to him, “What have you done?” For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.
translation: Awe bacoba umwenso wabekata nganshi pali aya mashiwi, bamwipusha abati, “Kanshi ico ucitile ni cinshi?” Kwena balishibe ukuti alefwaya ukufulumuka Yawe, pantu efyo abebele.

english: Then they said to him, “What shall we do to you, that the sea may be calm to us?” For the sea grew more and more stormy.
translation: Elyo bamwipwishe abati, “Kanshi cinshi twalakucita pakuti bemba atalale?” Pantu icimwela cilecililakofye ububi.

english: He said to them, “Take me up, and throw me into the sea. Then the sea will be calm for you; for I know that because of me this great storm is on you.”
translation: Nao epakubasuka ati, “Ala mbuulenifye mumpose muli bemba, mwalamona bemba alatalala no kutalala. Pantu nimona ukuti nine nalenga ici cimwela icikalamba nganshi ukuti cimwimine.”

english: Nevertheless the men rowed hard to get them back to the land; but they could not, for the sea grew more and more stormy against them.
translation: Bacoba ba bwato baesha na maka nganshi ukuti bafishe ubwato ku mulundu, awe bafilililwafye pantu icimwela calicilileko ububi.

english: Therefore they cried to the LORD, and said, “We beg you, LORD, we beg you, don’t let us die for this man’s life, and don’t lay on us innocent blood; for you, LORD, have done as it pleased you.”
translation: Epakulakuuta kuli Yawe abati, “We Yawe, twapapata wileka tufwile pa mulandu wa wakwipaya uyu muntu, witupeelelapo no mulandu pa mulopa uyu nga cakuti wakaele, pantu niwe we Yawe ucitile ico we mwine utemenwe.”

english: So they took up Jonah and threw him into the sea; and the sea ceased its raging.
translation: Ne cacine epakwikata Yona bamuposa na muli bemba, awe apopene na bemba atalalafye tondolo.

english: Then the men feared the LORD exceedingly; and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.
translation: Awe bacoba ba bwato pakumona ica uyu musango, batiina Yawe apakalamba, epakutuula Yawe ilambo, balaya ne filayo.

english: “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach against it, for their wickedness has come up before me.”
translation: “Ima kabiye ku Ninife kuli ulya musumba ukalamba, uye ushobaule abantu abalimo, pantu ububi bwabo nabwishibikwa kuli ine.”

english: But Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa, and found a ship going to Tarshish; so he paid its fare, and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD.
translation: Lelo Yona apanga ukufyukila ku Tashishi pakufulumuka Yawe. Aima, aya ku Yopa, eko aya sanga ubwato ubwali nokuya ku Tashishi, alipila ne fyalwendo, apatama no kupatama ukuya nabo ku Tashishi pakuti afulumuke Yawe.

english: But the LORD sent out a great wind on the sea, and there was a mighty storm on the sea, so that the ship was likely to break up.
translation: Lelo Yawe aimya umwela uukali nganshi pali bemba, paima icimwela icikalamba nganshi pali bemba icakuti no bwato bwalafwaya no kubunda.

english: Then the mariners were afraid, and every man cried to his god. They threw the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten the ship. But Jonah had gone down into the innermost parts of the ship and he was laying down, and was fast asleep.
translation: Bacoba wa bwato umwenso wabekata, elyo cila muntu alakuuta mutuule ku mulungu wakwe. Batampa no kuposa ifipe pali bemba pakuti ubwato bwangukeko. Lelo Yona ena aikile mu muputule wa panshi no kuya pona mu tulo utwine twine mukati ka bwato.

english: So the ship master came to him, and said to him, “What do you mean, sleeper? Arise, call on your God! Maybe your God will notice us, so that we won’t perish.”
translation: Mushika wa bwato aya mweba ati, “Iwe, bushe utu tulo twa musango nshi? Buuka. Nobe akupepa ku mulungu obe. Nalimo kuti watulangulukilako, watupusushako ku mfwa.”

english: They all said to each other, “Come! Let’s cast lots, that we may know who is responsible for this evil that is on us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
translation: Elyo bacoba balaebana abati, “Mwe, endesheni muleke tupendule, twishibe uwalenga ukuti uyu mupamba utuponene.” Awe balapendula, cawila Yona.

english: Then they asked him, “Tell us, please, for whose cause this evil is on us. What is your occupation? Where do you come from? What is your country? Of what people are you?”
translation: Elyo bamwipusha abati, “Twebe, bushe uwalenga uyu mupamba ukuti utuponene nani? Bushe mulimo nshi iwe ubomba? Ufumine kwi? Ku calo kumwenu ni kwi? Uli mutundu nshi?”

english: He said to them, “I am a Hebrew, and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, who has made the sea and the dry land.”
translation: Nao abasuka ati, “Ine ndi Muhibulu, kabili ine mpepa Yawe Lesa wa mu mulu, uwabumba bemba no mushili.”

english: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD, his God, out of the fish’s belly.
translation: Elyo Yona apepele kuli Yawe Lesa wakwe ilyo ali mu nda ya cisabi ati,

english: Then the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited out Jonah on the dry land.
translation: Elyo Yawe aeba icisabi, naco epakuya lukila Yona ku mulundu.

english: He said, “I called because of my affliction to the LORD. He answered me. Out of the belly of Sheol I cried. You heard my voice.
translation: “Mu kupelelwa kwandi nalilile kuli Yawe,

english: For you threw me into the depths, in the heart of the seas. The flood was all around me. All your waves and your billows passed over me.
translation: Pantu wamposele muli bemba uwashika,

english: I said, ‘I have been banished from your sight; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.’
translation: Na ine epakutila, ‘Iwe nauntamfya pa cinso cobe.

english: The waters surrounded me, even to the soul. The deep was around me. The weeds were wrapped around my head.
translation: Amenshi nayanjibisha,

english: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains. The earth barred me in forever; yet you have brought my life up from the pit, LORD my God.
translation: Nintotobela mwisamba lya mpili,

english: “When my soul fainted within me, I remembered the LORD. My prayer came in to you, into your holy temple.
translation: “Ilyo ndi mupepi no kuleka umweo,

english: Those who regard vain idols forsake their own mercy.
translation: “Abapepa ifilubi ifyabuwelewele,

english: But I will sacrifice to you with the voice of thanksgiving. I will pay that which I have vowed. Salvation belongs to the LORD.”
translation: Lelo ine kwishiwi ilyakutotela

english: The LORD’s word came to Jonah the second time, saying,
translation: Elyo ishiwi lyakwa Yawe lyaishile kuli Yona umuku wabubili aliti,

english: God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way. God relented of the disaster which he said he would do to them, and he didn’t do it.
translation: Lesa ati amone ifyo abantu bacita nefyo baleka imibeele yabo iyabipisha, Lesa epakubwesha umutima, kabili tabacitile ubonaushi ubo apangile ukubacitila.

english: “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach to it the message that I give you.”
translation: “Ima, kabiye ku Ninife kuli ulya musumba ukalamba, kabile imbila iyo nalakweba.”

english: So Jonah arose, and went to Nineveh, according to the LORD’s word. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, three days’ journey across.
translation: Yona epakwima, alaya na ku Ninife ukulingana ne shiwi Yawe amwebele. Umusumba wa Ninife wali ukalamba nganshi, pakulalanya pakati kupwisha inshiku shitatu.

english: Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he cried out, and said, “In forty days, Nineveh will be overthrown!”
translation: Kanshi Yona epakutendeka no kuya mu musumba, aenda ulwendo lwa bushiku bumo, alabila imbila aleti, “Kwashalafye inshiku amakumi yane (40), ninshi Ninife aonaulwa.”

english: The people of Nineveh believed God; and they proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their greatest even to their least.
translation: Abantu ba mu Ninife cilya baumfwa, awe basumina Lesa. Nabo babila ne mbila yakuti baleke ukulya, bafwale ne nsalu shabulanda, bonsefye ukutendekela ku bakankala ukufika na ku balanda bene.

english: The news reached the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, took off his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
translation: Ilyo imfumu ya mu Ninife yaumfwa, yaima pa cipuna caiko, yafuula ne cakufwala cabufumu, yafwala ne nsalu shabulanda, yaikala na mu mito.

english: He made a proclamation and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, “Let neither man nor animal, herd nor flock, taste anything; let them not feed, nor drink water;
translation: Nayo yapeela icebo, yacisabankanya na mu Ninife monse aiti, “Umfweni icipope icifumine ku mfumu na bacilolo baiko. Peba nelyo umo uwakulya akantu. Abantu bonse, kumo kwine ne nama, iŋombe ne mpaanga, peba uwakulya nangu ukunwa amenshi.

english: but let them be covered with sackcloth, both man and animal, and let them cry mightily to God. Yes, let them turn everyone from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands.
translation: Mwe bantu bonse, fwaleni nsalu shabulanda kumo kwine ne fitekwa, mulekuuta inkuuta ikalamba kuli Lesa. Kabili cila muntu aleke imibeele yakwe iyabipa ne fyongo ifyo alecita.

english: Who knows whether God will not turn and relent, and turn away from his fierce anger, so that we might not perish?”
translation: Nani eshibe, nalimo kuti Lesa abwesha umutima, aleka icipyu cakwe icikali, ninshi nefwe twapusukako kukufwa.”

english: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was angry.
translation: Lelo Yona ena ici cintu tacamusekeshe iyoo, afulilwe nganshi.

english: The LORD said, “You have been concerned for the vine, for which you have not labored, neither made it grow; which came up in a night and perished in a night.
translation: Elyo Yawe aeba Yona ati, “Iwe ulelangulukilafye akamuti ako iwe ushameseshe nangu ukukusha. Akene kaimenenefye pa bushiku bumo, kabili no kuma kayuminafye pa bushiku bumo.

english: Shouldn’t I be concerned for Nineveh, that great city, in which are more than one hundred twenty thousand persons who can’t discern between their right hand and their left hand, and also many animals?”
translation: Pali bufi ine, bushe nshili na kulangulukila Ninife, uyu musumba ushaikulila, umwaba abantu ukucila pa makana umwanda umo na makumi yabili (120,000) abashaishiba ukulekanya ukwabela ukuboko kwa kulyo no kwabela ukuboko kwa kuso, kabili umwaba ne fitekwa ifyafulisha nganshi?”

english: He prayed to the LORD, and said, “Please, LORD, wasn’t this what I said when I was still in my own country? Therefore I hurried to flee to Tarshish, for I knew that you are a gracious God and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and you relent of doing harm.
translation: Epakupepa kuli Yawe ati, “We Yawe, bushe tefyo ine nalandile ilyo ncili ku calo kumwesu ukuti efyo cikaba? E mulandu wine nafyukile bwangu bwangu ukuya ku Tashishi, pantu nalishibe ukuti iwe uli Lesa wacikuuku, waba no luse, taufulwa bwangu, walifulisha icitemwiko icishipwa, kabili ulabwesha umutima ilyo ufwile ukukanda.

english: Therefore now, LORD, take, I beg you, my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live.”
translation: Ecalenga nomba we Yawe, poka umweo wandi, pantu ukufwa kwawamapo ukucila ukuba umumi.”

english: The LORD said, “Is it right for you to be angry?”
translation: Isham 19:4

english: Then Jonah went out of the city and sat on the east side of the city, and there made himself a booth and sat under it in the shade, until he might see what would become of the city.
translation: Elyo Yona afumina kunse ya musumba lwa ku kabanga, aya ikala na panshi. Akuulako ne nsakwe iyakuubamo, alapembelela ukuti amone icalaponena umusumba.

english: The LORD God prepared a vine and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shade over his head to deliver him from his discomfort. So Jonah was exceedingly glad because of the vine.
translation: Ukuf 34:6

english: But God prepared a worm at dawn the next day, and it chewed on the vine so that it withered.
translation: Lelo ubushiku ubwakonkapo ilyo akasuba katula, Lesa ateyanya icinsenda, acituma naco caisa lya ishinte lya kamuti, awe kauma no kuma.

english: When the sun arose, God prepared a sultry east wind; and the sun beat on Jonah’s head, so that he was faint and requested for himself that he might die. He said, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
translation: Ilyo akasuba kasansama, Lesa ateyanya umwela uwakaba, na kasuba kalamoca pa mutwe wakwe. Yona abongoteka no kubongoteka ku cipuki, alafwaya no kufwa. Asosa no kusosa ati, “Awe, no kufwa kwawamapo ukucila ukuba umumi.”

english: God said to Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the vine?” He said, “I am right to be angry, even to death.”
translation: Lelo Lesa nao amwasuka ati, “Bushe wawamya ukufulwa pa mulandu wa kamuti, mwa?”

english: Now when Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem heard how Joshua had taken Ai, and had utterly destroyed it; as he had done to Jericho and her king, so he had done to Ai and her king; and how the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel, and were among them,
translation: Nomba Adoni Sedeki imfumu ya mu Yerusalemu yaumfwile ukuti Yoshua napoka umusumba wa Ai no kuonaula , elyo naipaya ne mfumu yauko pamo ngefyo acitile ku musumba wa Yeriko ne mfumu yauko. Nomba omfwile ukuti abantu ba mu musumba wa Gibeoni nabapanga icipangano ca kwikala umutende na bena Israeli, kabili nokuti bakulaikala mu calo cabo.

english: The LORD confused them before Israel. He killed them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them by the way of the ascent of Beth Horon, and struck them to Azekah and to Makkedah.
translation: Elyo Yawe nao abafulungenye amano ku cinso ca bena Israeli, alenga babacimfya no kubepaya ku Gibeoni. Abena Israeli batamfishe abalwani babo ukulungama umusebo walola ku Beti Horoni no kubakomaula nganshi inshila yonse ukuya fikafye na ku Aseka na ku Makeda.

english: As they fled from before Israel, while they were at the descent of Beth Horon, the LORD hurled down great stones from the sky on them to Azekah, and they died. There were more who died from the hailstones than those whom the children of Israel killed with the sword.
translation: Ilyo balefulumuka abena Israeli, pakutentemukila mu musebo uwafuma ku Beti Horoni ukuya ku Aseka, Yawe abaletele imfula yacitalawe, iya mabwe ayakulu ukufuma ku mulu, yaipaya abengi nganshi ukucila nabo baipeye ku bulwi bwa ku lupanga lwa bena Israeli.

english: Then Joshua spoke to the LORD in the day when the LORD delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel. He said in the sight of Israel, “Sun, stand still on Gibeon! You, moon, stop in the valley of Aijalon!”
translation: Mu bushiku bwine bulya Yawe apeele abena Amoli mu maboko ya bena Israeli, Yoshua asosele kuli Yawe pa cinso ca bena Israeli ati,

english: The sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged themselves of their enemies. Isn’t this written in the book of Jashar? The sun stayed in the middle of the sky, and didn’t hurry to go down about a whole day.
translation: Ne cacine akasuba kaimininafye,

english: There was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD listened to the voice of a man; for the LORD fought for Israel.
translation: Ukufumafye ku kale takwatalile akuba ubushiku ngobu ubo Yawe aumfwilile umuntu, nangufye ukubako inshita imbi ukutula pali iyi nshita. Nico pali ubu bushiku Yawe alelwilako abena Israeli.

english: Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp to Gilgal.
translation: Elyo Yoshua pamo na bena Israeli bonse babwelelamo ku nkambi ku Giligali.

english: These five kings fled, and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.
translation: Nomba imfumu ishi shisano shabutwike no kuya fisama mu ninga ya ku Makeda.

english: Joshua was told, saying, “The five kings have been found, hidden in the cave at Makkedah.”
translation: Lelo ilyo baebele Yoshua ukuti imfumu ishi shisano nabashisanga uko shibeleme mu ninga ya ku Makeda,

english: Joshua said, “Roll large stones to cover the cave’s entrance, and set men by it to guard them;
translation: Sam 1:18

english: but don’t stay there. Pursue your enemies, and attack them from the rear. Don’t allow them to enter into their cities; for the LORD your God has delivered them into your hand.”
translation: Lelo imwe mwileka ukusupila abalwani benu, mulingilefye ukubasansa mukupitila kunuma ya misumba yabo. Mwileka baleingila mu misumba yabo pantu Yawe Lesa wenu nabapeela mu maboko yenu.”

english: they were very afraid, because Gibeon was a great city, as one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty.
translation: Elyo natiina apakalamba pali ici cicitike, pantu Gibeoni wali umusumba uukalamba, kabili uukankala. Uyu musumba walifye kwati ni umo pa misumba umwaleikala imfumu. Kabili walicilile pa musumba wa Ai ku bukulu, na bantu bauko bonse bali abaume babulwi icine cine.

english: When Joshua and the children of Israel had finished killing them with a very great slaughter until they were consumed, and the remnant which remained of them had entered into the fortified cities,
translation: Eico Yoshua na bena Israeli ilyo bakomawile abalwani babo mupepi no kubapwisha. Bamo bamo ebashele baile fika ku misumba yabo,

english: all the people returned to the camp to Joshua at Makkedah in peace. None moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel.
translation: ne fita fyonse fyabwelele kuli Yoshua ku nkambi ya ku Makeda umutende. Takwali umuntu nelyo umo uwasoselepo ishiwi ilibi pa bena Israeli.

english: Then Joshua said, “Open the cave entrance, and bring those five kings out of the cave to me.”
translation: Panuma ya ifi elyo Yoshua atile, “Kesuleni umwinshi wa ninga no kufumya shilya mfumu shisano no kushileta kuli ine.”

english: They did so, and brought those five kings out of the cave to him: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.
translation: Awe nabo bafumishe imfumu shisano ukufuma mu ninga, imfumu sha bena Yerusalemu, Hebuloni, Yamuti, Lakishi elyo na Egiloni.

english: When they brought those kings out to Joshua, Joshua called for all the men of Israel, and said to the chiefs of the men of war who went with him, “Come near. Put your feet on the necks of these kings.” They came near, and put their feet on their necks.
translation: Ilyo bafishishe ishi mfumu kuli Yoshua, nao aitile bonse abana baume ba bena Israeli nokutila ku bakalamba ba fita abo ali nabo, “Iseni kuno pakuti mwise munyante amakasa yenu pa mikoshi ya ishi mfumu.” Nabo baile kuntanshi no kuya nyanta amakasa yabo pa mikoshi yabo.

english: Joshua said to them, “Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed. Be strong and courageous, for the LORD will do this to all your enemies against whom you fight.”
translation: Kabili Yoshua abebele ati, “Tecakwesha ukuba no mwenso, kabili mwinenuka. Mubefye abashipa kabili abakosa. Pantu ifi fine efyo Yawe ali nokucitila bonse abalwani benu.”

english: Afterward Joshua struck them, put them to death, and hanged them on five trees. They were hanging on the trees until the evening.
translation: Elyo Yoshua akomaula ishi mfumu, ashipaya no kushikulikila ku fimuti fisano no kubasha ifyo fine balepelela ku fimuti mpakafye ne nshita ya cungulo.

english: At the time of the going down of the sun, Joshua commanded, and they took them down off the trees, and threw them into the cave in which they had hidden themselves, and laid great stones on the mouth of the cave, which remain to this very day.
translation: Cilya akasuba kawa, Yoshua aeba abantu ukubasamuna ku fimuti no kuya baposa mu ninga umo baile fisama. Pa mwinshi wa ninga bacilikapo ifimabwe ifikulu, ifyo ificilipo no bwa lelo.

english: Joshua took Makkedah on that day, and struck it with the edge of the sword, with its king. He utterly destroyed it and all the souls who were in it. He left no one remaining. He did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
translation: Pa bushiku ubo bwine, Yoshua apokele Makeda no kwikata imfumu ya uyu musumba no kumwipaya ku lupanga. Apwishishisha ukonaula umusumba onse na bantu bonse abaleikalamo. Tamwali uwashelemo. Acitile imfumu ya ku Makeda ngefyo acitile ku mfumu ya musumba wa Yeriko.

english: Joshua passed from Makkedah, and all Israel with him, to Libnah, and fought against Libnah.
translation: Kabili panuma ya ifi fyonse, Yoshua pamo na bena Israeli bonse baimine ukufuma ku musumba wa Makeda no kuya ku musumba wa Libina mukuya balwisha.

english: Therefore Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, saying,
translation: Eico Adoni Sedeki imfumu ya mu Yerusalemu yatumine inkombe ku mfumu shibiye, Hoamu imfumu ya mu Hebuloni, Piramu imfumu ya mu Yamuti, Yafiya imfumu ya mu Lakishi elyo na kuli Debi imfumu ya mu Egiloni.

english: The LORD delivered it also, with its king, into the hand of Israel. He struck it with the edge of the sword, and all the souls who were in it. He left no one remaining in it. He did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
translation: Kabili Yawe apeela uyu musumba pamo ne mfumu yauko mu maboko ya bena Israeli. Kabili Yoshua aonawile umusumba no kwipaya abaleikalamo bonse ku lupanga. Tamwali uwashelemo nangu umo. Acitile kuli iyi imfumu ya musumba wa Libina pamo ngefyo acitile ku mfumu ya musumba wa Yeriko.

english: Joshua passed from Libnah, and all Israel with him, to Lachish, and encamped against it, and fought against it.
translation: Yoshua nakabili pamo na bena Israeli bonse bafuma mu musumba wa Libina no kuya ku musumba wa Lakishi. Baya ushinguluka no kuulwisha.

english: The LORD delivered Lachish into the hand of Israel. He took it on the second day, and struck it with the edge of the sword, with all the souls who were in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah.
translation: Kabili Yawe abalwishishako no kupeela uyu musumba mu maboko ya bena Israeli, elyo baupoka pa bushiku bwalenga shibili. Aonaula umusumba, aipaya na baleikalamo bonse ku lupanga pamo ngefyo acitile na ku musumba wa Libina.

english: Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish; and Joshua struck him and his people, until he had left him no one remaining.
translation: Elintu Holamu imfumu ya musumba wa Gesa aisa mukutulanyako umusumba wa Lakishi lelo Yoshua alimucimfishe pamo pene ne fita fyakwe. Tapashele nelyo umo.

english: Joshua passed from Lachish, and all Israel with him, to Eglon; and they encamped against it and fought against it.
translation: Yoshua nakabili pamo na bena Israeli bonse bafuma mu musumba wa Lakishi no kuya ku musumba wa Egiloni, baya ushinguluka no kuulwisha.

english: They took it on that day, and struck it with the edge of the sword. He utterly destroyed all the souls who were in it that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.
translation: Bapokele uyu musumba pali ubu bwine bushiku, baipaya ku lupanga bonse abaleikalamo. Yoshua apeele bonse kukonaulwa pamo ngefyo acitile ku musumba wa Lakishi.

english: Joshua went up from Eglon, and all Israel with him, to Hebron; and they fought against it.
translation: Yoshua nakabili pamo na bena Israeli bonse bafuma ku Egiloni baya ku Hebuloni no kuya lwisha uyu musumba.

english: They took it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, with its king and all its cities, and all the souls who were in it. He left no one remaining, according to all that he had done to Eglon; but he utterly destroyed it, and all the souls who were in it.
translation: Awe nao wine baliupokele no kwipaya abantu bonse ku lupanga, pamo pene ne mfumu yabo, na baleikala mu mishi ya mupepi bonse balifwile. Tamwali uwashelemo nangu umo. Califye kwati ni filya fine cacitike ku Egiloni, umusumba onsefye walyonawilwe pamo pene na baleikalamo bonse.

english: Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to Debir, and fought against it.
translation: Yoshua nakabili pamo na bena Israeli bonse balungama no kuya lwisha umusumba wa Debi.

english: He took it, with its king and all its cities. They struck them with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroyed all the souls who were in it. He left no one remaining. As he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir, and to its king; as he had done also to Libnah, and to its king.
translation: Bapoka uyu musumba pamo ne mfumu yauko ne mishi yauko, no kwipaya bonse abantu abalimo ku lupanga. Tamwali uwashelemo nangu umo. Bacitile kuli uyu musumba wa Debi ne mfumu yauko, pamo ngefyo bacitile ku musumba wa Libina ne mfumu yauko elyo na ku musumba wa Hebuloni.

english: “Come up to me and help me. Let’s strike Gibeon; for they have made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel.”
translation: Abebele ati, “Mwe, ala iseni kuno mungafweko ukulwisha Gibeoni. Pantu baliya panga umutende na Yoshua pamo na bena Israeli.”

english: So Joshua struck all the land, the hill country, the South, the lowland, the slopes, and all their kings. He left no one remaining, but he utterly destroyed all that breathed, as the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded.
translation: Kanshi efyo Yoshua acimfishe icalo conse, ukulundako ne calo cabelele ku mpili, ku matololo ya Negebu, ku masamba ya tupili, na ku calo cabela mu mutentemuko wa lupili, ukubikapofye ne mfumu shabo shonse. Tamwali uwashelemo nangu umo, lelo aonawile umuntu onsefye uupeema. Bonse balyonawilwe pamo ngefyo Yawe, Lesa wa bena Israeli, akonkomeshe.

english: Joshua struck them from Kadesh Barnea even to Gaza, and all the country of Goshen, even to Gibeon.
translation: Yoshua abacimfishe ukufuma ku Kadeshi Banea ukufikafye na ku Gasa. Kabili ukufuma ku calo conse ica Gosheni ukufikafye na ku Gibeoni.

english: Joshua took all these kings and their land at one time because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
translation: Yoshua acimfishe shonse imfumu no kupoka ifyalo fyashiko pa nshita imo ine. Pantu Yawe, Lesa wa bena Israeli, ewalwilileko abena Israeli.

english: Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp to Gilgal.
translation: Elyo Yoshua na bena Israeli bonse babwelela na ku nkambi ya ku Giligali.

english: Therefore the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon, gathered themselves together and went up, they and all their armies, and encamped against Gibeon, and made war against it.
translation: Awe imfumu shisano isha bena Amoli, pamo pene ne mfumu sha mu Yerusalemu, Hebuloni, Yamuti, Lakishi elyo na Egiloni basankanya ifita fyabulwi. Baimina pamo bonse ne fita fyabulwi fyabo no kuya shinguluka umusumba wa bena Gibeoni no kubalwisha.

english: The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, “Don’t abandon your servants! Come up to us quickly and save us! Help us; for all the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the hill country have gathered together against us.”
translation: Awe abena Gibeoni batumine amashiwi kuli Yoshua kuntu ali ku nkambi ya ku Giligali abati, “Mukwai, mwitulekelesha ifwe fwe babomfi benu! Isenifye bwangu mutwafwilisheko nokutupususha pantu imfumu shonse isha bena Amoli ishaikala ku calo ca mpili bonse bali pamo ne fita fyabulwi nabatwimina!”

english: So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and the whole army with him, including all the mighty men of valor.
translation: Awe Yoshua epakwima ku Giligali pamo pene ne fita fyabulwi, alundapo ne fita ifyacenjela nganshi kukulwa.

english: The LORD said to Joshua, “Don’t fear them, for I have delivered them into your hands. Not a man of them will stand before you.”
translation: Elyo Yawe aebele Yoshua ati, “Tecakwesha ukubatiina. Ine, nimbapeela mu maboko yobe. Takuli nelyo umo uuleya kwansha.”

english: Joshua therefore came to them suddenly. He marched from Gilgal all night.
translation: Panuma yakwenda ubushiku bonse ukufuma ku Giligali, Yoshua alibapumikishe.

english: When Jabin king of Hazor heard of it, he sent to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph,
translation: Nomba ilyo Yabini imfumu ya musumba wa Hasoli aumfwile ifyacitike, atumine inkombe kuli Yobabu imfumu ya ku Madoni, ku mfumu ya ku Shimuroni, elyo na ku mfumu ya ku Akishafu.

english: Joshua turned back at that time, and took Hazor, and struck its king with the sword; for Hazor used to be the head of all those kingdoms.
translation: Pa nshita ilya ine, Yoshua abwelulwike no kupoka Hasoli no kwipaya imfumu yauko ku lupanga. Pantu uyu Hasoli ewali musumba uukalamba untu yonse imisumba yashintilemo.

english: They struck all the souls who were in it with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them. There was no one left who breathed. He burned Hazor with fire.
translation: Onsefye umuntu uwali muli uyu musumba, balimwipeye ku lupanga. Apeela bonsefye kukonaulwa , tamwali uwashelemo uwamweo nangu umo. Kabili aoca no musumba wa Hasoli wine.

english: Joshua captured all the cities of those kings, with their kings, and he struck them with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroyed them, as Moses the servant of the LORD commanded.
translation: Yoshua acimfya no kupoka yonse imisumba ne mfumu yashiko, kabili aipaya bonse ku lupanga. Aonaulafye bonse ukulingana nefyo Mose umubomfi wakwa Yawe akonkomeshe.

english: But as for the cities that stood on their mounds, Israel burned none of them, except Hazor only. Joshua burned that.
translation: Nangu cali ifi, abena Israeli tabaocele umusumba nelyo umo uo bakuulile pa milundu ye loba lyabo, kanofye umusumba wa Hasoli, eo Yoshua aocele.

english: The children of Israel took all the plunder of these cities, with the livestock, as plunder for themselves; but every man they struck with the edge of the sword, until they had destroyed them. They didn’t leave any who breathed.
translation: Abena Israeli balisendele abene fyonse ifyo batapile, pamo ne fitekwa fya muli iyi misumba, lelo abantu bonsefye bena balibepeye ku lupanga mpaka bonse bapwililika. Tapali nangu umo uwashelepo uwamweo.

english: As the LORD commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua. Joshua did so. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD commanded Moses.
translation: Pamo ngefyo Yawe akonkomeshe umubomfi wakwe Mose, efyo Mose nao akonkomeshe Yoshua kabili nao efyo acitile. Tashilepo nangu kamo akabula ukubombwa pali fyonse ifyo Yawe akonkomeshe Mose.

english: So Joshua captured all that land, the hill country, all the South, all the land of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel, and the lowland of the same,
translation: Kanshi Yoshua epakupokafye icalo conse cilya. Icalo ca mpili, amatololo yonse aya Negebu, impangafye yonse iya calo ca Gosheni, icalo cabela pesamba, icalo ca Araba, icalo ca mpili sha bena Israeli ne mpanga ya mwishika.

english: from Mount Halak, that goes up to Seir, even to Baal Gad in the valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. He took all their kings, struck them, and put them to death.
translation: Kabili alipokele ne calo conse ukufuma ku lupili lwa Halaki, ulwanina ukulola ku sili, na ku Bali Gadi mwishika lya Lebanoni mwisamba lya lupili lwa Hemoni. Yoshua aikete imfumu shonse ashikomaula no kushipaya.

english: Joshua made war a long time with all those kings.
translation: Yoshua alwishishe ishi mfumu pa nshita iyitali.

english: There was not a city that made peace with the children of Israel, except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon. They took all in battle.
translation: Takwali umusumba nelyo umo uwacitile icipangano ca cibote na bena Israeli, kanofye abena Hifi abaleikala mu Gibeoni. Imisumba imbi yonse baipokele mu bulwi.

english: and to the kings who were on the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor on the west,
translation: Kabili atumine inkombe ku mfumu sha ku kapinda ka ku kuso, abali mu fyalo fya mpili, ku sha mu calo ca Araba ku kapinda ka ku kulyo ka Kinereti , ku sha mu calo ca mwishika, kabili na ku sha mu lulamba lwa Nafoti Dori ku masamba.

english: For it was of the LORD to harden their hearts, to come against Israel in battle, that he might utterly destroy them, that they might have no favor, but that he might destroy them, as the LORD commanded Moses.
translation: Pantu ni Yawe umwine ewabakoseshe imitima pakulwisha abena Israeli pakuti bonaulwe no kwipaiwa, no kuloba balobelele ukwabula uluse pamo ngefyo Yawe akonkomeshe Mose.

english: Joshua came at that time, and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah, and from all the hill country of Israel. Joshua utterly destroyed them with their cities.
translation: Kabili mu nshita ilya ine, Yoshua aile no kulofya abena Anakimu abaleikala mu calo ca mpili na ba mu Hebuloni, na ba mu Debi na mu Anabu, na bonse aba mu calo ca mpili conse ica bena Yuda, kabili no kufuma ku calo conse ica mpili sha bena Israeli. Yoshua apeele bonsefye kukonaulwa abantu pamo pene ne misumba yabo yonse.

english: There were none of the Anakim left in the land of the children of Israel. Only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod, did some remain.
translation: Takwali umwina Anakimu uwasheleko mu calo ca bena Israeli, kanofye mu Gasa na mu Gati elyo na mu Ashidodi emwashelefye bamo bamo.

english: So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the LORD spoke to Moses; and Joshua gave it for an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. Then the land had rest from war.
translation: Kanshi Yoshua epakupoka icalo conse, ukulingana nefyo Yawe aebele Mose ukucita. Elyo acipeela ku bena Israeli ukuba icuma cabo umwabela impuka shabo cila luko. Awe ne calo conse catuushishe ku bulwi, caikalafye tondolo.

english: to the Canaanite on the east and on the west, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite in the hill country, and the Hivite under Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
translation: Elyo kabili atumine inkombe ku bena Kenani ba ku kabanga na ba ku masamba, ku bena Amoli, ku bena Hiti, ku bena Perisi elyo na ku bena Yebusi aba mu calo ca ku mpili, kabili na ku bena Hifi, mwisamba lya Hemoni mu calo ca Misipa.

english: They went out, they and all their armies with them, many people, even as the sand that is on the seashore in multitude, with very many horses and chariots.
translation: Imfumu shonse shaishile ne mpuka ya fita fyashiko, kabili na bakabalwe impendwa iyikulu nganshi, pamo na maceleta. Kabili ubwingi bwa fita fya nkondo bwali kwati musensenga wa ku lulamba lwa bemba.

english: All these kings met together; and they came and encamped together at the waters of Merom, to fight with Israel.
translation: Shonse ishi mfumu shasankenye pamo ifita fyabo no kucita inkambi imo pa menshi ya Meromu pakuti balwishe bwino abena Israeli.

english: The LORD said to Joshua, “Don’t be afraid because of them; for tomorrow at this time, I will deliver them up all slain before Israel. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
translation: Elyo Yawe aeba Yoshua ati, “Tecakwesha ukubatiina, pantu mailo pa nshita nga ino ine ndi nokupeela bonse abalwani bobe mu minwe ya bena Israeli, ninshi balifye ifitumbi. Bakabalwe babo ukabalemanike no koca amaceleta yabo.”

english: So Joshua came suddenly, with all the warriors, against them by the waters of Merom, and attacked them.
translation: Awe Yoshua ne fita fyonse bafika uko bali nokubapumikisha mu bulwi pa menshi ya Meromu.

english: The LORD delivered them into the hand of Israel, and they struck them, and chased them to great Sidon, and to Misrephoth Maim, and to the valley of Mizpah eastward. They struck them until they left them no one remaining.
translation: Na Yawe nao abapeela mu maboko ya bena Israeli. Nabo bacimfya no kubabutusha bonse ku nshila yaya ku Sidoni Mukulu, na ku Misirefoti Maimu elyo na kwishika lya Misipa ku kabanga, mpakafye babapwisha. Takwali uwashelepo nangu umo.

english: Joshua did to them as the LORD told him. He hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
translation: Na Yoshua acitile ngefyo Yawe amwebele. Alemanika bakabalwe babo, elyo aoca na maceleta yabo yonse.

english: Now these are the kings of the land, whom the children of Israel struck, and possessed their land beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:
translation: Kanshi ishi e mfumu sha mu calo isho abena Israeli bacimfishe, kabili isho icalo cabo bapokele icabela kwishilya lya Yordani, ukufumafye ku mukonko wa Alinoni no kufika ku lupili lwa Hemoni, ukulundako ne ncende yonse iyabela lwa ku kabanga ka Araba.

english: the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
translation: Imfumu ya mu Yerusalemu imo,

english: the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
translation: Imfumu ya mu Yamuti imo,

english: the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
translation: Amaf 3:12

english: the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
translation: Imfumu ya ku Debi imo,

english: the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
translation: Imfumu ya ku Homa imo,

english: the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
translation: Imfumu ya ku Libina imo,

english: the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
translation: Imfumu ya ku Makeda imo,

english: the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
translation: Imfumu ya ku Tapua imo,

english: the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lassharon, one;
translation: Imfumu ya ku Afeki imo,

english: the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
translation: Imfumu ya ku Madoni imo,

english: Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and ruled from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the middle of the valley, and half Gilead, even to the river Jabbok, the border of the children of Ammon;
translation: Sihoni imfumu ya bena Amoli, uwaleteeka mu Heshiboni, ateekele ukufuma ku lulamba lwa mumana wa Aroeli ukufika ku mukonko wa Alinoni, kabili ukufuma pakati nankati ka mukonko ukufikafye na ku mumana wa Yaboku, uwapakana na bena Amoni. Kabili alundilepo ukufika pakati nankati ka calo ca Gileadi.

english: the king of Shimron Meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
translation: Imfumu ya ku Shimuroni Meroni imo,

english: the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
translation: Imfumu ya ku Tanaki imo,

english: the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
translation: Imfumu ya ku Kadeshi imo,

english: the king of Dor in the height of Dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;
translation: Imfumu ya ku Dori mu Nafoti Dori imo,

english: the king of Tirzah, one: all the kings thirty-one.
translation: Imfumu ya ku Tirisa imo.

english: and the Arabah to the sea of Chinneroth, eastward, and to the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, eastward, the way to Beth Jeshimoth; and on the south, under the slopes of Pisgah:
translation: Kabili ateekele no lubali lwa ku kabanga ka Araba ukufika kuli bemba wa Kinereti lwa ku kabanga elyo no kufika kuli bemba wa Araba wine, Bemba Wamucele no kushinta na ku Beti Yeshimoti no kulungamafye ku kapinda ka ku kulyo, mwisamba lya mutentemuko wa Pisiga.

english: and the border of Og king of Bashan, of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
